issues.title: DH: RenderTargets.resizeIfNeeded re-attaches the main depth texture to the DH terrain framebuffer, and reconnectDHTextures never restores DH's depth
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Distant Horizons and a shaderpack, DH's LOD depth ends up in Minecraft's main depth buffer whenever the main render target's depth texture changes but DH's depth texture does not. From then on near terrain fails the depth test wherever LODs exist, so distant LOD terrain is drawn over near walls (see screenshots). It stays broken until DH recreates its own depth texture, e.g. on a window resize. Without a shaderpack the bug does not occur.

**Cause** (code from branch `26.3` @ 671a5c8)

1. `DHCompatInternal` creates `dhTerrainFramebuffer` (and the water and generic framebuffers) through `pipeline.createDHFramebuffer` → `RenderTargets.createColorFramebuffer`, so they are in `RenderTargets.ownedFramebuffers` (RenderTargets.java:298, :351). It then attaches DH's depth texture with `addDepthAttachmentBypass`.
2. When `iris$getDepthBufferVersion()` of the main target changes, `RenderTargets.resizeIfNeeded` (RenderTargets.java:199) calls `addDepthAttachment(newDepthTexture)` on every owned framebuffer that has a depth attachment. That includes the DH framebuffers, so they now point at Minecraft's depth texture.
3. `DHCompatInternal.reconnectDHTextures` (DHCompatInternal.java:161) only re-attaches DH's depth when `storedDepthTex != depthTex` (line 166), i.e. only when DH's texture ID changes. It hasn't changed, so the attachment from step 2 is never undone.

A normal window resize hides this, because DH recreates its depth texture (new ID) in the same frame. It shows up when the main target's depth changes without a DH resize. I hit it with a portal mod (an unofficial 26.3 port of Immersive Portals) that renders each portal view into its own render target by redirecting `GameRenderer.mainRenderTarget()`, which changes the depth version twice per frame. I haven't checked whether anything in plain Iris + DH triggers it.

**Reproduction:** Iris + Sodium + DH + Complementary Reimagined + an Immersive Portals build for 26.3, real terrain with DH LODs loaded, stand in a closed stone room and have a portal exist in the scene.

**Fix I verified** (as a mixin in the portal mod): at the start of `reconnectDHTextures`, set `storedDepthTex = -1`, so DH's depth is re-attached before every DH pass. With that, automated before/after screenshots of the same scene (Complementary + DH, portals present) are correct again and distant LODs still render. Possible upstream fixes:

- skip the DH framebuffers in the re-attach loop of `resizeIfNeeded` (or keep them out of `ownedFramebuffers`), or
- have `DHCompatInternal` also re-attach when the main depth version changed; it already tracks it in `cachedVersion` in the same method.

### Screenshots

Same scene (closed stone room, glowstone ceiling, a portal on the far wall), before and after the workaround.

Before – LOD terrain drawn over the room walls; the portal on the far wall is hidden:

![before, looking at the portal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/w-Teilchen/dae94144957610c63e886ddba63d5da2/raw/d84b296395a089a11f9ba261932d0f57dea0d5c8/before_look_at_portal.png)

After – walls intact, portal visible:

![after, looking at the portal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/w-Teilchen/dae94144957610c63e886ddba63d5da2/raw/151fbabb0ff878596a34ecc3c806638de51ea0cd/after_look_at_portal.png)

Side wall (no portal in view, but portals exist elsewhere in the room), before and after:

![before, side wall](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/w-Teilchen/dae94144957610c63e886ddba63d5da2/raw/f45cff84e462c906a98c2f79daefd104f6310330/before_side_wall.png)
![after, side wall](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/w-Teilchen/dae94144957610c63e886ddba63d5da2/raw/08a8669daa417f237c1bb430161d056f0c681e2a/after_side_wall.png)

### Minecraft Version

26.3 (Fabric)

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.11.7+mc26.3.jar (with sodium-fabric-0.9.2+mc26.3, DistantHorizons-3.3.4-26.3, ComplementaryReimagined_r5.9.3)

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-38)

### What is your GPU?

AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Mesa 26.0.8, radeonsi)

### Additional context

Possibly related, but a different symptom: #3146 (DH transparent water over the player with Complementary).

issues.title: VRAM is not released when the shader pipeline is rebuilt (dimension change)
issues.body:
### What happened?

## Summary

Every time Iris rebuilds the shader pipeline (in my case on every Overworld ↔ Nether dimension change), the game's dedicated GPU memory grows and is never released until the game is restarted. With Complementary Reimagined on its default "Complementary" profile, after 4–5 Nether round trips the 16 GB card fills up. The driver then starts spilling into shared (system) memory, and FPS drops from ~80 to ~20. Disabling shaders (K) or reloading (F3+T) does not recover the memory. Only restarting the game does.

With shaders **disabled**, the same round trips do **not** grow VRAM, so this seems specific to the shader pipeline rather than Sodium or other mods.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 26.3 |
| Loader | Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Fabric API 0.164.0+26.3 |
| Iris | 1.11.7+mc26.3 |
| Sodium | 0.9.2+mc26.3 |
| Shader pack | Complementary Reimagined r5.9.3 |
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (16 GB), driver 32.0.31041.1004, OpenGL `3.3.0 Core Profile Context 26.8.1.260810` |
| Other GPU | AMD Radeon integrated graphics (Ryzen iGPU), not used by the game |
| CPU / RAM | Ryzen 7 7800X3D / 32 GB |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 |
| Java | Eclipse Adoptium 25.0.4.1, `-Xmx12G -XX:+UseZGC` |
| Resolution | 2560×1440 fullscreen |
| Notes | Sodium applies the `AMD_GAME_OPTIMIZATION_BROKEN` workaround. RivaTuner (RTSS) is injected. Distant Horizons 3.3.3 is installed with the Nether and End excluded. |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Load a world with Complementary Reimagined enabled.
2. Travel Overworld → Nether → Overworld repeatedly (portal or `/execute in minecraft:the_nether run tp ...`).
3. Watch the game's per-process GPU memory: Task Manager → Details → "Dedicated GPU memory" column, or the perf counter `\GPU Process Memory(pid_<PID>_*)\Dedicated Usage`.

**Expected:** after the first visit to each dimension, VRAM stays roughly flat across rebuilds.
**Actual:** VRAM grows with every pipeline rebuild (`Destroying pipeline ...` / `Creating pipeline for dimension ...` in the log) and never comes back down.

## Measurements

I sampled `\GPU Process Memory(pid_*)\Dedicated Usage` + `Shared Usage` every ~3 s and matched the samples with the log. Each test is a fresh game start with 4 round trips, render distance 16. The CSVs are attached.

### Test A: shaders ON (Complementary, `COLORED_LIGHTING=128`)

| Time | Event | VRAM (dedicated + shared) |
|---|---|---|
| 23:36:34 | Overworld loaded | 3.02 GB |
| 23:37:00 | → Nether (rebuild 1) | 4.27 GB (first-visit cost) |
| 23:37:23 | → Overworld (2) | 4.70 GB |
| 23:37:33 | → Nether (3) | 5.54 GB |
| 23:37:41 | → Overworld (4) | 6.13 GB |
| 23:37:48 | → Nether (5) | 6.77 GB |
| 23:37:56 | → Overworld (6) | 7.12 GB |
| 23:38:07 | → Nether (7) | 7.49 GB |
| 23:38:17 | → Overworld (8) | 8.36 GB |
| 23:38–23:56 | idle 18 min in the Overworld | **8.26 GB (never released)** |

After the first-visit cost, that is **≈ 0.57 GB retained per rebuild**.

### Test B: shaders OFF (same world and route)

| Time | Event | VRAM (dedicated + shared) |
|---|---|---|
| 00:22:50 | Overworld loaded | 1.92 GB |
| 00:22:55 | → Nether | 2.86 GB (first-visit cost) |
| 00:23:01 | → Overworld | 2.97 GB |
| 00:23:15 | → Nether | 3.06 GB |
| 00:23:21 | → Overworld | 2.85 GB |
| 00:23:27 | → Nether | 3.10 GB |
| 00:23:33 | → Overworld | 3.00 GB |
| 00:23:48 | idle | **2.99 GB (flat)** |

After the first-visit cost, that is **≈ 0 GB per rebuild**.

### Earlier session: Complementary profile defaults (`COLORED_LIGHTING=512`)

This is the setup where I first hit the FPS drop. I measured it after the fact: after 11 shader pipeline creations (startup, 8 from dimension changes, 2 reloads), then **disabling shaders**, the game still held **11.34 GB dedicated + 2.67 GB shared**, and FPS was ~20 instead of ~80.

At 512 the pack's custom images alone are about 1.24 GB per pipeline:
- `voxel_img` 512×256×512 R16UI ≈ 134 MB
- `floodfill_img` + `floodfill_img_copy` 512×256×512 RGBA16F ≈ 537 MB each
- `wsr_img` 512×64×512 R16UI ≈ 34 MB

That size matches the much faster growth seen in that session. Lowering the setting to 128 shrank the per-rebuild loss but did not remove it (Test A), so screen-sized render targets and/or shadow targets seem to be retained as well.

## What I checked

Disassembling `IrisRenderingPipeline.destroy()` in 1.11.7 (`javap -c`) shows that it does call:
- `renderTargets.destroy()`
- `shadowRenderTargets.destroy()`
- `customImages.forEach(GlResource::destroy)`, which goes to `GlImage.destroyInternal()` and then `GlStateManager._deleteTexture(id)`

So the deletes appear to be issued from the Java side, but the memory is not returned according to Windows' per-process GPU counters. Possible causes (I have not verified which):
- A deleted texture is still referenced somewhere (for example, still attached to a framebuffer or bound to an image unit), so GL never frees it.
- The AMD OpenGL driver does not release these allocations.

## Not tested yet

- [ ] Without Distant Horizons. It is installed, but its `Renderer already started` warning shows up identically in the shaders-off test, where VRAM stays flat.
- [ ] Another GPU vendor or driver version

## Already tested

- [x] Minimal mod set (Iris + Sodium + Fabric API only)

## Attachments

- `vram-log.csv` (Test A, shaders on)
- `vram-log-shaders-off.csv` (Test B, shaders off)
- Game log for Test A: <!-- mclo.gs link to 2026-10-19-7.log -->
- Game log for Test B: <!-- mclo.gs link to latest.log -->
- Game log for the `COLORED_LIGHTING=512` session: <!-- mclo.gs link, optional -->

issues.title: Large stretched black/colored polygons with a TTF resource-pack font and shaders enabled (26.3, Iris 1.11.7)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Steps to reproduce in our affected environment:
1. Launch Minecraft 26.3 with Iris 1.11.7 and Sodium 0.9.2. My reproduction uses Lunar Client; a clean Fabric-only reproduction has not yet been verified by me.
2. Enable Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1 and the affected resource pack, which adds NeoDunggeunmo Pro (ndp.ttf) to minecraft:default.
3. Join the multiplayer server and enter the affected area. Large black/colored surfaces obscure the world. We have not yet isolated the exact in-world text object or draw call that triggers it.
4. Keep the same scene, shader, and other resource-pack assets, but remove only the ndp.ttf provider from minecraft:default and restore vanilla font fallbacks. The large surfaces disappear.

Controlled comparisons, performed with shaders kept enabled:
- Original resource pack with its default TTF provider: artifact occurs.
- Remove only the default TTF provider, retaining the original HUD, effect bitmap glyphs, shaders, models, and textures: artifact disappears.
- Remove the seven special-effect bitmap providers while retaining the default TTF provider: artifact still occurs.
- Use vanilla resources without the custom pack: artifact disappears.

The relevant TTF settings are file=ndp.ttf, size=8, oversample=4, shift=[0,-1]. Standard ASCII letters/digits and selected punctuation are excluded from this TTF provider using skip.

### Screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b0273ac-b78e-4e4b-805c-5877f6f49cae

### Log output

I will attach it if needed.

### Minecraft Version

26.3

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.11.7+mc26.3.jar

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro 64-bit, build 26200

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080, NVIDIA driver 610.88 (OpenGL)

### Additional context

Possibly related to https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/3251. Our observed symptom includes huge stretched polygons, rather than only invisible sign/text_display text. We have isolated the default TTF provider as a trigger in this environment, but have not established that the underlying defect is identical to #3251.

Another player independently reported the issue on Fabric with Iris 1.11.7, using both Solas V3.8 and Complementary Unbound r5.9.3. Those shader-pack results are that player's report; my direct reproduction and controlled comparisons used Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1.

I do not recall this happening on Minecraft 26.1.2, but have not performed a controlled comparison with the old client, so I cannot confirm the first affected version.

Replacing the TTF with bitmap glyphs hides the artifact, but changes character spacing and coverage. We would like to retain the TTF and its original metrics rather than use that as a permanent workaround.

issues.title: [Bug] Severe GPU Throttle (25 FPS) and Forced Fullscreen Lock on macOS M2 - Minecraft 26.3
issues.body: ### What happened? After updating to Minecraft 26.3 (Wilderness Bound) on an M2 MacBook Pro via the Modrinth App, activating any shader pack (specifically Complementary Unbound) completely throttles performance down to a locked 25–50 FPS. Prior to the 26.3 update, the exact same system stably achieved 90+ FPS with shaders and 600+ FPS on pure vanilla. Additionally, the client completely ignores window parameters. The game forces an exclusive desktop capture on startup, trapping the system in fullscreen mode. Changing fullscreen:false and exclusiveFullscreen:false inside options.txt or toggling settings inside the Modrinth launcher does absolutely nothing; the SDL3 framework overrides the instructions on boot. This performance drop and window lock appear to heavily target M2 Apple Silicon architectures, as peer players on Windows and newer Mac hardware profiles are achieving native frame rates on the exact same Realm server. Steps to Reproduce:     1    Launch Minecraft 26.3 using Fabric/Modrinth on an M2 Mac.     2    Observe the game forcing exclusive fullscreen mode, ignoring launcher and config specifications.     3    Load into a multiplayer Realm or singleplayer world.     4    Enable Iris Shaders with Complementary Unbound.     5    Monitor FPS counter; performance immediately caps and locks between 25–50 FPS. System Information:     •    OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)     •    Hardware: M2 MacBook Pro     •    Game Version: Minecraft 26.3 (Wilderness Bound)     •    Window/Graphics Framework: SDL3 / Native OpenGL & Vulkan Layer     •    Mod Loader: Fabric (Modrinth Client)     •    Active Performance Mods: Iris Shaders, Sodium (26.3 compliant builds) ### Screenshots _No response_ ### Log output ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 26.3 ### Iris Version v1.11.7+mc26.3 ### Operating System MacOs (Apple Silicon) ### What is your GPU? Apple M2 Integrated GPU (Unified Memory) ### Additional context This bottleneck points directly to a severe optimization or threading conflict between 26.3's newly integrated SDL3 framework, the new Order-Independent Transparency (OIT) pipeline, and M2 core allocation. It seems Iris is forcing the game to render at raw Retina display pixel density while simultaneously dropping GPU utilization threads, creating a permanent hardware ceiling that settings modifications cannot break.

issues.title: Add Support for Minecraft's Native Vulkan Graphics Backend and External Shader Packs

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
I would like to request support for Minecraft Java Edition's built-in Vulkan graphics API backend in Iris Shaders.
To be clear, I am not requesting support for VulkanMod or any third-party Vulkan renderer. I am referring specifically to Minecraft's own graphics backend, selected using the --graphicsBackend vulkan launch argument or the corresponding in-game graphics setting where available.
Currently, Iris relies on OpenGL-specific rendering functionality. When Minecraft uses its native Vulkan backend, Iris may attempt to call OpenGL functions without an active OpenGL context. This prevents the two systems from working together correctly.
My main goal is to use Iris with Minecraft's native Vulkan renderer while retaining the ability to load external shader packs, including established packs such as Complementary Reimagined, Complementary Unbound, BSL, and other compatible Iris shader packs.
Why this matters
Minecraft's graphics backend and its shader-pack loader serve different purposes. The graphics backend handles rendering, while Iris provides the shader-pack loading and rendering infrastructure that makes a large ecosystem of visual enhancements possible.
Players who choose Vulkan should not necessarily have to give up that shader-pack ecosystem.
A Vulkan-compatible shader solution may provide its own shaders, but that does not automatically allow it to load existing Iris shader packs. Requiring every shader author to port their work separately creates fragmentation and additional maintenance.
I would like to retain the ability to select different external shader packs rather than being restricted to built-in shaders or a small collection of packs designed for another rendering system.
What should be implemented
1. Native Vulkan backend compatibility
Investigate how Iris can operate when Minecraft selects its built-in Vulkan graphics backend. Iris should avoid making OpenGL calls that require an OpenGL context when that context does not exist.
2. A backend-independent rendering architecture
Where technically feasible, separate shader-pack processing and higher-level rendering logic from OpenGL-specific operations. Provide backend-specific implementations for the necessary rendering operations, resource management, shader compilation, pipeline state, and synchronization.
I understand that Vulkan and OpenGL use different rendering models. This would require proper engineering work rather than simply changing a setting or redirecting a few function calls.
3. External shader-pack loading
Preserve the existing shader-pack selection interface and loading workflow where possible. Users should be able to install shader packs in the usual shader-pack directory, select them in-game, and configure their available options.
4. Compatibility with existing shader packs
Investigate how much of the existing Iris shader-pack format can be supported through the Vulkan backend. Prioritize commonly used features such as:
Dynamic shadows and shadow maps
Realistic water and reflections
Volumetric lighting and sun rays
Ambient occlusion and improved indirect lighting
Atmospheric fog and sky effects
Automatic exposure and tone mapping
Post-processing and other common shader effects
Not every feature necessarily has a direct Vulkan equivalent, so unsupported features should be documented rather than silently producing incorrect results.
5. Performance and stability
Test frame-time consistency, memory use, visual correctness, and stability on different supported hardware and drivers. Vulkan should not be advertised as automatically faster than OpenGL, since performance depends on the device, drivers, renderer, and shader pack.
6. Graceful handling of unsupported configurations
Until full support is implemented, Iris should detect when Minecraft is using an unsupported backend and show a clear, actionable compatibility message instead of crashing through an OpenGL call made without a valid context.
A possible development approach
I suggest starting with a technical feasibility study and a minimal Vulkan-compatible Iris prototype.
The development team could identify OpenGL-dependent components, define the rendering operations that need backend-specific implementations, and establish a small set of supported shader features. Compatibility could then be expanded incrementally, with testing against representative existing shader packs.
If maintaining full compatibility with every existing shader pack is not feasible, an experimental implementation with a documented subset of supported packs and features would still be valuable.
Collaboration with the developers responsible for Minecraft's native Vulkan implementation may also help clarify the available rendering hooks and architectural constraints.
Expected result
The ideal outcome would allow a player to:
Select Minecraft's built-in Vulkan graphics backend.
Launch a compatible version of Iris.
Install external shader packs in the normal shader-pack directory.
Select and configure those packs in-game.
Play with the supported shader effects without switching the game back to OpenGL.
This request is specifically about Minecraft's native Vulkan graphics API backend, not VulkanMod.
I understand that this is a substantial feature request and may require architectural changes. I am asking the Iris developers to investigate the possibility and consider Vulkan support as a longer-term development goal.
Thank you for your work on Iris and for considering this request.

issues.title: Water rendering changes abruptly above Y97 with Distant Horizons and Iris on Minecraft 26.3
issues.body: ### What happened? Description Water develops a sharp, dark patch with a clearly visible boundary when my character moves above approximately Y97. It changes suddenly between Y97 and Y98 and remains glitched above that height. Disabling Distant Horizons rendering fixes the issue. It happens with multiple shader packs and also reproduces in a new, clean instance. Versions Minecraft: 26.3 Distant Horizons: 3.3.4 Iris: 1.11.7+mc26.3 Shader shown in the screenshots: Complementary Reimagined 5.9.3 The Y97–98 threshold is consistently reproducible at this location. I have not confirmed whether the same threshold applies elsewhere. **Tests already performed** Disabled DH rendering: fixes the issue. Tested multiple shader packs: issue persists. Tested in a new, clean instance: issue persists. Pressed F1 to hide the interface and block selection outline: no improvement. Set Block Reflection Quality to Low: no improvement. Disabled water reflections: no improvement. Tried changing DH transparency: the option is greyed out, so I could not test it. ### Screenshots ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version minecraft 26.3 ### Iris Version Iris: 1.11.7+mc26.3 ### Operating System windows 11 ### What is your GPU? RTX 3060 TI ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: [26.3] Z Fighting
issues.body: ### What happened? There is a ton of Z fighting going on when using Distant Horizons + Shaders. It can mostly be seen with any kind of glass object(panes, blocks etc.), poppies and possibly other flowers, and amethyst clusters. At first, I thought this was a DH bug, so I reported it there, but the creator told me to report it to Iris instead. https://gitlab.com/distant-horizons-team/distant-horizons/-/work_items/1333 ### Screenshots ### Log output There is no relevant log messages, except for when looking at the amethyst cluster, although I am not even sure if it's related to the issue: ``` [02:26:51] [Render thread/ERROR]: Deleting stream buffers: Invalid operation. [02:26:51] [Render thread/ERROR]: Deleting stream buffers: Invalid operation. [02:26:51] [Render thread/ERROR]: Deleting stream buffers: Invalid operation. [02:26:51] [Render thread/ERROR]: Deleting stream buffers: Invalid operation. [02:26:51] [Render thread/ERROR]: Deleting stream buffers: Invalid operation. ``` ### Minecraft Version 26.3 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.11.7+mc26.3 ### Operating System Arch + Hyprland ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 3060 ### Additional context I have other mods installed too, but another person reported the same issue on the Distant Horizons tracker, so it's unlikely to be caused by a mod conflict or something. In case you suspect it matters, here's the modpack: https://github.com/nnra6864/NnSurvival

issues.title: Mod block entity (Create water wheel) not rendered > 64 blocks away with shaders enabled
issues.body: ### What happened? I noticed the [Create mod](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/328085) Large Water Wheel not rendering with any shader enabled at a distance bigger than 64 blocks. But they do render in vanilla! Vanilla: Signs disappear at 64, Water Wheels stay Shaders: Signs disappear at 64, Water Wheels disappear at 64 The same is likely true for other structures, but I already tested so much and skip further testing for now. These are all shaders I tried: - Bliss Shaders - BSL Shaders - Complementary Shaders - Reimagined - Complementary Shaders - Unbound - MakeUp - Ultra Fast | Shaders - Mellow - Photon Shader - Sildur's Vibrant shaders - Solas Shader This is why I assume this is a Iris issue. The water wheel is an important landmark for me that should be visible from a distance. That's why I care. ### Screenshots F3: ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.1 ### Iris Version 1.8.14-beta.1+mc1.21.1 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB ### Additional context Mods: - [Create](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/328085) [6\.0\.10] - [Iris](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/455508) [1\.8\.14\-beta\.1\+mc1\.21\.1] - [Sodium](https://www.curseforge.com/projects/394468) [0\.8\.13\+mc1\.21\.1] (Minimal test setup)

issues.title: DH water renders as flat mirror with any shader on MC 26.3 (fine with shaders off or DH off)
issues.body: ### What happened? ## What happened? With Distant Horizons rendering enabled and any shader active, the water looks like a flat, highly reflective mirror that hides the seabed, even close to the player. It looks normal when I look down from high up. When I disable DH rendering (Enable Rendering = off) the water looks correct, with waves and visible bottom. With shaders off and DH on, it also looks correct. issues.title: colorSpace other than sRGB freezes the world render when a first-person overlay is drawn (fire overlay / F3)
issues.body: ### What happened? ### Description With a shader pack enabled, setting Iris's **Color Space** to anything other than `sRGB` makes the **world rendering stop updating** as soon as a first-person screen overlay is drawn. The last rendered world frame stays on screen and never refreshes. Everything else keeps working normally: - **FPS is unaffected** (measured 119 fps while frozen) - the **F3 readout keeps updating live** - the **burning overlay keeps animating** - **player input and game logic work normally** (you can still move, open menus, etc.) Only the *world image* is stale. There is no stutter, no frame drop and no exception in the log. Setting Color Space back to `sRGB` completely avoids the issue. The two triggers found so far are: 1. **the player being on fire** (first-person fire screen overlay), and 2. **opening the F3 debug screen**. Both are first-person-only overlay passes, and both are instantly reversible. ### Steps to reproduce Minimal setup: only Fabric API + Iris + Sodium in `mods/`, a shader pack with default options, and a fresh world. 1. Enable the shader pack (`Solas Shader V3.7.zip`), leaving all pack options at their defaults. 2. In `Video Settings → Shader Packs → Iris → Settings`, set **Color Space** to anything other than `sRGB` (e.g. `REC2020`). 3. Enter a single-player world, then either: - press **`F3`** to open the debug screen, **or** - set yourself on fire (`/effect give @s minecraft:fire_resistance 999 0 true` + stand in a fire block). ### Expected behaviour The world keeps rendering normally. ### Actual behaviour The world image freezes on the last rendered frame. It is **not** a stutter and **not** an fps drop: - the frame counter keeps running at a normal rate (119 fps in the attached screenshot), - the F3 overlay redraws and updates live over the frozen world image, - the burning overlay (screen-space fire) keeps animating over the frozen world image, - gameplay is fully responsive. So new frames are still being produced and presented — only the world portion of the frame never changes anymore. ### Recovery (instant, no restart needed) | Action | Result | |---|---| | Press `F5` (third person) | renders normally again | | Switch back to first person | freezes again | | Press `F3` again / extinguish the fire | renders normally again | | Set Color Space back to `sRGB` | never happens | ### What has already been ruled out - **Not shader-pack specific** — reproduced with two unrelated packs (Solas Shader V3.7 and a Photon Voxy-support build). - **Not Voxy** — reproduced with Voxy removed entirely. - **Not an Iris/Sodium version mismatch** — reproduced on both the officially matched pair (`1.10.8` + `0.8.14`) and the older pair (`1.10.7` + `0.8.12`). - **Not another mod** — reproduced in a minimal instance containing only Fabric API + Iris + Sodium (see attached `latest.log`). Disabling `voxy`, `hdr_mod`, `skinlayers3d`, `entity_texture_features`, `entity_model_features` and `sodium-extra` individually made no difference either. - **Not corrupted game files** — re-validating / re-downloading `assets`, `libraries` and natives had no effect. - **Not the GPU driver** — updating the NVIDIA driver (596.49 → 617.14) had no effect. - **Not an exception** — nothing is thrown; the attached log is 393 lines with no errors related to rendering. ### Hypothesis The extra render-target / colour-conversion step that Iris adds for non-sRGB output does not restore its state correctly when a vanilla first-person overlay pass (`ScreenEffectRenderer` fire overlay, F3 debug overlay) runs in between. `sRGB` skips that extra step entirely and is unaffected. Supporting observations: - the trigger is a **first-person-only** overlay pass, - frames are still being **presented** (FPS and overlays are live), - it is a **pure state / presentation** problem, since it recovers instantly as soon as the overlay passes stop running. ### Environment | | | |---|---| | Shader packs | Solas Shader V3.7 (default options) · also a Photon Voxy-support build | | Sodium | 0.8.12+mc1.21.11 — also reproduced on 0.8.14+mc1.21.11 | | Fabric API | 0.141.5+1.21.11 | | Second GPU | AMD Radeon(TM) 610M (hybrid-graphics laptop) | | Display | 2560x1440, fullscreen, vsync on | | LWJGL | 3.3.3-snapshot | | OpenGL | 3.3.0 NVIDIA 617.14 | | Java | 21.0.3 | ### Screenshots https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6e693e3-3cda-4083-b044-621b3e20559f https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5763c35b-fb21-452d-a10e-e804c5c6e0a3 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e849d521-00d4-45b6-9c6e-f88c01dd609f ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32875903/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.11 ### Iris Version 1.10.7+mc1.21.11 (also reproduced on 1.10.8+1.21.11) ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, 10.0.26300 (Build 26300), 64-bit ### What is your GPU? NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (driver 617.14 / Windows 32.0.16.1714) also present: AMD Radeon(TM) 610M iGPU (32.0.11036.4) ### Additional context ### Sodium startup warnings (same machine) ``` [WARN]: Found graphics adapter: AdapterInfo{vendor=NVIDIA, description='NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU', ... openglIcdVersion=32.0.16.1714} [WARN]: Found graphics adapter: AdapterInfo{vendor=AMD, description='AMD Radeon(TM) 610M', ...} [WARN]: Sodium has applied one or more workarounds to prevent crashes or other issues on your system: [NVIDIA_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS_BROKEN, AMD_GAME_OPTIMIZATION_BROKEN] [INFO]: Modifying process environment to apply workarounds for the NVIDIA graphics driver... [INFO]: Modifying OpenGL context to apply workarounds for the NVIDIA graphics driver... ``` ### Driver history | When | NVIDIA driver | |---|---| | First observed | 596.49 (Windows `32.0.15.9649`) | | After updating | 617.14 (Windows `32.0.16.1714`) | The issue reproduces on both — driver version is not the cause. ### Iris config used for the reproduction ``` enableShaders=true shaderPack=Solas Shader V3.7.zip colorSpace=REC2020 ``` ### Prior issue search Searched existing issues for `colorSpace` (7 results) and `REC2020` (1 result) — nothing describing this behaviour, so opening a new report. ### Side note (possibly unrelated) When loading Solas Shader V3.7, Iris 1.10.7 logs 51 occurrences of: ``` [Render thread/INFO]: null:855:81: error: Bad token in expression: ``` This looks like a separate shader-properties expression parsing incompatibility between this Iris version and that pack. Mentioning it only in case it is relevant — it appears unrelated to the freeze.

issues.title: [26.3] Crash on first frame: "Missing uniform InSampler" in CenterDepthSampler.sampleCenterDepth
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

26.3

### Iris Version

1.11.6+26.3-fabric

### Sodium Version

mc26.3-0.9.2-fabric

### Operating System

Windows 11 Home (build 26200)

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 596.49, OpenGL backend)

### Java Version

Java 25.0.3 (JetBrains Runtime)

### Reproduction Steps

1. Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3, Sodium 0.9.2 and Iris 1.11.6
2. Enable a shaderpack that reads `centerDepthSmooth` (reproduced with both **BSL v10.1.8** and **Complementary Unbound r5.9.3**)
3. Join a singleplayer world
4. The game crashes on the first rendered frame

### Crash Report file and latest.log

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing uniform InSampler (should be COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER)
	at knot//com.mojang.renderpearl.frontend.FrontendRenderPass.validateDraw(FrontendRenderPass.java:476)
	at knot//com.mojang.renderpearl.frontend.FrontendRenderPass.drawIndexed(FrontendRenderPass.java:221)
	at knot//net.irisshaders.iris.pathways.CenterDepthSampler.sampleCenterDepth(CenterDepthSampler.java:110)
	at knot//net.irisshaders.iris.pipeline.IrisRenderingPipeline.beginHand(IrisRenderingPipeline.java:1050)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.wrapOperation$zde000$iris$beginTranslucents(LevelRenderer.java:4070)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.lambda$addMainPass$0(LevelRenderer.java:459)
	at knot//com.mojang.blaze3d.framegraph.FrameGraphBuilder.execute(FrameGraphBuilder.java:67)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.render(LevelRenderer.java:287)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.wrapOperation$zdl000$iris$renderLevel(GameRenderer.java:4018)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.renderLevel(GameRenderer.java:693)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.render(GameRenderer.java:496)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.renderFrame(Minecraft.java:1376)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.runTick(Minecraft.java:1274)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.run(Minecraft.java:967)
	at knot//net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:292)
```

Full crash report available on request.

### Additional context

Looks like a mismatch between the pipeline and the draw in `CenterDepthSampler.sampleCenterDepth()` on the `26.3` branch:

- It sets `CompositeRenderer.COMPOSITE_PIPELINE`, which declares `.withBindGroupLayout(BindGroupLayouts.IN_SAMPLER)`.
- The draw itself feeds its inputs through the legacy Iris program (`depth` / `altDepth` via `addDynamicSampler`) and never binds `InSampler` on the render pass.
- 26.3's `FrontendRenderPass.validateDraw` checks every bind group the pipeline declares before drawing, so it throws on the missing `InSampler`. 26.2 didn't validate this, which is presumably why it only shows up now.

It only triggers for packs that read center depth (the early return in `sampleCenterDepth` skips it otherwise), so packs without DOF / auto-exposure may load fine. `CenterDepthSampler.java` hasn't changed on `26.3` since before 1.11.6, so it doesn't appear to be fixed on the branch yet.

Possibly related (same validation, different sampler): #3347, #3137.

Reproduced in a Fabric dev environment (Loom `runClient`) with other mods present (LibGui, ModMenu, Litematica/MaLiLib, and my own mod), none of which appear in the trace.

issues.title: [26.2] Regression in Iris 1.11.4: terrain renders see-through in Vivecraft VR eye views
issues.body: ### What happened? Versions: Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3, Sodium 0.9.1, Vivecraft 26.2-1.3.15. RTX 4080, Valve Steam Frame via SteamVR. Works: Iris 1.11.2. Broken: Iris [1.11.3 /] 1.11.4. Everything else unchanged. Problem: In VR with two shader packs I tried (tested Complementary Reimagine and BSL), only terrain within a few blocks renders. Beyond that, the ground is see-through and deeper terrain/caves show through the floor. Details: Only the left/right eye views are affected. Vivecraft's first-person desktop mirror renders correctly at the same moment. Flat screen (Vivecraft installed, VR off) is fine. Reproduces in a minimal instance (Fabric API, Sodium, Iris, Vivecraft, one shader pack). Vivecraft version doesn't matter (tested 1.3.11 through 1.3.15). Changing shader pack settings, Vivecraft render settings, and Sodium culling options had no effect. ### Screenshots ### Log output ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 26.2 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.11.4+mc26.2 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? RTX 4080 ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Leftover debug logging: "Type is VERTEX/FRAGMENT" logged at WARN on every DH shader transform
issues.body:
### Summary

A leftover debug statement logs `Type is VERTEX` / `Type is FRAGMENT` at **WARN** level on every Distant Horizons shader transform. It's context-free — no prefix, no explanation — so it just looks like something is wrong.

Two identical occurrences on the current `26.1` branch:

- [`DHGenericTransformer.java:76`](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/26.1/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/pipeline/transform/transformer/DHGenericTransformer.java#L76)
- [`DHTerrainTransformer.java:93`](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/26.1/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/pipeline/transform/transformer/DHTerrainTransformer.java#L93)

```java
Iris.logger.warn("Type is " + parameters.type);
```

### Why it looks unintentional

It sits mid-routine, wedged between two blocks of matrix-uniform injection, and it is the **only** `logger` call in either file:

```java
tree.parseAndInjectNode(t, ASTInjectionPoint.BEFORE_DECLARATIONS,
    "uniform mat4 iris_ProjectionMatrixInverse;");

Iris.logger.warn("Type is " + parameters.type);   // <-- here

// TODO: All of the transformed variants of the input matrices, preferably
// computed on the CPU side...
root.rename("gl_ModelViewMatrix", "iris_ModelViewMatrix");
```

### Impact

Every Iris + Distant Horizons user hits it, and it fires per shader transform rather than once. One launch of my setup produced **114 lines** (57 `VERTEX` + 57 `FRAGMENT`), and it repeats on every shader reload or shader-option change.

It's only log noise, but it's noise at WARN in a file that otherwise logs nothing, and it makes real warnings harder to spot when users are reading logs to diagnose something else.

```
[22:20:35] [Render thread/WARN]: Type is VERTEX
[22:20:35] [Render thread/WARN]: Type is FRAGMENT
[22:20:35] [Render thread/WARN]: Type is VERTEX
[22:20:35] [Render thread/WARN]: Type is FRAGMENT
...
```

### Suggested fix

Delete both lines, or drop them to `debug`.

### Environment

- Iris `1.9.7+mc1.21.10` (Fabric), MC 1.21.10, Sodium `0.7.3`
- Distant Horizons `3.3.2`, Complementary Unbound `r5.9.3`
- Confirmed present in the current `26.1` branch, so not specific to my build

---

### Second, smaller item — happy to split this into its own issue

`LodRendererEvents` sets DH config values through the API overload that doesn't identify the caller, which DH now warns about:

```
[Render thread/WARN]: Config [enableDhFog] was set by [net.irisshaders.iris.compat.dh.LodRendererEvents$2]
    via the deprecated API method that doesn't define the API caller.
[Render thread/WARN]: Config [enableSsao] was set by [net.irisshaders.iris.compat.dh.LodRendererEvents$13]
    via the deprecated API method that doesn't define the API caller.
```

DH 3.3.2's changelog notes this: *"When a config value is being controlled by the API, API users can now provide their mod's name to show who is actively controlling that option — for old API users this value will appear as 'UNKOWN' and a warning will be logged."*

The three call sites are all in `common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/compat/dh/LodRendererEvents.java`:

| line | call |
|---|---|
| 93 | `DhApi.Delayed.configs.graphics().fog().drawMode().setValue(...)` |
| 274 | `DhApi.Delayed.configs.graphics().ambientOcclusion().enabled().setValue(false)` |
| 275 | `DhApi.Delayed.configs.graphics().fog().drawMode().setValue(EDhApiFogDrawMode.FOG_DISABLED)` |

Passing Iris's name through the newer overload would clear the warnings and make DH's config screen attribute the override to Iris instead of `UNKOWN`, which seems strictly better for users wondering why their DH fog setting is being ignored.

---

### A non-report, for completeness

My log also has `Failed to resolve uniform inSulfurCaves, reason: Unknown variable: BIOME_SULFUR_CAVES` with a full 40-line stack trace, from `CustomUniforms.<init>`. I checked and **no** `sulfur_caves` biome exists in any of my installed mods, so Complementary is referencing a biome that isn't present — that's the shaderpack's business, not Iris's, and I'm not reporting it as an Iris bug. Mentioning it only because a full `RuntimeException` stack trace at WARN for a shaderpack optionally referencing a modded biome may be heavier than it needs to be; entirely your call whether that's worth softening.

issues.title: Shadows bounce with View Bobbing on 26.2 (Sodium): terrain and gbufferModelView appear out of sync while walking
issues.body:
### What happened?

With **View Bobbing** enabled, shadows (and anything else a shaderpack derives from reconstructed world positions) bounce up and down in sync with the walking bob. Stand still or fly and they are stable; turn View Bobbing off and the problem disappears completely.

It is most visible when the sun is low (sunrise/sunset): shadow edges on walls and the ground jump by several blocks between steps, then settle back when you stop walking. At noon it is subtler but still present.

**Reproduction**

1. Minecraft 26.2 + Sodium 0.9.2 + Iris 1.11.4, any shaderpack with shadows (seen with our own pack; a user report suggests Complementary Reimagined/Unbound are affected too, see *Additional context*).
2. Enable View Bobbing.
3. Set the time to early morning or late evening (for example `/time set 23500` or `12500`) so the sun is low.
4. Walk forward and backward slowly near terrain and watch the shadow edges.

**Expected:** shadows stay fixed in the world while walking, as they do with View Bobbing off.
**Actual:** shadows move up and down with every step of the bob.

### How our pack uses the matrices

The deferred and composite passes rebuild world positions from depth in the standard way:

```glsl
vec3 viewPos   = projectAndDivide(gbufferProjectionInverse, vec3(uv, depth) * 2.0 - 1.0);
vec3 playerPos = mat3(gbufferModelViewInverse) * viewPos + gbufferModelViewInverse[3].xyz;
```

and sample the shadow map with `shadowProjection * shadowModelView * vec4(playerPos, 1.0)`. The shadow pass itself is unaffected by bobbing. So the bounce means the matrices shaders receive (`gbufferModelView` and/or `gbufferProjection`) do not match the transform terrain was actually rasterized with, while the camera bobs.

### Where I think the mismatch is (hypothesis)

`MixinModelViewBobbing` skips the `mul(bobbingEffectsModel)` on the projection, stores the bob in `bobStack`, and applies it with `modelViewMatrix.mulLocal(bobStack)` at the `LevelRenderer.render(...)` call. `MixinLevelRenderer.iris$setupPipeline` then captures that (bobbed) model-view as `gbufferModelView`, and `gbufferProjection` comes from `sodium$getProjectionMatrix()`.

If Sodium's terrain renders with a model-view obtained before or independently of that `mulLocal` (so without the bob) while `gbufferModelView` includes it, every terrain pixel reconstructed with `gbufferModelViewInverse` would be offset by the bob, which matches the symptoms exactly: only while walking, only with View Bobbing on, and strongest at grazing sun angles where a small position error moves shadow edges far. On the 26.1 branch the `render` target also received a `ChunkSectionsToRender` that was prepared before the wrapped call, which is one way that could happen. I have not confirmed which object Sodium reads on 26.2, so please treat this part as a lead, not a diagnosis.

Supporting observation: deriving terrain normals through `gbufferModelViewInverse * gl_NormalMatrix` instead of using `gl_Normal` directly also wobbled with the bob, which reduced but did not remove the shadow bounce once we switched to `gl_Normal`.

### Screenshots

A series taken while walking forward a few steps at sunrise shows the shadow edge on a cliff face jumping between frames. I can attach these if helpful.

### Log output

I can provide `latest.log` on request. Relevant versions are listed below; no errors or warnings are logged when it happens.

### Minecraft Version

26.2 (Fabric Loader 0.19.5)

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.11.4+mc26.2.jar (with sodium-fabric-0.9.2+mc26.2.jar, Distant Horizons 3.3.2)

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (driver 616.56)

### Additional context

- Flying (no bob) is fine; walking with View Bobbing on is not; turning View Bobbing off fixes it entirely.
- A LabyMod idea report describes shadows shaking with View Bobbing under Iris + Sodium in Complementary Reimagined/Unbound and Astralex: https://www.labymod.net/en/idea/17783 (I have not reproduced those packs myself).
- I could not find an existing Iris issue for this.

issues.title: [26.3] Deferred/composite alpha-channel outputs corrupted while Distant Horizons renders (blend or color-mask state leak?)
issues.body: ### What happened? **Summary** With Distant Horizons rendering on 26.3, deferred/composite outputs that store data in the alpha channel get corrupted: they appear to be blended with, or keep, previous-frame values. In Complementary Reimagined this shows up as dark rectangular patches/outlines on reflective blocks that smear while the camera moves and settle when it stops. Moving that data out of the alpha channel fixes it completely, with DH still rendering. **Environment** - Minecraft 26.3 (Fabric), Iris 1.11.6+mc26.3, Sodium [version], Distant Horizons 3.3.2-26.3 - Complementary Reimagined r5.9.3, default High profile - DH: Extreme quality, CPU load "I Paid For The Whole CPU" - NVIDIA RTX 5080, driver 617.14, Windows 11 - Other mods: CCME, Continuity, Essential, Fabric Language Kotlin, Lithium, Sodium, Reese's Sodium Options, Sodium Extra **Steps to reproduce** 1. Load Complementary Reimagined r5.9.3 with default settings (Block Reflection Quality: High). 2. Stand in a cave lit by torches or lava, looking at a stone/deepslate floor. 3. Turn or move the camera. Expected: stable reflections. Actual: dark block-shaped patches and outlines that trail the camera motion. **Isolation** - Gone with DH "Enable Rendering" off. - Gone with Block Reflection Quality set to Low (disables Complementary's PBR reflections). - The same shader pack version is fine on 26.2. - Not the hand, TAA, SSAO or shadows: it reproduces in spectator mode, and toggling those changes nothing. **What fixed it** Complementary keeps reflection data in alpha channels: fresnel in colortex4.a (deferred1, draw buffer 2) and reflection-history depth in colortex7.a (composite, draw buffer 0). Its main color outputs write alpha = 1.0, which is why the rest of the image looks normal. A local edit that moves this data into RGB and writes alpha = 1.0 removes the artifact entirely (diff attached). That points to GL state leaking into these passes: either blending left enabled (SRC_ALPHA-style blending with alpha < 1 mixes each output with the previous frame) or alpha writes masked off. Possible cause: 26.3 tracks blend enable per draw buffer, and Iris now sets that cache directly (BLEND_ENABLE[i]) instead of the old setUnknownState() resync. If something (possibly DH) changes the real GL state without updating the cache, the cached GlStateManager._disableBlend(i) calls behind IrisRenderSystem.disableBlend() would be no-ops, and likewise for _colorMask in the composite pass setup. Forcing raw glDisablei(GL_BLEND, i) / glColorMaski per draw buffer in the composite pass setup should confirm it. **Related** - https://github.com/ComplementaryDevelopment/ComplementaryReimagined/issues/366 (ghosting/smearing on 26.3 + Iris 1.11.6) - https://github.com/X0nk/Bliss-Shader/issues/657 (glitching once DH generates LODs on 26.3 + DH 3.3.2 + Iris 1.11.6) **Attachments** [DHFIX_CHANGES.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32577061/DHFIX_CHANGES.txt) ### Screenshots ### Log output Full log available on request. ### Minecraft Version 26.3 ### Iris Version Iris 1.11.6+mc26.3 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 ### Additional context I am just a player that enjoys your mod, this bug was found thanks to the help of Claude Opus 5.5. I'm not taking any credit. All I can say is that it works.

issues.title: Feature discussion: built-in decoding of resource-pack equipment geometry before shaderpack processing

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I maintain a custom armor project whose resource pack encodes mesh positions, UVs and face-selection metadata in equipment textures. A vanilla core shader reconstructs the mesh from the native, already-posed armor carrier quads. When a shaderpack is enabled, replacing that core shader leaves the carrier geometry and incorrect texture coordinates visible instead.

I understand this is the documented core-shader limitation, not an Iris regression. This proposal does not ask Iris to merge arbitrary GLSL programs or run a server-provided Java module.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Would a narrowly specified, opt-in equipment geometry format with a decoder built into Iris be within the project's scope? The decoder would emit ordinary entity vertices before shaderpack processing, preserving Minecraft's native limb poses rather than approximating them with server-driven entities.

The intended contract is:

- Read and validate declarative geometry data from the active resource pack, with explicit format/version and resource limits; no executable code supplied by the server.
- Reconstruct the original surface before Iris/Sodium derives extended vertex attributes, preserving UVs, normals, lighting, overlay and entity/item context.
- Supply consistent geometry to the world, shadow and enchantment-glint paths; keep equipment context per deferred submission rather than in a shared last-texture variable.
- Leave the player's shaderpack unchanged. No shaderpack detection by name, forced shaderpack download or shaderpack-specific patch is intended.

The distribution constraint matters: vanilla players should only need the resource pack, and shader users should not need another compatibility mod or a special Iris fork. An extension API alone would not satisfy this unless the required implementation also ships with Iris. I recognize that accepting and maintaining this functionality is entirely the maintainers' decision; this is a scope/integration question, not a demand or ETA request.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Server-provided or adapted shaderpacks: these restrict or replace the player's selected shaderpack and are a different approach from this proposal.
- An additional client compatibility mod: technically possible, but does not meet the project's installation requirement.
- Server-driven display entities: do not preserve the original native per-frame articulation under that requirement.
- Adding mesh fields to vanilla equipment JSON: Minecraft 1.21.11's equipment codec does not consume those fields as custom body geometry.

Related requests: #2606 proposes server shaderpack delivery; #2757 proposes server compatibility information/payloads. This proposal instead concerns a data decoder before shaderpack processing. If it belongs under an existing discussion, please redirect it rather than treating this as a request to reopen general core-shader compatibility.

**Additional context**

There is a local experimental implementation targeting Minecraft 1.21.11, Iris source commit `0a1fcaae55099356bf53410b4f5302753edb0ffc` and Sodium 0.8.14. It decodes static payloads through both ordinary VertexConsumer and Sodium bulk paths, with a per-equipment glint replay. An independent local GPU comparison against the original GLSL and limited visual checks with unmodified shaderpacks provide partial evidence; the code and fixtures are not attached here, so these are reported local results, not independently reproducible evidence for maintainers yet.

It is not merge-ready. Animation, materials, mixed ordinary/custom layers, GUI, draw-base context, reload behavior, performance and wider visual coverage remain open. It also does not solve the separate glint limitation in a genuinely vanilla client. I am not claiming compatibility with every shaderpack or GPU.

Before preparing a public synthetic reproduction and focused patch, I would appreciate guidance on whether this belongs in Iris at all and, if so, the preferred integration point and data contract. It is also useful to know if this is outside the project's scope.

Reference: [Iris core-shader compatibility explanation](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/26.1/docs/development/compatibility/core-shaders.md).

issues.title: Latest Iris beta for Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric breaks emissive textures
issues.body: ### What happened? The latest update breaks emissive textures supported by mods like Continuity. This only occurs while shaders are enabled (any) and does not occur on previous versions. The bug happens when an item with emissive texture support is rendered in the world (held, dropped, in an item frame, etc) and another item with emissive texture support, or a seemingly random other assortment of items, is also rendered in the world in one of those ways as well. This occurs in a minimal environment with only the required mods installed (Sodium, Iris, Continuity, an emissive texture supported content mod or emissive texture support resource pack, and all of their dependencies) 1. Enable a shaderpack, I used Complementary Reimagined as a popular baseline. 2. Render in an item with emissive texture support. For my testing I used the Wizard Staff from the Wizards (RPG Series) mod by Daedelus. 3. Render in another item with emissive texture support, or test various random items to see which ones do and don't also trigger the bug. Examples that triggered it for me were an Apple and Item Frame, but a Stick did not in spite of it triggering the bug when these mods were used in a full modpack (Dungeon Heroes). 4. Observe the broken emissive textures, either on the first or second rendered item. In my minimal setup testing the first rendered item broke, while in the modpack I discovered this in it was the second rendered item that did. 5. When picking the item back up or swapping to a non-offending item/empty hand, the texture returns to behaving like it should. Expected outcome is that the emissive textures should behave consistently and not break from rendering in another item, regardless of the item's features ### Screenshots Item renders normally with an empty hand Emissive texture breaks when another emissive texture is present A stick did not cause an issue in this minimal setup However an apple did Similarly, an item on its own on the ground renders normally But holding another emissive texture breaks the dropped item's emissive texture With shaders disabled, both examples (item frame and dropped) function normally ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32488506/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.8.14-beta.1+mc1.21.1 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 2070 ### Additional context To get mod content emissive texture support to actually activate with Continuity, a resource pack is still needed to trigger the activation. I used this simple resource pack to define the optifine emissive properties support. Testing with an emissive textures resource pack shouldn't require this [Emissive Items.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32488927/Emissive.Items.zip)

issues.title: DISTANT_HORIZONS absent until manual reload: DH-ready re-bake never rebuilds the pipeline
issues.body:
## Versions

- Iris `1.10.7+mc1.21.11` (Fabric)
- Distant Horizons `3.3.1-1.21.11-fabric-neoforge`
- Minecraft `1.21.11`, Fabric Loader `0.19.5`, Fabric API `0.141.6`
- Sodium `0.8.12+mc1.21.11`
- Also installed and relevant to one detail below: Super Resolution `0.9.1-alpha.2+opengl`

## Summary

With Distant Horizons installed, the shader pack that Iris compiles for the first world of a session was preprocessed **without** `DISTANT_HORIZONS`. DH's `DhApiAfterDhInitEvent` makes Iris load the pack a second time (a second `Using shaderpack:` line, this time with the macro), but that second load only replaces `Iris.currentPack`; the `IrisRenderingPipeline` already cached in `PipelineManager` — built from the first, macro-less pack — keeps rendering. The DH bridge then draws `dh_terrain`/`dh_water` into a pipeline whose deferred passes have no DH arm (in my pack: no `dhDepthTex*` read, so LOD terrain resolves as sky). Pressing R (`Iris.reload()`) fixes it for the rest of the session.

## Reproduction

1. Install Iris 1.10.7, Distant Horizons 3.3.1 and any shader pack that forks on `#ifdef DISTANT_HORIZONS` (something visible, e.g. reading `dhDepthTex0` in a deferred pass).
2. Launch and join a world. Do not touch the shader menu.
3. Observe that the pack behaves as if DH were absent (the `DISTANT_HORIZONS` arm is not compiled) while DH's LODs are being submitted to Iris's DH programs.
4. Check `logs/latest.log`: two `Using shaderpack:` lines, the second a few seconds after `DH Ready, binding Iris event handlers...`, and no `Creating pipeline` after the second one.
5. Press R (or reload from the shader pack screen): the pipeline is destroyed and re-created and the DH arm now works.
6. Every launch of this install reproduces it (three consecutive sessions checked).

## Log excerpt (Iris and DH lines only, one session)

```
[02:05:19] [Render thread/INFO]: Distant Horizons client Initialized.
[02:05:22] [Render thread/INFO]: Debug functionality is enabled, logging will be more verbose!
[02:05:24] [Render thread/INFO]: Profile: Custom (+6 options changed by user)
[02:05:28] [Render thread/INFO]: Using shaderpack: Bulle-Shader
[02:05:30] [Render thread/INFO]: Creating pipeline for dimension minecraft:overworld
[02:05:36] [Render thread/INFO]: Running Delayed setup...
[02:05:36] [Render thread/INFO]: Delayed setup complete, firing DhApiAfterDhInitEvent event...
[02:05:36] [Render thread/INFO]: DH Ready, binding Iris event handlers...
[02:05:36] [Render thread/INFO]: DH Iris events bound.
[02:05:37] [Render thread/INFO]: Profile: Custom (+6 options changed by user)
[02:05:40] [Render thread/INFO]: Using shaderpack: Bulle-Shader
          ... (world joined at 02:06:47; DH LODs drawn through the 02:05:30 pipeline) ...
[02:12:57] [Render thread/INFO]: Destroying pipeline minecraft:overworld        <- manual R
[02:12:57] [Render thread/INFO]: Profile: Custom (+6 options changed by user)
[02:13:02] [Render thread/INFO]: Using shaderpack: Bulle-Shader
[02:13:02] [Render thread/INFO]: Creating pipeline for dimension minecraft:overworld
```

Note the 02:05:40 `Using shaderpack:` has neither a `Destroying pipeline` before it nor a `Creating pipeline` after it.

## Mechanism (from the 1.10.7 jar)

1. **The macro is decided by a cached static flag.** `StandardMacros.createStandardEnvironmentDefines()` defines `DISTANT_HORIZONS` iff `isModLoaded("distanthorizons") && DHCompat.hasRenderingEnabled()`. `hasRenderingEnabled()` returns `DHCompat.checkFrame()` → `DHCompatInternal.checkFrame()`, which returns the static `DHCompatInternal.dhEnabled` (initially `false`).

2. **The flag is only refreshed once a pipeline exists.** `DHCompatInternal.checkFrame()` refreshes `dhEnabled` (and calls `Iris.reload()`) only inside
   `if ((dhEnabled != configs.graphics().renderingEnabled().getValue() || guiScale != …) && Iris.isPackInUseQuick())`,
   and `Iris.isPackInUseQuick()` is `getPipelineNullable() instanceof IrisRenderingPipeline` — false until the first `IrisRenderingPipeline` is built. So any pack load that happens before the first pipeline (and before DH's event) bakes the macro set with `dhEnabled == false`, even though `DhApi.Delayed.configs` is already non-null at that point (DH assigns it in `Initializer.preConfigInit()` during `onInitializeClient`).

3. **The pipeline gets built from that pack.** `Iris.onLoadingComplete()` (from `MixinTitleScreen`, first `TitleScreen.init`) calls `PipelineManager.preparePipeline(OVERWORLD)`, which builds `new IrisRenderingPipeline(currentPack.getProgramSet(dim))` and caches it in `pipelinesPerDimension`. On this install that happens at 02:05:30, before DH's event at 02:05:36. (What makes the title screen initialise that early on this install is a mod-ordering question I have not pinned down, but Iris's handling below is wrong whenever it happens.)

4. **DH-ready re-loads the pack but not the pipeline.** `LodRendererEvents$1.afterDistantHorizonsInit` (DH's `DhApiAfterDhInitEvent`, fired from DH's `CLIENT_STARTED` listener) does:
   - `Iris.loadShaderpackWhenPossible()` — a flag that `Iris.handleKeybinds()` (next `Minecraft.tick`) consumes with a **bare `Iris.loadShaderpack()`**, not `Iris.reload()`. `loadShaderpack()` → `loadExternalShaderpack()` creates a new `ShaderPack` (this time `createStandardEnvironmentDefines()` sees `dhEnabled == true` and defines the macro) and assigns `currentPack`, then logs `Using shaderpack:`. It never calls `PipelineManager.destroyPipeline()`, so `preparePipeline(OVERWORLD)` on world join returns the cached pipeline compiled from the previous `ShaderPack` instance. `destroyPipeline()`'s only callers are `Iris.reload()` and the dimension-change hook in `MixinMinecraft_PipelineManagement`.
   - `DHCompatInternal.dhEnabled = configs.graphics().renderingEnabled().getValue()` — a **direct write**. This is what disarms the one remaining self-repair: `checkFrame()` is called at `LevelRenderer.renderLevel` HEAD every frame (`MixinLevelRenderer.iris$setupPipeline`), and on the first world frame `isPackInUseQuick()` is finally true; had `dhEnabled` still been `false`, `checkFrame()` would have seen `dhEnabled != renderingEnabled` and called `Iris.reload()`. Because the event handler already made them equal, the condition is never true and no reload ever happens.

Net: the pack is baked twice, the second time correctly, and the pipeline is built exactly once, from the first bake.

One detail specific to this install, mentioned for completeness: `Iris.onRenderSystemInit()` correctly skips `loadShaderpack()` when DH is loaded, but Super Resolution (`io.homo.superresolution…MinecraftMixin.onClientStarted`, injected into `Minecraft.<init>`) reflectively calls `Iris.reload()` during client construction, which is where the 02:05:24–02:05:28 first bake comes from. That mod is not the cause of the bug — any `preparePipeline` that precedes DH's event produces the same result, and a pipeline built from a `currentPack == null` state (`VanillaRenderingPipeline`) would equally never be replaced by the bare `loadShaderpack()` — but it explains why the first `Using shaderpack:` line appears at all under DH.

## Expected behaviour

Either of:

- **Rebuild after the DH-triggered load.** Have the `loadShaderpackWhenPossible` path (or `afterDistantHorizonsInit` itself) go through `Iris.reload()` semantics — destroy the cached pipelines, load, and `preparePipeline` if a level exists — instead of a bare `loadShaderpack()`. Equivalently, make `PipelineManager.preparePipeline` notice that `currentPack` is no longer the instance its cached pipeline was built from.
- **Or defer the first bake/pipeline until DH is ready** when `distanthorizons` is loaded, so that `createStandardEnvironmentDefines()` is never evaluated with the stale `dhEnabled`, and do not pre-empt `checkFrame()`'s reload by writing `dhEnabled` directly in the event handler.

## Workaround

Reload the pack once after joining the first world (R in the shader pack screen, or `IrisApi.getInstance().getConfig().setShadersEnabledAndApply(true)` from a mod). Pack authors cannot work around it from GLSL: the macro is simply absent from the running program set.

issues.title: [26.1.2] IllegalStateException: Missing sampler Sampler1 — Iris-overridden program declares Sampler1 for vanilla RenderTypes that never bind overlay (e.g. item_cutout/item_translucent)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Environment
- Minecraft 26.1.2, NeoForge 26.1.2.109, Java 25 (dev run; IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE = true)
- Iris 1.11.4+mc26.1.2 (sha256 32D672A890D3C74F75227ABC7E7EF048BBB83A799BF46632F03F0583D4C22BE5)
- Sodium 0.9.1+mc26.1.2
- Shader pack: ComplementaryUnbound_r5.9.3.zip (config/iris.properties: enableShaders=true)

Crash
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing sampler Sampler1
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.trySetup(GlCommandEncoder.java:531)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.executeDraw(GlCommandEncoder.java:406)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlRenderPass.drawIndexed(GlRenderPass.java:145)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderPass.drawIndexed(RenderPass.java:95)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.rendertype.RenderType.draw(RenderType.java:112)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource$BufferSource.endBatch(MultiBufferSource.java:99)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.lambda$addMainPass$0(LevelRenderer.java:707)

Analysis (source-level, Iris branch 26.1 @ bff1e69c, MOD_VERSION 1.11.4)
1. Vanilla is self-consistent for item rendering: RenderPipelines.ITEM_SNIPPET declares only
   withSampler("Sampler0") and withSampler("Sampler2") (RenderPipelines.java:75-82) and
   RenderTypes.ITEM_CUTOUT / ITEM_TRANSLUCENT deliberately omit useOverlay()
   (RenderTypes.java:151-174), so RenderSetup.getTextures() (RenderSetup.java:88-116) never
   provides "Sampler1" for those passes.
2. Iris maps those pipelines to ENTITY-format shader keys:
   IrisPipelines.java:37 assignToMain(RenderPipelines.ITEM_CUTOUT, p -> getCutout(p)) ->
   ShaderKey.ENTITIES_CUTOUT_DIFFUSE; IrisPipelines.java:36 ITEM_TRANSLUCENT -> ShaderKey.ENTITIES_TRANSLUCENT;
   both use IrisVertexFormats.ENTITY (ShaderKey.java:42-43) which contains UV1
   (IrisVertexFormats.java:48-56).
3. ExtendedShader builds its sampler uniform list from the vertex format, not from the vanilla
   pipeline's declared samplers: "if (vertexFormat.contains(VertexFormatElement.UV1)) samplerList.add("Sampler1");"
   (ExtendedShader.java:119-121, then super.setupUniforms(..., samplerList) at :127).
4. MixinUniform redirects the name "Sampler1" to the pack's "iris_overlay"
   (MixinUniform.java:36-38); the pack shader actually declares and uses iris_overlay because
   EntityPatcher injects it whenever inputs.hasOverlay() is true (EntityPatcher.java:46,55;
   ShaderAttributeInputs.java:42-44) — i.e. exactly when the vertex format has UV1.
   => program().getUniforms() contains "Sampler1" for a pass whose samplers only contain
   Sampler0/Sampler2 => vanilla validation throws (GlCommandEncoder.java:526-532).
5. Throwing validation is vanilla code; Iris only adds @Inject(HEAD, cancellable) for Iris custom
   passes and @Inject(RETURN) for its own state setup (MixinGlCommandEncoder.java:91-160, 162-172).
   Iris already handles the missing sampler case by binding a 1x1 white pixel to unit 1
   (ExtendedShader.java:213-219) — but that runs AFTER the vanilla check.

Scope
- The exception is dev-only: the whole validation block is behind
  GlRenderPass.VALIDATION = SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE && !Boolean.getBoolean("neoforge.disableGlValidation")
  (GlRenderPass.java:25, SharedConstants.java:126). In production the missing sampler is silently
  skipped (GlCommandEncoder.java:609-613).
- Reproduces with shaders ON; does not reproduce with shaders OFF. Independent of other mods
  (verified with ImmediatelyFast both enabled and disabled).

Suggested fix
- Restrict the sampler list used for setupUniforms to the samplers the vanilla pipeline/RenderSetup
  can actually supply (e.g. intersect the format-derived list with what the RenderType provides), or
  treat "Sampler1"/"Sampler2" as optional for ENTITY-format programs (same spirit as the
  white-pixel fallback already present in ExtendedShader.iris$setupState).

Workaround for users/dev
- run with -Dneoforge.disableGlValidation=true (dev), or disable shaders.

_No response_

NeoForge 26.1.2.109

issues.title: Iris Shader crashing after Sodium update
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

26.1.2

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.11.3+mc26.1.2.jar

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-0.9.2-beta.1+mc26.1.2.jar / sodium-fabric-0.9.2+mc26.1.2.jar

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 

### Java Version

Java 25

### Reproduction Steps

Since Sodium was updated today, Iris Shaders has caused my Minecraft to crash when I start loading into my world, even if I use an older version of Sodium. I was able to linked it that Iris was the issue going through my mods one by one to see what was causing the crash. If I use the new version of Sodium, I get the fabric loader incompatible mods error and using Sodium on it's own without Iris allows me to launch into the world.

issues.title: Constant log spam when using Iris Shaders alongside Estrogen and Immersive Engineering
issues.body: ### What happened? Enabling [Iris Shaders](https://modrinth.com/mod/iris/) while having [Estrogen](https://modrinth.com/mod/estrogen) and [Immersive Engineering](https://modrinth.com/mod/immersiveengineering/) installed causes a constant log spam. Disabling Shaders causes the spam to stop. Reproduction Steps: 1. Create a Minecraft: 1.21.1, NeoForge: 1.21.248 instance 2. Install - [Iris Shaders [1.8.14-beta.1]](https://modrinth.com/mod/iris/version/1.8.14-beta.1+1.21.1-neoforge), (and its dependency, [Sodium [0.8.13]](https://modrinth.com/mod/sodium/version/mc1.21.1-0.8.13-neoforge)), - [Estrogen [1.0.8]](https://modrinth.com/mod/estrogen/version/6.0.8+1.21.1-neoforge), (and its dependencies, [Kotlin for Forge [5.12.0]](https://modrinth.com/mod/kotlin-for-forge/version/5.12.0), [Cynosure [1.0.2]](https://modrinth.com/mod/cynosure/version/1.0.2-neoforge), and [Curios API [9.5.1]](https://modrinth.com/mod/curios/version/9.5.1+1.21.1)) - [Immersive Engineering [12.4.2-194]](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/immersive-engineering/files/all?page=1&pageSize=20&version=1.21.1&showAlphaFiles=show) - [Complementary [r5.8.1]](https://modrinth.com/shader/complementary-reimagined/version/r5.8.1) 3. Create a new world. 4. Enable shaders (Default key: O), wait for them to be enabled, unpause the game and look around to make sure the shaders are enabled. 5. Disable shaders. 6. Check your latest.log, if you CTRL+F search for `[Render thread/INFO] [Iris/]: Using shaderpack:`, you will find the moment you enabled shaders. Looking beyond this point, you will see log spam up until right before you turned off the shaders. That end point can also be found by searching for `[Render thread/INFO] [Iris/]: Shaders are disabled because enableShaders is set to false in iris.properties in your latest.log.` All of the spam is sandwiched between those enable/disable logs. The log spam does not occur with only Estrogen, or only Immersive Engineering installed. Both mods, alongside Shaders are all the minimum required things for this to occur. ### Screenshots ## Log Spam ## Disabling Shaders After disabling shaders (2nd [Iris/] message down, "`[Render thread/INFO] [Iris/]: Shaders are disabled because enableShaders is set to false in iris.properties in your latest.log.`"), the constant spam finally stops. ### Log output ## Log Spam - Immersive Engineering 12.4.2-194 - Estrogen 1.0.8 - Iris 1.8.14-beta1 - [debug](https://mclo.gs/6uUpyTj) - [latest](https://mclo.gs/Xv0rCTN) ## Non-spammed 2 way Logs to confirm its a 3 way issue - Estrogen 1.0.8, Immersive Engineering 12.4.2-194 - [debug](https://mclo.gs/vNcJcsS) - [latest](https://mclo.gs/J6OK78h) - Estrogen 1.0.8, Iris 1.8.14-beta1 - [debug](https://mclo.gs/PfQLAts) - [latest](https://mclo.gs/DKEaYrO) - Immersive Engineering 12.4.2-194, Iris 1.8.14-beta1 - [debug](https://mclo.gs/sVbgiM5) - [latest](https://mclo.gs/6JAdUbb) ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.14-beta.1+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia Geforce GTX 1060 3GB ### Additional context These aren't duplicate issues, they're semi-related but I think they might help with context somehow. ## Old 1.20.1 Oculus report This issue was nearly identical to one I reported to the 1.20.1 Oculus GitHub, https://github.com/Asek3/Oculus/issues/855, with the only difference being that this issue has Iris shaders (being on 1.21.1, of course), instead of Oculus. Other than that, the issue is exactly the same, requiring specifically Immersive Engineering, Estrogen, and (Iris/Oculus) Shaders. I just thought it was worth mentioning because I thought it was odd how the error stayed the exact same throughout all the ports, the error message in this new 1.21.1 issue is identical to that old 1.20.1 one. ## "Fixed warn about shader uniforms in logs" update in Estrogen 1.0.8 There was a separate issue with a similar (but not identical) log spam that occurred when using ***only*** Iris and Estrogen 1.0.7. I previously reported to Estrogen first, (https://github.com/MayaqqDev/Estrogen/issues/398), and in their most recent update after that report (1.0.7 -> 1.0.8) the log spam that occurred from that issue no longer occurs. I'm unsure if that issue is still causing anything to happen internally that isn't visible from the log. Maybe I should open that one as a separate issue here as well now? Still just thought it was worth mentioning for context here. That 1.0.8 changelog has nothing to do with this new issue. ## Final note Apologies for the length of this, the 3-way-mod-issue does not make it easy, especially with the other issues and context that went behind me getting to this issue specifically. Thank you to anybody dealing with this!

issues.title: [26.2] Iris breaks cache of ProjectionMatrixBuffer.getBuffer(Projection)
issues.body:
### What happened?

If you start the game with a shader pack enabled and then disable shaders, the cached buffer slice returned by `ProjectionMatrixBuffer.getBuffer(Projection)` becomes unusable with the same Projection instance as used before disabling shaders. Getting it to work again requires increasing the version of the Projection instance (setting it to dirty, e.g. with `setSize`). I assume what fixes the issue is `writeBuffer` being called again. 
I could be wrong with the exact mechanics of this as I don't know what changes Iris/Sodium make here.
This does not occur if you start the game with shaders disabled, then enable a shader pack and then disable them again, so I can only conclude that this is a bug on your end or Sodium. 
This causes a compatibility issue with my minimap mod. I am planning to implement a fix/workaround on my end, but I thought it'd be a good idea to report it here too.

issues.title: Huge fps drop with any shader in a 437 mod pack: GPU sits at 40%, one thread pinned (1.8.14-beta.1)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Framerate collapses the moment I turn a shader on, and the size of the drop is way out of line with what the same shaders cost me in smaller packs.

Same machine, same world, same spot, standing still:

- no shader: **120-140 fps**
- shader on: **~40 fps**

On lighter packs those same shaders take me from around 130 to around 90, which feels normal to me. Here it is a third of the framerate.

What I do not get is that nothing is actually busy. I sampled once a second for 45 seconds while playing normally, with the shader on:

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU utilisation | 41% average, 48% peak |
| Power draw | 84 W of a 250 W limit |
| Core clock | 2905 MHz, so it is boosting fine and has nothing to do |
| VRAM | 6.9 GB of 12 GB |
| Busiest game thread | **83.8% of a single core** |
| Every other thread added up | about 40% of a core |

So the GPU is coasting at 40% while one thread carries the whole thing, on a 12 core / 24 thread CPU. That reads as render thread bound to me, not as the shader being expensive to shade.

Things I already ruled out:

- swapping to a completely different shader pack: no change
- fullscreen vs windowed: about 5 fps
- moving the window to the monitor that is actually wired to the discrete GPU: no change
- the game is running on the RTX and not on the iGPU, confirmed with nvidia-smi

The pack is heavy on block entities, there is a lot of Create machinery in view at all times. My guess is the shadow pass roughly doubles draw call submission on the render thread and that is where it runs out of road. What I would like to know is whether a drop of this size is expected in this situation, or whether something is going wrong that should not be.

Happy to run test builds or pull more numbers if that is useful.

### Minecraft Version

1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248

### Iris Version

iris-neoforge-1.8.14-beta.1+mc1.21.1, alongside sodium-neoforge-0.8.13-beta.2+mc1.21.1

### Operating System

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045)

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070, driver 32.0.16.1656 (2026-08-19).
CPU is a Ryzen 9 7900X, 32 GB of RAM, 8 GB allocated to the game on G1GC.

### Additional context

Modpack is All the Mods 10: Aeronautics v0.5.1, 437 mods.

The shader I normally run is Complementary Reimagined r5.4 with Euphoria Patches 1.5.2, but as above, the drop is the same on other packs.

I will attach latest.log in a comment right after posting this.
