issues.title: `MixinRenderPipeline` returns a 1-element array from `getVertexFormatBindings()`, crashing `validateDraw` in dev environments (MC 26.2)
issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary.** On Minecraft 26.2, with any shaderpack active, the client crashes 15–90 seconds
after entering any world — **but only in a development environment** (Loom / ModDev
`runClient`). The cause is `MixinRenderPipeline#iris$change2` replacing the pipeline's
vertex-format-bindings array with a one-element array, while the vanilla contract is a fixed
sixteen-slot array that `GlCommandEncoder.validateDraw` iterates in full. A minimal,
verified fix is included below.

**Reproduction:**
1. A mod-dev environment (`runClient` — anything where `SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE` is true).
2. Iris 1.11.2+mc26.2 and Sodium 0.9.1+mc26.2 as the **only** two mods installed.
3. Enable any shaderpack (reproduced with Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1 + EuphoriaPatches 1.9.3 and a custom pack).
4. Enter any world — a freshly created vanilla world reproduces it.
5. Crash within 15–90 seconds (eight consecutive sessions, one identical signature).

**Stack trace:**

```
Description: Render Frame
java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 1 out of bounds for length 1
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.validateDraw(GlCommandEncoder.java:506)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.executeDraw(GlCommandEncoder.java:521)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlRenderPass.drawIndexed(GlRenderPass.java:153)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderPass.drawIndexed(RenderPass.java:179)
	at net.minecraft.client.renderer.rendertype.PreparedRenderType.drawFromBuffer
	at net.minecraft.client.renderer.feature.RenderTypeFeatureRenderer.executeGroup
	at net.minecraft.client.renderer.feature.FeatureRenderDispatcher$PreparedFrame.executeSolid
	at net.irisshaders.iris.pathways.HandRenderer.renderSolid(HandRenderer.java:119)
```

The enclosing pass varies (`HandRenderer.renderSolid` or `ShadowRenderer.renderShadows`);
the exception never does.

**Root cause.** Vanilla's `RenderPipeline` keeps vertex format bindings in a fixed-size
array, one slot per vertex buffer:

```java
private final @Nullable VertexFormat[] vertexFormatPerBuffer = new VertexFormat[16];

public @Nullable VertexFormat[] getVertexFormatBindings() {
    return this.vertexFormatPerBuffer;
}
```

`MixinRenderPipeline#iris$change2` injects at RETURN and replaces the value with a
**one-element** array:

```java
cir.setReturnValue(new VertexFormat[]{IrisVertexFormats.TERRAIN});
```

`GlCommandEncoder.validateDraw` then walks all sixteen slots:

```java
for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
    if (renderPass.vertexBuffers[i] == null && pipeline != null
            && pipeline.info().getVertexFormatBindings()[i] != null) { ... }
}
```

Second iteration → AIOOBE.

**Why this is rarely reported:** `GlRenderPass.VALIDATION` is
`SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE && !Boolean.getBoolean("neoforge.disableGlValidation")`,
so the check only runs in a development environment. Players can never trigger it; mod
developers testing with shaders enabled hit it every time.

**Fix (verified).** Preserve the array length — clone the original and replace the slot
instead of returning a new one-element array:

```java
VertexFormat[] original = cir.getReturnValue();
if (original == null || original.length == 0) return;

VertexFormat vf = original[0];
VertexFormat replacement = null;
if (Objects.equals(vf, DefaultVertexFormat.BLOCK)) {
    replacement = IrisVertexFormats.TERRAIN;
} else if (Objects.equals(vf, DefaultVertexFormat.POSITION_TEX_LIGHTMAP_COLOR)) {
    replacement = IrisVertexFormats.GLYPH;
} else if (Objects.equals(vf, DefaultVertexFormat.ENTITY)) {
    replacement = IrisVertexFormats.ENTITY;
} else if (Objects.equals(vf, ChunkMeshFormats.COMPACT.getVertexFormat())) {
    replacement = WorldRenderingSettings.INSTANCE.getVertexFormat().getVertexFormat();
}

if (replacement != null) {
    VertexFormat[] copy = original.clone();
    copy[0] = replacement;
    cir.setReturnValue(copy);
}
```

This is also slightly more correct in production: slots 1–15 of the original bindings are
preserved instead of dropped.

Verification: the change was applied to a local build of 1.11.2 and run **with GL validation
enabled** — the exact condition under which the stock jar died within 16–83 seconds in eight
consecutive sessions. The patched build survived full sessions and shut down cleanly. It was
additionally run in a regular launcher installation (validation off) on both NeoForge builds
with no visible rendering regressions.

**Workaround for anyone hitting this today:** `-Dneoforge.disableGlValidation=true` on the
dev run configuration (at the cost of losing GL validation entirely).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Log output

Crash report from the minimal reproduction (Iris + Sodium as the only two mods, fresh
vanilla world). Local filesystem paths are redacted; the full `latest.log` is available on
request.

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 26.2 (NeoForge 26.2.0.59 and 26.2.0.66 — identical crash on both)

### Iris Version

iris-neoforge-1.11.2+mc26.2.jar (stock, SHA-1 6533…dd15)

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (driver 610.88)

### Additional context

Sodium 0.9.1+mc26.2, Java 25.0.4, dev environment NeoForge ModDev Gradle 2.0.144
(`runClient`). While isolating this we also reproduced the Sodium 0.9.2-alpha
incompatibility already tracked in #3290 — it is unrelated to this bug.

Happy to open a PR with the change above if that's easier for you.

---

**Disclosure:** this bug was investigated, root-caused, patched and verified by Claude
(Opus 5) running in Claude Code — including decompiling the release jar, locating the mixin,
and building the fixed class for verification. The human developer ran every in-game session
that produced and later disproved the crashes, and asked me to write this report. We are
stating this openly so you can weigh the report accordingly; every claim above is
reproducible from the environment described.

issues.title: Allow Unknown Vanilla Shaders to load with Iris by default

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Overview**
I'm a developer for a mod by the name of "Jaden's Nether Expansion" and it utilizes a library mod by the name of LodestoneLib to add custom render types for things like entities and particles. The issue however is that these custom render types do not load properly when Iris with Sodium is installed, often preventing the game from loading entirely or leading to entities and particles which utilize said custom render types to be invisible.

I've gotten numerous complaints about this over the course of a few months now and I kept redirecting them to the one solution that I found to have worked in resolve this issue, and that is to set the `allowUnknownShaders` boolean flag to true in the `iris.properties` config. This seemingly fixes both the game perpetually getting stuck during loading and causes the entities to render as intended when shaders are being used.

https://github.com/ThatJadenXgamer/Jadens-Nether-Expansion/issues/281

**Proposed Solution**
I request some kind of feature for mod developers such as myself be added to force our unknown shaders to load automatically regardless of the config value is set to, and/or looking into making `allowUnknownShaders` enabled by default. I don't know if this causes any issues but I found people mention that JNE is not the only mod which requires you to fiddle with iris configs to properly work. And that this might be a universal issue with anything that introduces custom render types that utilize their own vanilla shaders.

issues.title: Gizmos do not render correctly with a shaderpack: `debug_filled_box` is missing from the override list, and the always-on-top depth clear is skipped
issues.body:
### What happened?

## What happens

`net.minecraft.gizmos.Gizmos` draws nothing useful once a shaderpack is enabled. A cuboid gizmo
marked `setAlwaysOnTop()` should be a filled, outlined box drawn through terrain. With a shaderpack
on, the fill disappears entirely and the outline is occluded by any block in front of it.

Without a shaderpack, the same code is correct on both loaders.

This affects vanilla's own debug renderers as well as mods, since `Gizmos` is the public drawing
API on 26.x.

## Reproducing

1. Install Iris and enable any shaderpack.
2. From a client tick, emit a cuboid gizmo behind a wall:

```java
Gizmos.cuboid(pos, 0.02F, GizmoStyle.strokeAndFill(0xFF00FF00, 2.5F, 0x4000FF00))
      .setAlwaysOnTop();
```

3. Expected: a filled green box visible through the wall. Actual: no fill, and the outline is hidden
   behind the wall.

Vanilla's `F3 + B` hitboxes or any debug renderer that uses filled gizmos should show the same
thing.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Log output

Logs, four combinations:

- Fabric 26.1.2, Iris 1.11.3: https://mclo.gs/F6hjJ3f
- NeoForge 26.1.2, Iris 1.11.3: https://mclo.gs/ptQNxn6
- Fabric 26.2, Iris 1.11.2: https://mclo.gs/m4uFI63
- NeoForge 26.2, Iris 1.11.2: https://mclo.gs/RPjSLcB

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 26.1.2/26.2

### Iris Version

Iris 1.11.2/1.11.3

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

Radeon RX 5700 XT

### Additional context

## Two separate causes

These look like one bug and are not, so I have kept them apart.

### 1. `debug_filled_box` is not in the override list

```
[Render thread/FATAL]: Missing program minecraft:pipeline/debug_filled_box in override list.
This is likely an Iris bug!!!
```

`IrisPipelines` assigns around sixty vanilla pipelines and none of the four `DEBUG_*` ones
(`DEBUG_FILLED_BOX`, `DEBUG_QUADS`, `DEBUG_TRIANGLE_FAN`, `DEBUG_POINTS`). Gizmo quads go through
`RenderTypes.debugFilledBox()`, so they land here, while gizmo lines go through
`RenderTypes.lines()`, which is mapped to `ShaderKey.LINES` and does render. That is exactly the
split seen in game: outlines yes, fill no.

An assignment along the lines of the existing entries looks like it would cover it:

```java
assignToMain(RenderPipelines.DEBUG_FILLED_BOX, p -> ShaderKey.BASIC_COLOR);
```

I have not opened a PR because I do not know which `ShaderKey` you would want for each of the four,
and whether debug pipelines are excluded deliberately. Happy to send one if you say which mapping
you prefer.

Worth noting the log line appears only once per pipeline per session, because of the
`missingShaders.add(renderPipeline)` guard in `MixinShaderManager_Overrides`. Switching shaderpacks
afterwards will not log it again, which can make it look shaderpack specific when it is not.

### 2. The always-on-top depth clear is skipped under shaders

`MixinLevelRenderer`:

```java
@WrapOperation(method = "lambda$addLateDebugPass$0",
    at = @At(value = "INVOKE", target = "...CommandEncoder;clearDepthTexture(...)"))
private void skip(CommandEncoder instance, GpuTexture texture, double v, Operation<Void> original) {
    if (!IrisApi.getInstance().isShaderPackInUse()) {
        original.call(instance, texture, v);
    }
}
```

That `clearDepthTexture` call is the whole mechanism behind `setAlwaysOnTop()`. Vanilla clears the
main depth texture immediately before executing the phase, in `addLateDebugPass` on 26.1 and
`addAlwaysOnTopPass` on 26.2, so anything in it draws over the world. Skipping it means always-on-top
silently stops meaning anything.

I assume this guard is deliberate, since clearing the main depth texture mid frame would destroy
depth that composite passes rely on. If so, this is a feature request rather than a bug: some way to
run that phase against a target where depth can be discarded, so gizmos keep their documented
behaviour under shaders. I am not asking for the guard to be removed.

Fixing only 1 would restore the fill but leave the box buried in terrain, so on its own it does not
make always-on-top gizmos usable.

## Why it matters

`Gizmos` is the supported way to draw world space markers on 26.x, and `setAlwaysOnTop()` is the
only documented way to draw through terrain without a custom pipeline. Any mod using it for markers
or highlights loses the feature whenever a shaderpack is on, with no error a user would connect to
the cause.

issues.title: DH terrain lightmap sampler is not usable with Iris on Minecraft 26.2
issues.body: ### What happened? The lightmap sampler no longer provides the actual Minecraft lightmap when used from dh_terrain. My shader receives valid lmcoord values, and the coordinates correspond correctly to the expected light levels. However: > vec4 light = texture2D(lightmap, lmcoord); does not return the vanilla Minecraft lightmap. gl_Color also only contains the block albedo/color and does not contain block/sky lighting. This worked in previous versions. Expected behavior texture2D(lightmap, lmcoord) in dh_terrain should provide the same lightmap texture used by vanilla terrain, so shaderpacks can reproduce vanilla lighting exactly. This is especially important because manually reconstructing lighting from lmcoord.x/y does not reproduce vanilla lighting correctly (brightness settings, block light colors, sky light, gamma, etc.). Minimal reproduction > #version 130 compatibility > > uniform sampler2D lightmap; > > in vec2 lmcoord; > > void main() { > gl_FragColor = texture2D(lightmap, lmcoord); > } With normal terrain this samples the expected lightmap, but with dh_terrain the result is not the vanilla lightmap. Why this matters Shaderpacks that want vanilla-style lighting for Distant Horizons LOD terrain currently have no way to sample the actual Minecraft lightmap. Could lightmap (or an equivalent sampler exposing the same texture) be made available to dh_terrain? Thanks. ### Screenshots 26.2 I didn’t keep track of which version this started happening in, but as you can see, this bug is clearly not present in IRIS 1.7.6 yet. 1.20.1 Mods 1.20.1 ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 26.2 ### Iris Version 1.11.2 ### Operating System 10 ### What is your GPU? 5060ti ### Additional context I tried 1.21.11, but it was the same there I’ll upload a simple shader for testing. issues.title: Add GPU-accessible world raycast / occlusion query for shader packs
issues.body:
## Goal

Add a GPU-accessible raycast / occlusion query mechanism for shader packs.

The goal is not general-purpose path tracing, but a lightweight visibility/occlusion query that can be used for sparse samples such as shadows.

## Use Case

Currently, shadow rendering generally requires generating a full shadow map every frame, potentially at very high resolutions such as 8192×8192, even though a large portion of those texels may never contribute to the final image.

Instead, shader packs could query visibility only for the receiver samples that are actually needed for the current frame.

**Concrete example:** A shader could quantize visible block surfaces into a fixed 16×16 shadow grid per block, then perform occlusion queries only for the visible grid cells that require a shadow result, rather than rendering an entire 8192×8192 shadow map.

This could significantly reduce unnecessary rasterization and memory bandwidth for intentionally pixelated or sparse shadow techniques.

## Desired Functionality

Shader packs should be able to cast rays from arbitrary positions in arbitrary directions and receive:

**Minimum required:**

- Hit / miss result
- Distance to the first hit

**Highly desired, if feasible:**

- Hit position
- Surface normal
- Block information
- Entity information

## Important Constraints

- **GPU-accessible:** The query needs to be usable from GLSL shaders rather than relying on CPU-side APIs such as `BlockView.raycast()`.
- **Suitable for high query counts:** It should be practical to perform many visibility queries per frame.
- **Geometry support:** Block geometry alone would already be useful. Entity geometry would be beneficial, but is not required if supporting it would significantly complicate the implementation.

## Rationale

Traditional shadow maps have some limitations for this type of rendering:

1. Surfaces viewed at oblique angles from the light source receive reduced effective texel density.
2. Large shadow maps may rasterize and store many texels that are never sampled by the final image.
3. Shadow-map resolution is tied to light-space projection rather than the desired resolution of the receiving surface.

A sparse, on-demand GPU occlusion query mechanism would allow shader packs to determine visibility only at the samples they actually need.

This could enable techniques such as fixed-resolution pixel-art shadows—for example, exactly 16×16 shadow samples per block face—without requiring an equivalently massive full-resolution shadow map.

issues.title: **Feature Request: Hardware-accelerated ray tracing support via NVIDIA's GL_NV_ray_tracing extension**

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Problem**
Right now, "ray traced" shaderpacks like SEUS PTGI do ray tracing entirely in software: they raymarch/voxel-trace inside a fragment shader on regular shader cores. It works, but it's expensive and doesn't use the dedicated ray tracing hardware (RT cores) that's been sitting unused on modern GPUs since 2018.

**Proposal**
Expose NVIDIA's RTX hardware to shaderpack authors through the `GL_NV_ray_tracing` extension, which NVIDIA maintains specifically to bring their RT cores into OpenGL (same hardware path Vulkan/DirectX games use, just wrapped for GL).

**To be clear about scope:** I'm not asking Iris to implement ray tracing itself, or to build any specific effect (GI, reflections, shadows, etc.). Iris wouldn't need a ray tracing renderer of its own — similar to how SSBOs are already exposed as a low-level primitive, Iris would just expose the acceleration-structure/trace primitives to the shader API. Whether and how to actually use hardware ray tracing would stay entirely up to each shaderpack author (SEUS, Complementary, etc.) to decide, same as any other optional feature flag.

This would be purely additive: shaderpacks that don't use it keep working exactly as today, on every GPU.

**Why this can only work on NVIDIA**
This isn't a design choice, it's a limitation of OpenGL itself. Unlike Vulkan, which got an official, vendor-neutral ray tracing standard in 2020 that AMD, Intel and NVIDIA all implement, OpenGL never got one. NVIDIA built its own private "bridge" (`GL_NV_ray_tracing`) so their RT cores could still be reached from OpenGL, but AMD and Intel never built an equivalent — their ray tracing hardware can only be reached through Vulkan or DirectX 12. So on OpenGL there's simply no door to walk through for non-NVIDIA cards; Iris wouldn't be choosing to leave AMD/Intel out, there's currently no API for them to use even if it wanted to.

**Why it matters**
Minecraft has one of the most popular "true" ray traced shaderpacks around (SEUS PTGI), and it's currently bottlenecked running entirely on shader cores. Hardware RT support could mean better quality and/or framerate for players who have the hardware, at zero cost to everyone else.

(Again, I'm not saying that Iris has to implement it itself, but give shader creators the ability to implement it on their own).

issues.title: [26.2] Reversed-Z projection appears to break advanced shadow culling and nearly doubles rendered sections
issues.body:
### Description

Minecraft 26.2 causes a large shader performance regression compared with 26.1.2 when using the corresponding Iris 1.11.2 and Sodium 0.9.1 builds. The regression correlates with Iris' advanced shadow frustum selecting almost twice as many terrain sections.

The cross-version test keeps the Iris/Sodium version numbers, shader pack, world, camera position, video settings, and shader settings the same.

### Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU
- Driver: NVIDIA 610.62 (OpenGL 3.3)
- Resolution: 1920x1080
- Fabric Loader: 0.19.3
- Shader pack: Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1
- Shader pack SHA-256: `3F1CD389E717B2E62F58EDFF222059B9C60DE71B14BB49B517EB58318CE35B15`
- Render distance: 25
- Iris shadow distance: 15
- FPS limit: 140
- Graphics backend on 26.2: OpenGL
- Material filtering: disabled in both tests

Test A:

- Minecraft 26.1.2
- Iris 1.11.2+mc26.1.2
- Sodium 0.9.1+mc26.1.2

Test B:

- Minecraft 26.2
- Iris 1.11.2+mc26.2
- Sodium 0.9.1+mc26.2

### Results at the same location and camera angle

| Metric | 26.1.2 | 26.2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Instantaneous FPS | 138 | 84 |
| GPU utilization | 96% | 100% |
| Iris shadow section stats | `C:682/51384 (F) D:25` | `C:1310/51384 (F) D:25` |
| Sodium terrain geometry memory | `G:785/1388 MiB` | `G:909/1576 MiB` |
| Sodium index memory | `I:2/51 MiB` | `I:2/51 MiB` |
| Loaded region buffers | `#139` | `#139` |

The loaded region count and total section count are identical, but the shadow pass selects 92% more sections. Frame time increases from about 7.25 ms to 11.90 ms while the GPU becomes fully saturated.

A previous comparison using Iris 1.10.9/Sodium 0.8.12 on 26.1.2 showed the same general 26.2 regression, but the test above removes the mod-version-number confound.

### Source/bytecode findings

I compared the actual release jars used in the test.

These Iris classes are byte-for-byte identical between `1.11.2+mc26.1.2` and `1.11.2+mc26.2`:

- `BaseClippingPlanes.class`
- `AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum.class`
- `BoxCullingFrustum.class`
- `BoxCuller.class`

`ShadowRenderer#createShadowFrustum` is also semantically identical in both builds.

However, Minecraft's `Projection#getMatrix` changed:

26.1.2 effectively calls:

```java
setPerspective(fov, aspect, zNear, zFar, zZeroToOne);
```

26.2 effectively calls:

```java
setPerspective(fov, aspect, zFar, zNear, zZeroToOne);
```

The main depth clear value also changed from `1.0` to `0.0`, consistent with Minecraft 26.2's documented reversed-depth-buffer change.

Iris captures Sodium's raw projection matrix in `MixinLevelRenderer`:

```java
CapturedRenderingState.INSTANCE.setGbufferProjection(
    new Matrix4f(((GameRendererStorage) Minecraft.getInstance().gameRenderer)
        .sodium$getProjectionMatrix())
);
```

That matrix is later used by `ShadowRenderer#createShadowFrustum` to construct `AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum`. `BaseClippingPlanes` is unchanged and still derives six planes using fixed clip-space directions, including Z = -1 and Z = +1.

This suggests the advanced shadow culling code is consuming the new reversed-Z projection without normalizing it to the convention expected by `BaseClippingPlanes`. The observed result is an overly permissive shadow frustum and roughly twice as many submitted shadow sections.

Relevant source paths:

- https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/844542b8440f1ce6479d2914c212d099ff9d264c/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/mixin/MixinLevelRenderer.java
- https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/844542b8440f1ce6479d2914c212d099ff9d264c/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/shadows/ShadowRenderer.java
- https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/844542b8440f1ce6479d2914c212d099ff9d264c/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/shadows/frustum/advanced/BaseClippingPlanes.java
- https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/844542b8440f1ce6479d2914c212d099ff9d264c/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/shadows/frustum/advanced/AdvancedShadowCullingFrustum.java

### Expected behavior

The 26.2 advanced shadow frustum should select approximately the same number of sections as 26.1.2 for the same camera, world, render distance, and shadow distance.

### Possible fix direction

Normalize/reconstruct the camera projection used by advanced shadow culling so that it uses the clip/depth convention expected by `BaseClippingPlanes`, or make `BaseClippingPlanes` explicitly aware of reversed-Z and zero-to-one depth.

I can provide both F3 screenshots and logs if needed.

issues.title: Vanilla clouds don't render using shaders
issues.body:
### What happened?

When enabling shaders there are no clouds (If a shader doesn't have custom clouds or you configured a shader to use vanilla clouds). Even when reloading shaders clouds don't appear.

You can force vanilla clouds to render by changing setting in Iris config to allowUnknownShaders=true, but still everytime you load the game you have to reload shaders to make clouds appear

Tested with just Sodium 0.8.12 and Iris 1.8.14 Beta 1 on 1.21.1 Neoforge

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Download shaders that don't have custom clouds (for ex Miniature Shader)
2. Load a world with shaders enabled
3. See no clouds

issues.title: Armor Trim Render Issue NeoForge Minecraft 1.21.1
issues.body: ### What happened? **Description** There is an issue with Iris rendering armor trims on NeoForge. Armor trims are rendered beneath the armor model instead of on top, making them appear invisible during normal gameplay. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Install Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge 21.1.235. 2. Install Sodium 0.6.13 and Iris 1.8.12 (no other mods required for reproduction). 3. Create or equip any trimmed armor. 4. Observe that the trims do not appear in-game. **Expected Behavior** Armor trims should render on top of the armor model, as they do in vanilla and on Fabric. **Actual Behavior** The armor trim is rendered underneath the armor model. Using Shoulder Surfing Reloaded to make the player model translucent reveals that the trim is still being rendered, but behind the armor. **Additional Testing** * The issue occurs with no shaders enabled. * The issue occurs with no resource packs enabled. * The issue occurs with Iris installed alongside only Sodium. * Removing Iris immediately restores correct armor trim rendering, both in an isolated test and in my full modpack. * The issue appears to be specific to NeoForge. I was unable to reproduce it on Fabric. * Fabric 0.19.3 on Minecraft 26.2 using sodium-fabric-0.9.1+mc26.2.jar and iris-fabric-1.11.2+mc26.2.jar didn't produce the issue. * Fabric 0.19.3 on Minecraft 1.21.1 using sodium-fabric-0.6.13+mc1.21.1.jar and iris-fabric-1.8.8+mc1.21.1.jar didn't produce the issue. * I tested multiple Iris versions on NeoForge, and all exhibited the same behavior. Attached are: 1. A screenshot of the armor in the inventory showing the trim. 2. A screenshot showing the trim missing in-game. 3. A screenshot with translucent armor (using Shoulder Surfing Reloaded) showing the trim rendered underneath the armor. ### Screenshots ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 10 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080Ti ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Rendering Corruption After Changing FullScreen Scale. [NeoForge 1.21.1]
issues.body: ### What happened? Changing Minecraft's Fullscreen scale causes immediate visible rendering corruption. This happens with all of the shaders I've tested, (Complementary Reimagined, Rethinking Voxels, Photon). I was able to recreate these issues in a minimal pack with NeoForge 21.1.234 and 21.1.235 where only the following mods were on it, Sodium 0.8.12, Iris 1.8.14 (Earlier Versions crashed the game during loading), and Distant Horizons 3.1.2-b. I was able to determine that Distant Horizons wasn't the main cause of the rendering error as having the mod disabled or having the rendering turned off still produced rendering corruption upon changing the fullscreen scale. The specific rendering corruption appears in 3 ways, the first way is without Distant Horizons. What can happen is all blocks and clouds become completely transparent, making it 100% impossible to see anything. The second way is that you get artifacts appearing around your backgrounds, chat, inventories, and options. The final way is with Distant Horizons Enabled, where only the LOD's and entities are visible, and the actual loaded chunks the player is in are completely invisible, including the player itself. To Reproduce: 1. Download and Install NeoForge 21.1.234 or 21.1.235 on Minecraft 1.21.1 (21.1.234 has a much worse problem with the rendering corruption). 2. Download and Install Sodium 0.8.12 and Iris 1.8.14 Beta 1. 3. Download and Install Shaderpacks (I used Complementary Reimagined for testing). 4. Optionally Download Distant Horizons. 5. Run the game and enter a world. 6. Upon Entering the world, select the shaders and enable them. 7. From there, go the the Video Settings and change the Fullscreen Resolution. 8. The problem should immediately appear. Here is a quick Reproduction Matrix for understanding the issue I'm having Configuration | Render Scale | Window Mode Vanilla: | ✅ Works | ✅ Works DH only: |✅ Works | ✅ Works Iris + Shader: |❌ Breaks | ✅ Works Iris + Shader + DH: |❌ Breaks | ❌ Breaks A couple things I did to see if I could fix the issue: F3+A Changing render distance Changing Sodium chunk update mode Shader reloading Windowed/Fullscreen Mode changing Different render scale options The Results of the attempted fixes ended up not recovering the rendering for any realistic gameplay ability. On the plus side, because this is a visual rendering issue, the issues presented do not actually affect chunk generation or world data, and as long as the Fullscreen settings are restored to "Current" the issue goes away after a quick shader reload. (As for why I'm trying to run a different that is smaller than my monitor, I'm running a pretty heavy modpack and there are some player-made areas where running the full monitor resolution completely tanks my FPS with shaders enabled. Below I've attached the logs and screenshots of what I've witnessed. ### Screenshots ### Log output [debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29730208/debug.log) [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29730209/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version Neoforge 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.14 -beta.1+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 10GB ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Invisible Items in Inventories
issues.body: ### What happened? I cant find where this bug was reported before so I'm making a new thread. There is a bug where items in any inventory will not display their icon. I have taken many of the typical troubleshooting steps like: uninstalling all unrelated mods, updating graphics drivers, and restarting my PC. I have been told that other people have had trouble with recreating this bug, so I will try to outline the steps I take to get the biggest result. The easiest way for me to reproduce the bug is, on a fresh boot of the game, go into a singleplayer creative world, toggle shaders to either enabled or disabled(whichever is the opposite from what I logged into the world as), then when I open the creative inventory most or all of the items aren't loaded in. I did discover a "fix" for this bug. When I try to re-produce the bug with the steps above, but I scroll through the entire creative inventory first, none of the items are invisible after enabling/disabling shaders. I changed from the default minecraft launcher over to a fresh instance on multiMC, just to make sure that none of my settings were affecting the bug. With only iris sodium and fabric installed on the instance, I can no longer recreate the bug in singleplayer mode. However, when I connect to any of my servers(modded or not), I can recreate the bug with the same steps as before. None of my settings or configs were copied over to this instance. Things I haven't tried yet since I've run out of patience: - connecting to a server on a different network. - using other iris versions. - using other mod loaders. - using different shader packs Version info: - fabric-loader-0.19.3-26.2 - fabric-api-0.154.0+26.2 - iris-fabric-1.11.1+mc26.2 - sodium-fabric-0.9.0+mc26.2 - ComplementaryUnbound_r5.8.1 System info: Device Name DESKTOP-CHTP72T Processor AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor 3.70 GHz Installed RAM 32.0 GB Storage 932 GB SSD Samsung SSD 980 PRO 1TB, 1.82 TB SSD WD_BLACK SN770 2TB Graphics Card NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (16 GB) ### Screenshots ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 23.2 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.11.1+mc26.2 ### Operating System Windows 10 Home ### What is your GPU? issues.title: DH (Distant Horizons) incompatible with BLAZE_3D rendering engine
issues.body:
## Problem
Distant Horizons (DH) does not render properly when using the BLAZE_3D rendering engine. The LODs fail to display correctly and the mod becomes unusable.

This is likely because Iris's BLAZE_3D (Vulkan) rendering path does not properly integrate with DH's rendering hooks.

## Temporary Workaround
Changing DH's rendering engine from AUTO (which selects BLAZE_3D on MC 26.1.2+) to OPEN_GL resolves the issue.

## Expected Behavior
DH should work correctly when Iris uses the BLAZE_3D rendering engine.

## Environment
- Minecraft: 26.1.2
- Iris version: latest for 26.1
- Distant Horizons: 3.1.2-b-26.1.2
- Arch Linux 2026.06.01
- Nvidia RTX 3050 TI 
- Nvidia driver version: 595.58.03
- 11th Gen Intel Core i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz
## Severity
Breaks DH functionality entirely when BLAZE_3D is active. Requires manual config change to OPEN_GL as workaround.

issues.title: The screen will break in the Nether or the End
issues.body: ### What happened? A bug happened! If you are using ComplementaryReimagined r5.8.1: Placing a boat in the Nether or End will cause the screen to turn black and white (or completely black). The way the bug manifests varies depending on the shader pack. This issue does not occur if the boat is not in your line of sight, if you place a bamboo boat, or if chunk boundaries are visible. ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29593470/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 26.2 (fabric-loader-26.2) ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.11.1+mc26.2 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce RTX 3050 ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Color Spaces other than sRGB, breaks the f3 menu.
issues.body:
### What happened?

When setting color spaces with shaders enabled... i found that any color space other than sRGB broke the f3 screen... 
but i also found that other shaders like complmentary or bsl didnt break it... 
Recreatable ~

1. fabric 1.21.11 
2. install iris and sodium and fabric api
3. photon shader, solas shader.
4. set color space to anything other than sRGB and save and quit the shaders menu

issues.title: Regression: Armourer's Workshop models render incorrectly in Iris 1.8.12 (NeoForge 1.21.1)
issues.body: ### What happened? Summary After updating Iris from 1.8.8 to 1.8.12 on Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge, Armourer's Workshop models no longer render correctly. This issue only occurs while Iris is enabled. If Iris is disabled, both Armourer's Workshop and Pixelmon render correctly. According to the Iris 1.8.12 release notes, Pixelmon compatibility was fixed in this version. While Pixelmon now renders correctly, Armourer's Workshop appears to have developed a rendering regression. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I’m a user from Korea who has been using Iris Shader for a long time. When Pixelmon was updated to Minecraft 1.21.1, I naturally started using Iris as well. After seeing that the Pixelmon-related rendering issues had been resolved in Iris 1.8.12, I was very relieved and continued developing my server with confidence. Since I’m a solo developer, my plan was to build the core systems first and then move on to creating the map, decorations, and other content. However, after finishing the basic framework of my server, I started preparing to use Armourer's Workshop to decorate the world with custom interiors, furniture, themed buildings, and various decorative elements. That was when I discovered that Armourer's Workshop models render incorrectly in Iris 1.8.12. I searched through the GitHub Issues to see if anyone had experienced the same problem, and I found an issue from about a year ago mentioning that downgrading Iris to **1.8.8** resolved the Armourer's Workshop rendering issue. Unfortunately, that isn't a practical solution for me. Both **Pixelmon** and **Armourer's Workshop** are essential parts of my server. If I downgrade to Iris 1.8.8, Armourer's Workshop works correctly again [#2786](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/2786), but Pixelmon's rendering breaks. If I stay on Iris 1.8.12, Pixelmon works perfectly, but I have to give up Armourer's Workshop, which I planned to use throughout my server for decorating interiors, creating themed areas such as casinos, and making the world feel much more immersive. After spending so much time developing the server by myself, discovering this compatibility issue only after reaching the map-building stage has honestly been heartbreaking and incredibly frustrating. I completely understand that the Iris team is busy developing new features and maintaining the project, and I truly appreciate all the hard work that has gone into Iris over the years. However, if it is at all possible, I would sincerely appreciate it if someone could take a look at this compatibility issue between Iris 1.8.12 and Armourer's Workshop. Even if it cannot be fixed immediately, simply knowing whether this is something that could be addressed in the future would mean a lot to me. Thank you very much for taking the time to read this, and thank you again for all of your hard work on Iris. ### Screenshots You can't see anything in the screenshot, but... This is what it looks like after I've placed the blocks from the Armourus Workshop... ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System window 11 ### What is your GPU? RTX4080 ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Iris breaks Essential UI elements (skin preview, social panel) on the TitleScreen — mc26.2
issues.body:
**Iris version:** 1.11.1+mc26.2
**Sodium version:** 0.9.0+mc26.2
**Minecraft version:** 26.2
**Mod loader:** Fabric (loader 0.19.3-26.2)
**Essential version:** 1.4.0.2 (essential-loader 1.7.4, stage2)

**Bug description:**
With Iris installed and enabled, Essential's UI elements on the main
TitleScreen (skin preview on the left, Social/Wardrobe/Settings/Account
panel on the right) do not render at all. No errors, warnings, or
exceptions are logged related to Essential or Iris — Essential connects
to its Connection Manager successfully and loads with no issues.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Install Fabric Loader 0.19.3-26.2 on Minecraft 26.2
2. Install Essential 1.4.0.2 + essential-dependencies
3. Install Sodium 0.9.0+mc26.2 only -> Essential UI renders correctly
   on the TitleScreen
4. Add Iris 1.11.1+mc26.2 -> Essential UI elements disappear
   completely from the TitleScreen, even with no shaderpack active

**Isolation testing performed:**
- Sodium alone: Essential UI works fine
- Sodium + Iris (no shaderpack selected): Essential UI elements missing
- No crash, no error in latest.log

**Suspected cause:**
Iris ships a `net.irisshaders.iris.mixin.MixinTitleScreen` mixin
(registered in `mixins.iris.json`) that modifies the TitleScreen
rendering. This likely conflicts with how Essential injects its own
UI elements into the same screen.

I'm happy to provide the full latest.log if needed.

issues.title: Regression (1.10.8 → 1.10.9): "lines" program emitted as "#version 330 compatibility" on macOS, breaks all shaders
issues.body:
### What happened?

Minecraft: 26.1.1 (Fabric Loader 0.19.3, Fabric API 0.151.0)
Iris: 1.10.9+mc26.1.1  (regressed from 1.10.8+mc26.1)
Sodium: 0.8.9+mc26.1.1
OS: macOS 27.0, Apple M5 (OpenGL 4.1 Metal — core profile only, no compatibility profile)
Java: 25

What happens:
On 1.10.9, enabling any shader pack on macOS fails to build the pipeline:
  net.irisshaders.iris.gl.shader.ShaderCompileException: lines: lines: ERROR: 0:1: '' : syntax error: #version
  -> Failed to create shader rendering pipeline, disabling shaders!
The patched dump shows the "lines" program emitted as:
  #version 330 compatibility
Apple's GL driver is core-profile-only and rejects the "compatibility" profile, so the program won't compile.

Regression window (key detail):
With the *same shader pack, unchanged*, only swapping the Iris jar:
  - Iris 1.10.8 -> patched lines.vsh = "#version 330" (bare -> core by spec) -> compiles, shaders run.
  - Iris 1.10.9 -> patched lines.vsh = "#version 330 compatibility" -> rejected on macOS.
So the profile keyword on the "lines" program changed between 1.10.8 and 1.10.9.

Not pack-specific:
  - Reproduces on stock Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1 (its lines program is also emitted without a forced core profile on 1.10.9).
  - Within a pack, neighboring programs are fine: composites/deferred are bare "#version 330" and compile; shadow_lines comes out "#version 400 core" and compiles. Only the "lines" program leaks "compatibility".
  - Removing the pack's gbuffers_line entirely still produces a "compatibility" lines program, confirming it's generated by Iris's internal rendertype_lines path, not pack source.

Expected:
The "lines" program should be emitted in core profile on macOS, same as it was in 1.10.8 and same as every other program the patcher rewrites to core.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Shader/Entity Warmup System to Prevent First-Encounter Lag Spikes
issues.body:
## Summary

When entering water or encountering specific blocks/entities for the first time in a session, the game experiences a significant lag spike (FPS drop from ~160 to ~27-50 FPS for 0.5-1 second). This is caused by OpenGL lazy shader compilation and GeckoLib entity model initialization occurring simultaneously at first render. A warmup/precompilation system integrated in Iris would eliminate this issue.

---

## Environment

- Minecraft Version: 1.20.1
- Mod Loader: Fabric
- Fabric Loader Version: 0.15.x
- Iris Version: 1.7.6+mc1.20.1
- Sodium Version: 0.5.13+mc1.20.1
- Shader Pack: Complementary Unbound r5.8.1 + Euphoria Patches 1.9.3
- Java Version: Java 17
- JVM Flags: -Xms10G -Xmx12G -XX:+UseG1GC
- RAM Allocated: 10-12 GB
- Total Mods: 875 mods
- Platform: Windows

---

## Description

In a heavily modded Fabric 1.20.1 environment (875 mods), a consistent and reproducible lag spike occurs at the first contact with water in any new game session. Secondary spikes also occur at first contact with certain block types (leaf piles, specific flora). After the first occurrence, gameplay returns to normal and the spike never repeats for those same elements in the same session.

FPS behavior observed:
- Normal gameplay: ~130-170 FPS
- At first water contact (with all mods): drops to ~1-27 FPS for ~0.5-1 second
- After spike: returns to normal immediately

---

## Root Cause Analysis

Extensive profiling was performed using Spark Profiler across multiple test configurations. Five .sparkprofile files were collected under different mod combinations to isolate the cause.

All profiles were captured at the exact moment of first water contact.

---

## Key Finding: Layered Cause

The profiling revealed the spike is not caused by a single mod but by the cumulative simultaneous initialization of multiple systems at first water contact:

1. GeckoLib model initialization
First encounter with any GeckoLib-animated entity triggers model loading and animation controller setup. With mods like Hybrid Aquatic (80+ entities) and Naturalist, this creates a massive burst. GeckoLib has no preloading mechanism.

2. OpenGL Lazy Shader Compilation
Complementary Unbound + Euphoria Patches must compile or reconfigure shader pipelines the first time new entity types, fluid shaders, and particle effects are encountered. This is a well-documented OpenGL behavior: shaders are compiled lazily at first use, not at startup.

3. Mod-specific first-tick initialization
Several mods perform expensive first-tick operations:
- subtle_effects: sends ClientBoundEntityLandInFluidPayload and sendServerPlayerSplashes network packets
- immersivesnow + snowrealmagic: hook into precipitation tick with addToQueue and srm_randomTickProxy
- FluidGeneratorsHandler (Immersive Weathering): scans biome tags on first fluid spread

---

## GC Not Involved

VisualVM profiling confirmed that no GC pause occurs during the spike. The JVM heap was stable throughout. The cause is purely render-thread and server-thread blocking, not garbage collection.

---

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install Fabric 1.20.1 with Iris 1.7.6 and Complementary Unbound r5.8.1 + Euphoria Patches
2. Add a significant number of mods using GeckoLib (e.g. Hybrid Aquatic, Naturalist, any mob mod)
3. Create a new world
4. Open F3 overlay to monitor FPS
5. Walk into water for the first time
6. Observe FPS drop of 50-150 FPS lasting ~0.5-1 second
7. Walk into water a second time -> no spike

Minimum reproducible set:
- Iris 1.7.6 + Complementary Unbound
- Any GeckoLib-heavy mod (Hybrid Aquatic recommended)
- Subtle Effects

---

## Expected Behavior

The first contact with water should not produce a noticeable lag spike. Shader pipelines and entity models should be warm and ready before the player first encounters them in gameplay.

---

## Feature Request

We request the implementation of a warmup/precompilation system in Iris that addresses both components of this issue.

Option A - Shader Pipeline Warmup at World Load:
During world loading (the existing loading screen), Iris could iterate over registered entity render types, fluid shaders, and particle shaders and trigger a dry run compilation pass. This would pre-compile the OpenGL programs before the player enters the world, eliminating first-encounter compilation spikes. This approach is used by several game engines (Unity shader warmup API, Godot 4 pipeline pre-compilation) precisely to solve this class of problem.

Option B - Background Async Compilation:
Iris could compile shader variants for known entity/block/fluid types on a background thread during world load or shortly after spawn, before the player is likely to encounter them.

Option C - Shader Cache Persistence:
Persist compiled shader programs to disk between sessions (similar to OpenGL program binary caching), so that second and subsequent sessions benefit from cached compiled shaders without any spike.

---

## Additional Notes

- The spike occurs only once per session. Caching works at runtime, the problem is the first compilation.
- The spike is proportional to mod count. With ~10 mods it is imperceptible, with 875 mods it is 0.5-1 second.
- Disabling shaders entirely reduces but does not eliminate the spike (GeckoLib init still occurs).
- The issue is not hardware-specific. Reproduced on multiple systems, lower-end systems experience longer spikes.
- This is a well-documented OpenGL behavior referenced in multiple game engine communities as "lazy shader compilation".

---

## References

- OpenGL lazy shader compilation: documented side-effect causing first-render spikes in multiple engines
- GeckoLib 4.x: no preloading API available as of version 4.8.3
- Similar reports in Iris issue tracker: entity rendering stutters with complex shader packs

This explanation was written with the assistance of Claude AI solely because the amount of technical information to convey was too large to organize manually. That is the reason the report is structured in such a detailed and orderly way.

issues.title: Distant Horizons transparent LOD water renders over/through player with Complementary shader water
issues.body: ### What happened? When using Iris with Distant Horizons and Complementary Reimagined, enabling Distant Horizons transparency while Complementary shader water is enabled causes Distant Horizons LOD water to render over or through the third-person player model. (Or other player models in multiplayer) This only happens when the player is visually in front of the DH-rendered/LOD water area. Normal Minecraft water within regular render distance does not appear to have the same issue. Expected behavior: The player/entity should render normally in front of the water. Distant Horizons transparent water should not draw over the player model. Actual behavior: With Distant Horizons transparency enabled and Complementary shader water enabled, the water visually overlays the player model in third person, making the player look partially submerged/transparent even when standing above the water. Reproduction steps: 1. Install Iris, Sodium, Distant Horizons, and Complementary Reimagined. 2. Enable Complementary Reimagined shader. 3. Enable shader water in Complementary. 4. In Distant Horizons (OpenGL), set Transparency to Complete. 5. Go to an ocean or body of water. 6. Switch to third person and position the camera so the player is in front of distant/LOD water. 7. The distant/LOD water renders over/through the player model. Testing already done: * The issue happens with Complementary Reimagined r5.8.1. * I also tested with Euphoria Patches removed completely; the issue still happens with plain Complementary Reimagined. * If Complementary shader is turned off, Distant Horizons transparency looks correct. * If Distant Horizons transparency is turned off, the player renders correctly, but distant water has an obvious LOD seam. * Changing Distant Horizons transparency-related settings such as Blocks To Ignore, Tint With Avoided Blocks, and Vanilla Fade Mode did not fix it. * Changing Complementary water settings such as water reflections, darker oceans, generated normals, and caustics did not fix it. ### Screenshots Attached screenshots show: 1. The bug with Distant Horizons transparency enabled and Complementary shader water enabled, where water renders over/through the third-person player. 2. A comparison with shader disabled, where the player/water transparency issue mostly disappears. 3. A comparison with Distant Horizons transparency disabled, where the player renders correctly but the distant water seam becomes visible. ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28921734/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 26.1.2 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.10.9+mc26.1.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 Super (8 GB) ### Additional context This is happening on a multiplayer server. Multiple players in different areas of the world are experiencing the same issue, so it does not seem to be tied to one location, one player skin/model, or one specific ocean.

issues.title: Heads-up: Mekanism compat pseudo-mixins (MekaSuit/SPS/Flame) crash with the upcoming Mekanism 26.1 — targets changed in their renderer rework
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 26.1.2 (NeoForge 26.1.2.74 / 26.1.2.75)

### Iris Version

iris-neoforge-1.10.9+mc26.1.1.jar

### Sodium Version

sodium-neoforge-0.8.12+mc26.1.2

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti

### Java Version

Java 25

### Crash Report file / log

https://gist.github.com/reguizz/f5ed4e928fe34672f8313afae09d50e0

### Description

Hi! First off, thanks for Iris — and apologies in advance if this isn't actionable yet, since it involves a mod that hasn't even released: I've been testing **Mekanism's in-development 26.1 branch** (built from source) inside an ATM11 instance, so I fully understand if you'd rather wait until Mekanism actually ships before touching this. I mostly wanted to leave a heads-up on record, because once Mekanism releases for 26.1, modpack users will likely hit this as a hard crash on startup.

The three Mekanism compat pseudo-mixins in `mixins.iris.forge.json` no longer match the 26.1 branch of Mekanism, which reworked its renderers for the new render pipeline (`MultiBufferSource` → `SubmitNodeCollector`, `RenderType` moving to `net.minecraft.client.renderer.rendertype`):

- **`MixinRenderMekasuit`** — hard crash as soon as `MekaSuitArmor` is classloaded (during `RegisterClientExtensionsEvent`, before the main menu). `renderArm` has a new signature and no longer accesses `MekanismRenderType.MEKASUIT` directly, so the `@Redirect` fails its injection check (`(0/1) succeeded, Scanned 0 target(s)` — full stacktrace in the gist).
- **`MixinRenderSPS`** — would crash lazily when `BillboardingEffectRenderer` loads; its target method is now `render(CustomEffect, CameraRenderState, ...)`.
- **`MixinRenderFlame`** — would crash when the flamethrower's `RenderFlame` loads; it moved to the new entity render state system.

For what it's worth, Mekanism's `MekanismRenderType.MEKASUIT` / `SPS` / `FLAME` fields are currently null placeholders on their 26.1 branch (port TODOs), and all three Iris mixins currently have their bodies commented out (pass-throughs), so the compat will probably need a fresh look on both sides once Mekanism's renderer work settles — no idea what the right final shape is, you folks know that much better than I do.

As a stopgap I removed the three entries from `mixins.iris.forge.json` locally and everything runs fine alongside the ~200-mod ATM11 set, so nothing else seems affected.

Full disclosure: the diagnosis was done with the help of Anthropic's Claude (Fable 5) via Claude Code — it traced the injection failure against Mekanism's current sources. I verified the crash and the workaround myself in both Mekanism's dev environment and a production instance, but please take the analysis with a grain of salt.

Related, for cross-reference: the crash on the Mekanism side that started this investigation was https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism/issues/8588 (already fixed by their team).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build Mekanism's `26.1` branch from source and drop the jars in a NeoForge 26.1.2 instance alongside iris-neoforge-1.10.9+mc26.1.1
2. Launch the client
3. Crash before the main menu with the injection failure in the gist

issues.title: Iris appears to break Blaze3D screen capture callback during Flashback exports on macOS Apple M4
issues.body:
### What happened?

Iris Version: Iris 1.10.9+mc26.1.1
Minecraft Version: Minecraft 26.1.2
Loader: Fabric Loader 0.19.2
Environment: macOS Tahoe 26.5.1, Apple M4, Java 25.0.1
Related Mods: Flashback 0.40.0, Sodium 0.8.12+mc26.1.2, Fabric API 0.151.0+26.1.2

Description:
When exporting a replay in Flashback with Iris shaders enabled, the export freezes shortly after starting. The issue occurs even in a minimal test profile with only Fabric API, Flashback, Sodium, Iris, and a shaderpack enabled.

The Flashback developer reviewed the thread dump and said it looks like Iris may be breaking Blaze3D’s screen capture callback. The thread dump shows Flashback waiting while trying to submit downloaded frames, while the image rescale and video encode threads are waiting for frames to arrive.

What I expected to happen was...:
Flashback should be able to capture frames and complete the export while Iris shaders are enabled.

What actually happened was...:
The export freezes shortly after beginning. The game becomes unresponsive and the export never completes. This happens with shaders enabled, even after stripping the instance down to a minimal set of mods.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Launch Minecraft 26.1.2 on Fabric with Fabric API, Flashback, Sodium, Iris, and a shaderpack enabled.
2. Open a Flashback replay.
3. Start an export at 1920x1080, 30 FPS, H.264.
4. Wait for the export to begin.
5. The export freezes shortly after starting.

Additional Notes:
This was originally tested in a larger modpack, but the issue still reproduced after disabling most other mods. The remaining minimal setup was Flashback, Fabric API, Sodium, Iris, and shaders.

The regular Minecraft log repeatedly reaches `Rescaling to pixel format: 0`, followed by `colorSpaceFragment` shader warnings and Dynamic Transforms UBO resizing before the freeze.

The thread dump captured during the freeze shows:

* Render thread parked in `com.moulberry.flashback.exporting.ExportJob.submitDownloadedFrames`
* Image Rescale Thread waiting in `AsyncFFmpegVideoWriter`
* Video Encode Thread waiting in `AsyncFFmpegVideoWriter`
* Flashback dev suggested this may indicate Iris is breaking Blaze3D’s screen capture callback

This does not appear to be an encoder issue, because the same freeze occurred with both VideoToolbox and libopenh264.

issues.title: Missing sampler Sampler1 with PBR shaders on MC 26.1+
issues.body:
## Environment
- Iris 1.10.9+mc26.1.1
- Sodium 0.8.11+mc26.1.2
- NeoForge 26.1.2
- Shader pack: BSL (also reproduces with other PBR packs)

## What happens
Game crashes shortly after entering a world with a PBR shader pack enabled, usually as soon as the camera moves and the buffer source flushes block entity / item entity geometry.

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing sampler Sampler1
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.trySetup(GlCommandEncoder.java:489)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlCommandEncoder.executeDraw(GlCommandEncoder.java:406)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlRenderPass.drawIndexed(GlRenderPass.java:145)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.systems.RenderPass.drawIndexed(RenderPass.java:95)
    at net.minecraft.client.renderer.rendertype.RenderType.draw(RenderType.java:112)
    at net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource$BufferSource.endBatch(MultiBufferSource.java:99)
    ...
    at LevelRenderer.lambda$addMainPass$0(LevelRenderer.java:707)
```

## Root cause
On MC 26.1+, `GlCommandEncoder.trySetup` strictly validates every declared `Uniform.Sampler` in the GL program against `renderPass.samplers`. If a declared sampler has no binding in the map, vanilla throws `IllegalStateException("Missing sampler " + name)`.

`ExtendedShader` declares Sampler1 (normal map) and Sampler2 (specular) as uniforms when the shader pack uses PBR.

`ExtendedShader.iris$setupState` does bind a default white-pixel texture to GL texture units 1 and 2 when those samplers are absent:

```java
if (!samplers.containsKey("Sampler1")) {
    IrisRenderSystem.bindTextureToUnit(GL46C.GL_TEXTURE_2D, 1, pipeline.getBiggerWhitePixel().getTexture().iris$getGlId());
}

if (!samplers.containsKey("Sampler2")) {
    IrisRenderSystem.bindTextureToUnit(GL46C.GL_TEXTURE_2D, 2, pipeline.getWhitePixel().getTexture().iris$getGlId());
}
```

The problem:
1. These bindings happen via raw GL calls, not by inserting a `TextureViewAndSampler` into `renderPass.samplers`, so vanilla's map-based validation still throws.
2. `MixinGlCommandEncoder.iris$setupState` is injected at `@At("RETURN")` of `trySetup`, but vanilla's validation loop runs inside `trySetup` BEFORE the return, so iris's setup runs too late to prevent the throw.

## Reproduction
1. NeoForge 26.1.2 client with Iris 1.10.9 + Sodium 0.8.11
2. Install BSL or any PBR shader pack
3. Enter a world, move around for a few seconds
4. Game crashes with the stack above

## Suggested fix
Either:
- Insert placeholder `TextureViewAndSampler` entries into `renderPass.samplers` for any declared Sampler that is missing, before vanilla's validation runs (HEAD inject instead of RETURN), or
- Mixin the validation loop directly and skip the throw when the program is an `ExtendedShader` that already binds defaults at GL level

A working mod-side workaround that proves the fix: at HEAD of any draw call on `GlRenderPass`, iterate `pipeline.program().getUniforms()` and put a placeholder entry into `renderPass.samplers` for each `Uniform.Sampler` not already in the map (reusing any existing entry as the placeholder). Iris's `iris$setupState` then overrides the GL binding with the correct white-pixel texture and rendering is correct.

issues.title: Semi-transparent pixels on player skin outer layer render incorrectly with shaders
issues.body: ### What happened? Minecraft: 1.21.8 Iris: 1.9.6 Description: Semi-transparent pixels on the player skin outer layer (Hat Layer) are rendered incorrectly when any shader is enabled. The issue occurs even without ETF, EMF, resource packs, or emissive textures. Steps to reproduce: 1. Create a skin with a semi-transparent pixel on the Hat Layer. 2. Launch Minecraft with Iris. 3. Enable a shader pack. 4. Observe the pixel rendering. Expected behavior: Semi-transparent pixels should render the same way as without shaders. Actual behavior: - Complementary Unbound: parts of the outer layer disappear or render incorrectly. - Photon: semi-transparent pixels become fully opaque. - Bliss: semi-transparent pixels become fully opaque. Additional notes: The issue disappears when: - shaders are disabled; - the Hat Layer is disabled; - semi-transparent pixels are replaced with fully opaque or fully transparent pixels. issues.title: Translucent texture leads to shaders quirks only on 26.1 and above
issues.body:
### What happened?

In the NewDefault+ texture pack, leaf textures have translucent sections (opacity 1/255) to make them look better for people using fast graphics/non-see-through leaves. This used to work fine up to 1.21.11. Since 26.1, these translucent textures made shaders behave weirdly.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Download the NewDefault+ resource pack and some shaders (Complementary Unbound, Red Hat, and Steadfast in my case) into versions 1.21.11 and 26.1.2
2. Apply the shaders and notice how tree leaves appear foggy and do not wave in 26.1.2 but work fine in 1.21.11

### Screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd6ad8af-3c74-4585-87c1-796228a3bda9

26.1.2

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.10.9+mc26.1.1.jar

### Operating System

macOS 26.5

### What is your GPU?

M4 Max

### Additional context

Unsure if it is related to any sodium behavior change since 26.x but the foggy effect is also mentioned in [this issue](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3649) about how the translucent bushy leaves occluded clouds incorrectly.

### What happened?

It may not be this mod's fault, so you might not be able to do anything, but I have a good amount of performance mods and create addons and I'm still lagging. When playing on my server over time the FPS drops, I added performance mods to try to fix this. 

Now I get 100FPS but over time I get 30FPS then it turns to 20FPS. I don't know how to fix this. Maybe Iris shaders aren't compatible with Sable Mod or Create Aeronautics. I tried using NeoOculus and Embedium and I think I got better results but there not compatible with Sable mod. I really hope the lag goes away I just want to play with Distant Horizons+Iris Shaders+Create Mod+Create Aeronautics and there create addons. 

I feel like shaders should work. When turning off shaders I see performance increase, but I think it still degrades over time. So, I'm suspecting Iris or Sodium. I removed mods and did so many testing and cannot figure this out. It's been multiple days trying to fix this. 

Optifine isn't compatible so can't use that. I don't know what else to do. I pretty sure Sable and Create Aeronautics are not very good with shaders or Iris, I really hope there is a fix for this eventually. Also, I'm on the lowest settings for the shaders and I'm still lagging. 

I don't understand why. It also can't be my PC I have 96GB RAM, X67E motherboard, AMD Ryzen 7950X 16-Core Processor, 1440P Monitor. I know my PC can handle it. 8GB RAM was allocated to MInecraft it used to be 10GB but I lowered it. My JVM Agreements are -Xms4G -Xmx8G -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational. I did pregenerate chunks in my world specifically a 10,000 by 10,000 block radius but I don't think that should be an issue, but I don't know.

issues.title: A probable scam website impersonating Iris?
issues.body: I have found a website which appears to attempt to impersonate the Iris Shaders project. I am unsure if this is the right place to report this, although **because whoever created the website seems to have put some effort into it, I am concerned some people could end up getting fooled by it.** Moreover, whoever created the website also appears to have made several social media accounts also bearing the name and logo of Iris... I have already reported the website on DuckDuckGo and Google, I have also reported all its social media accounts (excluding X which is already suspended), and I believe if this website is in-fact impersonating Iris then it would be good to have that officially confirmed in an issue like this. ### List of misdeeds 1. The website appears to call itself "Iris Shaders Official". 2. The website provides a link to download a suspicious `.jar` file. 3. The website outright claims it is the "official Iris website" and urges readers to exclusively download "Iris" from it. 4. Uses the first-person pronoun "we" when describing Iris. 5. Does NOT link to any known official Iris site and instead links to several social media accounts which also appear to be impersonating Iris.

issues.title: Leaf lighting bug with awoolanche's Bushy Leaves resourcepack
issues.body: ### What happened? Having shaders enabled alongside [this](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/bushy-leaves) resourcepack causes some strange lighting bugs on leaves. They will appear totally dark if lit only by daylight, and block light causes a very sharp contrast as those illuminated by the block light will be so bright they're almost glowing, and then go to dark immediately once out of range. I expected to happen: the leaf blocks to be lit properly like other blocks. How I triggered the bug: 1. Installed and enabled Sodium and Iris. 2. Installed and enabled Complementary Shaders (5.7.1). 3. Installed and enabled awoolanche's Bushy Leaves. 4. Entered world. ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27084293/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1 ### Iris Version 1.8.12-snapshot+mc1.21.1-local ### Operating System Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Workstation) ### What is your GPU? AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT ### Additional context Using NeoForge 21.1.228. I've reached out to the pack dev as well, but only a little bit ago, so they haven't responded yet.

issues.title: Ender Dragon death animation causes most shaderpacks to break, when GUI is hidden
issues.body: ### What happened? The Ender Dragon death animation is cursed asf. Reproduction Steps (**follow them, they're important**) - Hide GUI with F1 - `/execute in minecraft:the_end run tp @s 70 70 0 0 90.00` - `/summon ender_dragon 1 80 1 {Health:0f}` The visuals become corrupt. Affects all shaders (confirmed on Complementary, BSL, Photon, Solas) ### Screenshots ### Log output No errors are logged, even with debug context. ### Minecraft Version 26.1 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.10.9+mc26.1.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Intel Arc B580 (confirmed on 7900XTX and 4080 as well) ### Additional context _No response_

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 26.1.1

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.10.9+mc26.1.1

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-0.8.9+mc26.1.1

### Operating System

Macbook Pro (M3)

### What is your GPU?

No idea, i got a basic macbook Pro M3 without any expansions on GPU

### Java Version

Java 18 (i think?? I have no idea tbh)

### Reproduction Steps

1. I've got Fabric installed for 26.1.1, sodium, iris, got my shaders, etc...
2. In the launcher I go to Java edition, check if my game is set on fabric 26.1.1 and open the game.
3. Minecraft opens up, i can see and navigate through the menu.

- disable shaders before joining a world
- enable shaders before joining a world

issues.body:
## Problem

When a Wynncraft custom skybox is active, it blocks/covers distant horizon LODs rendered by Distant Horizons. This likely also affects other LOD mods like Voxy and Bobby, but hasn't been confirmed yet.

## Root Cause

The skybox post-process pass renders a fullscreen overlay that covers everything behind the normal render distance, including LOD chunks from these mods.

## Expected Behavior

LOD chunks from Distant Horizons / Voxy / Bobby should remain visible through or behind the custom skybox effect, or the skybox should only replace the actual sky portion without occluding distant terrain.

## Notes

- Low priority — cosmetic issue, skybox still works correctly otherwise
- Needs investigation into how LOD mods integrate their rendering relative to Iris post-process passes

issues.title: Crash on first startup with Iris shader mod: Missing vertex elements mc_midTexCoord and at_tangent
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.11

### Iris Version

Iris 1.10.7 for Fabric 1.21.11

### Sodium Version

Sodium 0.8.7 for Fabric 1.21.11

### Operating System

Win. 11 Home

### What is your GPU?

AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (8 GB)

### Java Version

Java 21.0.10

### Reproduction Steps

[CrashLog.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26520948/CrashLog.txt)

ERROR:
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing elements in vertex: mc_midTexCoord, at_tangent

ENVIRONMENT:
Minecraft: 1.21.11
Essential: 1.3.10.8
Iris: 1.10.7+mc1.21.11
Shaderpack: Solas Shader V3.5.zip
Fabric Loader: 0.18.4
Java: OpenJDK 21.0.10 (Azul Systems)
Launcher: Theseus (Modrinth)
OS: Windows 11

CRASH DETAILS:
- JVM uptime at crash: 130.627s
- Time to crash: ~90 seconds after world fully loads
- Thread: Render thread

FULL STACK TRACE:
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Missing elements in vertex: mc_midTexCoord, at_tangent
at net.minecraft.class_287.method_60806(class_287.java:131)
at net.minecraft.class_287.method_60805(class_287.java:97)
at net.minecraft.class_287.method_22912(class_287.java:160)
at gg.essential.universal.vertex.VanillaVertexConsumer.pos(VanillaVertexConsumer.kt:30)
at gg.essential.model.Face.draw(Face.kt:71)
at gg.essential.model.Cube.render(Cube.kt:167)
at gg.essential.model.Bone.render(Bone.kt:161)
at gg.essential.model.BedrockModel.render$render(BedrockModel.kt:252)
at net.minecraft.class_310.method_1514(class_310.java:966)
at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:250)

CRASH ANALYSIS:
The crash occurs in Essential's BedrockModel rendering pipeline. Essential tries to render 
Bedrock models (cosmetics, capes, player skins) before Iris has fully initialized its vertex 
format transformations. The required vertex elements mc_midTexCoord and at_tangent are missing.

REPRODUCTION:
1. Clear shader cache
2. Launch with Iris + Solas Shader + Essential
3. Wait for world to load (~90 seconds)
4. Game crashes with vertex format error
5. Relaunch - works perfectly

ROOT CAUSE:
First startup: Iris hasn't finished vertex format initialization when Essential renders
Second startup: Shader cache exists, Iris initializes faster, completes before Essential

Workaround: Relaunch the game (second startup always works)

TAGS: bug, crash, shader, vertex-format, essential, iris, first-launch

issues.title: ConcurrentModificationException on client tick with monocle + architectury (NeoForge 1.21.1)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug
Game crashes with ConcurrentModificationException during the first client tick after launching. The crash occurs in the Architectury event system when iterating event listeners, with monocle's MixinClientHooks injection involved.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install FTB StoneBlock 4 modpack (v1.9.5)
2. Enable shaderpack: ComplementaryReimagined_r5.7.1.zip
3. Launch game
4. Crash occurs after ~1 client tick

### Expected behavior
Game should load normally with shaders enabled.

### Workaround
Disabling shaders in iris.properties resolves the crash:
```
enableShaders=false
shaderPack=off
```

### Log output
```
java.util.ConcurrentModificationException: null
	at java.base/java.util.ArrayList$Itr.checkForComodification(ArrayList.java:1096)
	at java.base/java.util.ArrayList$Itr.next(ArrayList.java:1050)
	at TRANSFORMER/architectury@13.0.8/dev.architectury.event.EventFactory$1.handleInvocation(EventFactory.java:61)
	at MC-BOOTSTRAP/com.google.common@32.1.2-jre/com.google.common.reflect.AbstractInvocationHandler.invoke(AbstractInvocationHandler.java:87)
	at TRANSFORMER/jdk.proxy4/jdk.proxy4.$Proxy203.tick(Unknown Source)
	at TRANSFORMER/architectury@13.0.8/dev.architectury.event.forge.EventHandlerImplClient.event(EventHandlerImplClient.java:61)
	at MC-BOOTSTRAP/net.neoforged.bus/net.neoforged.bus.EventBus.post(EventBus.java:360)
	at TRANSFORMER/neoforge@21.1.220/net.neoforged.neoforge.client.ClientHooks.fireClientTickPost(ClientHooks.java:1077)
	at TRANSFORMER/minecraft@1.21.1/net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.tick(Minecraft.java:1915)
```

### Minecraft Version
1.21.1

### Iris Version
iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1

### Sodium Version
N/A (using Embeddium 1.0.15)

### Operating System
Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

### Mod Loader
NeoForge 21.1.220

### Mod Loader Version
21.1.220

### Additional context
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
- Crash occurred after system reboot (possibly driver state related)
- monocle mod (monocle-mod-file.jar v0.2.3.ms) injects MixinClientHooks
- Full crash report: https://pastebin.com/raw/cbb7f636 (if needed)

The issue appears to be a race condition where event listeners are modified during iteration when shaders are active.

Please describe.** Block display entities are rendered like entities instead of blocks, which means for emissive blocks, they appear dimmer than the real blocks. **Describe the solution you'd like** Perhaps either render block_display entities the same way as blocks and block entities, or maybe pass block_state data to shaders so they can handle it themselves. **Describe alternatives you've considered** I've tried with a few different shaderpacks to see if any of them have the block_display entity render the same as the real block, but none do. issues.title: Iris breaks emissive Bumblezone entities at certain camera angles and player positions when shaders are turned on [1.20.1, 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge]
issues.body: ### What happened? In my [Bumblezone mod](https://legacy.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/the-bumblezone-forge), my Purple Spike, Electric Ring, and Cosmic Crystal's laser all use these 2 rendertypes https://github.com/TelepathicGrunt/Bumblezone/blob/e88be880a5e7a3654903140b445e6d5e2fde6487/common/src/main/java/com/telepathicgrunt/the_bumblezone/client/BumblezoneClient.java#L110-L144 The issue is when running Iris (or Oculus for that matter) and have a shader applied (any shader), the above entities will randomly go pitch black when viewed at certain camera angles and player positions. The problematic angles/player positions are narrow. And it doesn't matter where the problematic entities are one player is at the broken angle + position, all the visible entities are affected on screen at the exact time. Otherwise, outside those narrow looking angles and player positions, the entities look fine. I suspect the bug is within Iris itself as I lack the ability to debug this further as it is quite odd. Easiest reproduction step is to put on Iris, a shader, and Bumblezone. Then run this command `/bumblezone_modify_data is_bee_essenced @s true` and then `/setblock ~ ~ ~ the_bumblezone:essence_block_yellow`. And then try viewing that ring entity in the arena from various angles until you find the very specific broken angle. It seems more likely to happen when in the arenas than outside it but I had seen the ring entity broken once in overworld underground outside of arena. I have found the issue on Iris for 1.21.1 Fabric/NeoForge and on 1.20.1 Fabric. Even Oculus on 1.20.1 Forge is affected. Doesn't matter what shader is used. As long as shader flow is activated, the bug can happen. (I tried Complementary, Proton, and a bunch others) I did not have any `_e` or `_s` file for the entity textures. Linking my bug report here: https://github.com/TelepathicGrunt/Bumblezone/issues/550 ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26171788/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? 4090 Super (Laptop version) ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Panini Projection Support

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Rectilinear Projection has really annoying and frankly ugly distortion.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I basically want either an option from iris itself or support for shader packs to implement proper Panini Projection.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I have tried to contact other mod developers and shader pack creators, and searched for mods but they're either not for 1.20.1 fabric or don't exist properly.

**Additional context**
I think it's really good if iris had the option for panini since it would help push for a world without rectilinear distortion.


below is an example for Panini Projection, where you can clearly notice the distortion and depth perception being fixed at high FOVs which Minecraft could really benefit from since speed potions and sprinting can result alot of distortion in vanilla.


![243ab65f-b1ef-4a6c-b52f-6ac3c2395e98(1).png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbf66149-b2ae-41a8-80a6-fd5d9d66a421)

issues.title: Intel Arc shader rendering errors (GBuffer/shadow/composite issues)
issues.body: ### What happened? Hello, I'm testing Minecraft shaders on an Intel Arc B580 GPU and I'm seeing consistent rendering issues across multiple shader packs. Shaders affected include: SEUS PTGI IterationT Wisdom Derivative AstraLex Typical problems include: GBuffer errors (gbuffers_skytextured, gbuffers_textured) Shadow pass errors Composite pass errors Broken lighting Missing sky in The End dimension OpenGL Error 1282 The same shaders work correctly on an NVIDIA RTX 2060 using the same Minecraft versions and settings. Iris fixes some texture glitches like the sky in the end dimension, but brings different issues, like overworld and nether is completely white Intel support suggested contacting shader or mod developers to help identify whether this is a driver-level OpenGL issue. Do these symptoms look like a known Intel Arc OpenGL driver problem? I've provided screenshots, and the problem can be reproduced. My email - cleotheedgecraft@gmail.com ### Screenshots ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version Multiple versions, tested on including 1.21.11, 1.21.10 and 1.21.4 with optifine, iris and sodium ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.8.8+mc1.21.4 and iris-fabric-1.10.6+mc1.21.11 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? I didn't contact you on Discord because, well, I don't have that. But please reach me on my e-mail Address :

issues.body: ### What happened? when using a shader that does not have a deferred shader pass, the game will log opengl errors with `No active program` when rendering a player with a translucent block in the hand using this shaderpack it is easy to reproduce, just hold a stained glass block in 3rd person and disable the `DEFERRED` setting in the shaderpack options [deferred.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25348438/deferred.zip) ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25348426/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.11 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.10.5+mc1.21.11.jar ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia RTX 4080, driver 572.42 ### Additional context _No response_
