issues.title: Resizing game window causes FPS to be ~halved
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Iris installed, resizing the game window after a world is loaded causes FPS to be halved. For instance, loading a world with the window maximized, downsizing it to the "default" window size (or any other size), and then maximizing it again causes FPS to be ~half of what it was. Also, loading the world in the "default" window size, then maximizing the window causes FPS to be ~half of what it would be had the world been loaded with the window already maximized.

This behavior persists even if you quit to title and reload the world in a maximized window, the only way to "clear" it is to restart the game.

This behavior occurs with just Iris and Sodium installed.

*Ensuring that the game window either **launches maximized or is maximized before the main menu is reached prevents the bug from occurring**, allowing to to resize the game window at-will while in a world without causing FPS loss. It is not sufficient to simply ensure that the game window is maximized before loading the world.*

### Screenshots

[I keep getting failed to upload when I try to attach a screenshot, but I have two if anyone knows how to get this to work]

### Log output

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25294153/latest.log)
[debug.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25294154/debug.log)

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 1.21.1

### Iris Version

iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia RTX 4070 Ti

### Additional context

Of note, certain mods (KubeJS most notably) will cause this bug to occur even if the game window is never resized while a world is loaded, but this can be preempted by ensuring the game window is maximized prior to the main menu being reached as discussed above.

issues.title: Flip issue with colortex containing raw textures
issues.body:
### What happened?

In [this commit](https://github.com/GeForceLegend/Sundial-Lite/commit/c9eb6160d431c74a3777ee3feec97b35a3b4652e), I added atmosphere trasmittance LUT for Sundial Lite, using some flip to get it available through colortex7 while avoid affecting TAA after. This works well on Optifine, however, after the manually flip, Iris still feed colortex7 with that LUT, causing TAA completely broken.

This is what I do:
1. `flip.composite_pre.colortex7 = true`
2. `texture.composite.colortex7 = textures/AtmosphereTransmittance.bin TEXTURE_2D RGB16 256 256 RGB UNSIGNED_SHORT`
3. `flip.composite5.colortex7 = true`

We expect, and in Optifine it is, composite - compisite5 will get the transmittance LUT through colortex7, and after composite6, colortex7 will turns normal (TAA color and previous water depth). But in Iris, as described above, we still get the LUT from colortex7 even after composite6.

This issue is exclusive on raw texture. Removing attach colortex7 with the LUT, or even just replace the LUT with `texture.composite.colortex7 = minecraft:textures/atlas/blocks.png`, TAA will still working right.

### What happened?

I want to ask if it is possible to map
- `ModelViewMat` of `ChunkSection` Uniform to `ModelViewMat` of `DynamicTransforms` Uniform

`ChunkPosition` is an ivec3, not a vec3 like `ModelOffset`, but it represents a `BlockPos`, not `SectionPos`, so it should be compatible with `ModelOffset`.

I don't know how `TextureSize` of the `ChunkSection` Uniform can be handled, or if that uniform is relevant with regards to Iris shaders.

issues.title: Dimension types now indicated by skybox and cardinal_light, not effects
issues.body:
### What happened?

## My issue

Using a Multiverse-core PaperMC server, my nether-type levels/worlds trigger the overworld shaders instead of nether shaders Complementary Shaders running in Iris. (1.21.11, 25w45a, with the Fabulously Optimised modpack through Modrinth, which relies on Iris + Sodium)

## The problem, I think

The Iris code for NamespacedId [here](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/11e691d94343a6e372affc1a80a0a1f06d6378ff/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/Iris.java#L623) checks the removed `effects` field to guess at the shader to use, rather than the new `skybox` and `cardinal_light`. The `effects` field for dimension types has been [removed](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Dimension_type) as of 1.21.11 (25w45a) in favour of `skybox` and `cardinal_light`.

## Temporary solution

One can customise the `dimension.properties` in the client's shaderpack to explicitly list the levels. I don't think this is a good permanent solution because servers cannot distribute hints to a particular shader.  (Hint to inexperienced people like me, all lowercase seems to be expected in `dimension.properties` and altering your shaders in the client seems to revert the client to built-in shaders until you select your altered shader.)

## My suggested fix, use skybox and cardinal_light

I think the Iris method for NamespacedId above should check `skybox` and `cardinal_light` instead of `effects`.  I think it should check both so that it doesn't accidentally recognise some other sort of custom dimension and makes the best guess possible based on the information it can get.

Perhaps it should check `effects` still too for backwards compatibility.

## Another possible fix, refactor for wildcards

I briefly thought `dimension.properties` [supported wildcards](https://github.com/ComplementaryDevelopment/ComplementaryReimagined/issues/272#event-22239360573). But it does not. I'm not sure if this would be a better approach, because it would require shader developers to tweak their `dimension.properties` to represent the current consensus on naming style, which may change.


I hope this report is helpful.

Respectfully submitted,

issues.title: [1.21.6] Extreme FPS drop (2-3 fps) when GUI is hidden with HDR enabled, and in shader settings menu regardless of HDR
issues.body:
### What happened?


When using Iris 1.9.6 with shaders enabled on Minecraft 1.21.6, pressing F1 to hide the GUI causes the frame rate to drop from normal (e.g., 60+ fps) to an unplayable 2-3 fps. This occurs only when the screen is completely devoid of any GUI elements.

The critical clue: The moment any GUI is opened (inventory E, pause menu ESC, or even the shader selection screen), the frame rate instantly returns to normal. Closing the GUI returns the game to the 2-3 fps state.

Furthermore, opening the shader settings/configuration menu (where individual shader options are tuned) also triggers the same severe lag, even with Windows HDR turned off.

System Information
Minecraft Version: 1.21.6

Fabric Loader: 0.18.1

Iris Version: 1.9.6+mc1.21.8

Sodium Version: 0.7.3+mc1.21.8

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti

GPU Driver: 591.74

OS: Windows 11

Display Mode: The primary issue occurs with Windows HDR enabled. Hiding GUI with HDR off does not cause the lag, but the shader settings menu lag persists.

Steps to Reproduce
Ensure Windows HDR is ON.

Launch Minecraft with a minimal mod set: Fabric Loader, Fabric API, Sodium, Iris.

Enable any shader pack (tested with BSL_v10.1.zip and ComplementaryReimagined_r5.1.1.zip).

Join a world. Frame rate should be normal.

Press F1 to hide the entire GUI.

Observed: FPS immediately drops to 2-3.

Press E to open the inventory.

Observed: FPS immediately returns to normal.

Close the inventory (E). FPS drops back to 2-3.

(Additional test) With HDR ON or OFF, open the shader configuration menu (Video Settings > Shader Packs > [Shader Pack] > Settings).

Observed: Severe lag (2-3 fps) occurs within the settings menu itself.

What I've Already Tried / Exclusion List
✅ Updated NVIDIA graphics driver to the latest (591.74).

✅ Used completely different, well-maintained shader packs (BSL, Complementary). The issue is not shader-specific.

✅ Created a pristine Minecraft instance with only Fabric API, Sodium, and Iris. The issue persists, ruling out conflicts with other mods.

✅ Confirmed the GPU is being fully utilized (not stuck on idle clocks).

❌ The issue is not present when shaders are completely disabled ((off)).

Hypothesis / Additional Context
The problem appears to be tied to a specific rendering path within Iris. The "world-only" render path (no GUI) seems to have a critical performance bug or infinite wait state under HDR. The "GUI composite" render path (which is also used by the shader settings menu) inadvertently bypasses this bug, restoring performance.

The fact that the shader settings menu lags even without HDR suggests the issue might be related to how Iris handles its own configuration interface's render targets, which could share a faulty code path with the HDR + no-GUI scene rendering.

Request
Could the developers please investigate the rendering pipeline difference between "fullscreen world rendering" and "GUI-over-world composite rendering"? The switch between these two states (triggered by F1) is where the catastrophic performance difference manifests.

Thank you for your work on Iris. I hope this detailed report is helpful.

issues.title: Add: Custom UBO (ChunkFix) support for MaLiLib/Litematica (1.21.11+)

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Rendering with Shaders ON using the custom `legacy_terrain` core shader works, but the textures are showing in Low Resolution due to the Texture Atlas Size problem.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Adding support for the MaLiLib's Custom Patch UBO called `ChunkFix` which is designed as a replacement for the Vanilla `ChunkSections` UBO; which injects the `Texture Atlas Height, Width` (ivec2), the `chunkVisibility` param (float), the `RGSS` config status (boolean int -- 0 or 1), and the `Iris Shader Status` (boolean int -- 0 or 1) for use in the Custom Core Shader.

Also, Iris does not properly support the Vanilla `ChunkSections` UBO itself when used in mods for Vanilla rendering compatibility.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Checking to see if Iris supports it in the updated releases.
- Listening to advice on how to better modify my custom terrain core shader.
- Telling users to not use Shaders while using Litematica's rendering features.

**Additional context**

In order to get this good of a result, I had to force Litematica to continue using the `DynamicUniforms` UBO for Chunk Batching instead of the `ChunkSections` UBO.  This is because users demand to have the `renderBlocksAsTranslucent` to be functional in the MOD, and it cannot work with the 1.21.11 Vanilla Terrain Core Shader.  This is because they removed the `ColorModulator` Parameter, which is required for this feature to work.  Also, Iris' Chunk Offset calculations do not work using the Vanilla `ChunkSections` UBO alone without other adjustments and modifications while Shaders are ON.


[legacy_terrain.fsh](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/malilib/blob/fc917907d874bf8196e41f5f94bd8794cafad89c/src/main/resources/assets/malilib/shaders/legacy_terrain.fsh)

[ChunkFixUniform.java](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/malilib/blob/fc917907d874bf8196e41f5f94bd8794cafad89c/src/main/java/fi/dy/masa/malilib/render/uniform/ChunkFixUniform.java)

[Example commented out code using Vanilla `ChunkSections` UBO where it doesn't work with Iris Shaders ON](https://github.com/sakura-ryoko/litematica/blob/304d16ada2ea495978dca5e0d810e9e7e8f7a338/src/main/java/fi/dy/masa/litematica/render/schematic/WorldRendererSchematic.java#L712)

When texture filtering is set to anisotropic before turning on shaders, it disables/breaks a specific feature in Complementary shaders, which is the "World-Space Reflections", upon enabling anisotropic, this option stops working. issues.title: No mod-accessible hook for final composited color buffer (post-shader)
issues.body:
In vanilla Minecraft, reading the main framebuffer during WorldRenderEvents.LAST works because the framebuffer contains the final image.

Under Iris, the final color output exists only transiently during shader passes, and the main framebuffer is cleared or reused afterward.

This makes it impossible for mods to:
- Capture the final lit scene
- Implement scopes, mirrors, picture-in-picture, or post effects
- RenderDoc confirms that the final composite pass is not accessible via public API.

**Request:**
Is there an intended way for mods to access the final composited color texture, or a post-shader render hook?

If not, would Iris consider exposing a stable capture hook?

Repro steps
1. Install Fabric + Iris
2. Enable any shader pack
3. Mod listens to WorldRenderEvents.LAST
4. Copies MinecraftClient.getInstance().getFramebuffer().getColorAttachment()
5. Resulting texture is black or invalid

issues.title: Bending from the Emotecraft mod does not work.
issues.body: ### What happened? The problem is that the flexion of the limbs does not work in the emotions of emoticraft. I know that the problem lies in the Sodium mod, and more specifically in the configs "features.render.entity.CuboidMixin" and "features.render.entity.ModelPartMixin". But! If you remove these configs, the problem will not be fixed. Iris will inherit these configs in the file "mixins.iris.compat.sodium.json", specifically in the lines: ` "copyEntity.CuboidMixin", "copyEntity.ModelPartMixin", ` If you delete them from this file, the problem disappears without affecting performance in any way. At least that's how I noticed it. ### Screenshots Animation before the fix. Animation after the fix. ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 1.20.4 ### Iris Version 1.7.2+mc1.20.4 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? GeForce RTX 4050 Mobile ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: [Performance] Severe FPS drop in 1.21.5+ caused by HorizonRenderer vertex format mismatch with RenderPass
issues.body: ### What happened? Since Minecraft 1.21.5, there has been a significant performance degradation when using Iris. After investigation, I've traced the root cause to an inefficient rendering mode in HorizonRenderer.java. The issue stems from a mismatch between the generated vertex primitive type (QUADS) and the format expected by Minecraft's new RenderPass system for the sky pipeline (RenderPipelines.SKY), which is TRIANGLE_FAN. It effectively tripling the number of primitives to be rendered. On my hardware, this single draw call takes up to 9ms, reducing my framerate to around 30 FPS. ### Screenshots 1.21.4: 1.21.5: ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version ≥Minecraft 1.21.5 ### Iris Version ≥1.8.8 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 3GB ### Additional context _No response_

issues.body: ### What happened? This bug report was originally written for Sodium and copied over here, I'm not sure if it's already been reported cause I don't know what any of the words in all these issues mean <3 ### Bug Description Since Sodium 0.7.0 or later + Iris 1.9.2 or later, a bug is present causing incorrect normal orientation on log blocks. Shown here are screenshots of the Bliss shaderpack, with and without normal debug view enabled: ### Screenshots Correct behaviour (or what looks like it) is exhibited in Sodium version 0.6.13 paired with Iris 1.9.1: The resource pack used for testing is attached: [sodium normals bug demo pack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23302375/sodium.normals.bug.demo.pack.zip) ### Reproduction Steps 1. In an instance with a 0.7.x version of Sodium and a compatible version of Iris, enable the provided resourcepack and a shaderpack supporting normal maps 2. Observe incorrect behaviour ### Log File These logs were from a few months ago on slightly older versions, but the bug persists in the most current mod versions and game version. Iris 1.20.1 reverses the order of Vertex Buffers Rendering
issues.body: ### What happened? I'm running 1.20.1 Fabric, and the only mod I have loaded is a custom one I'm working on called WAY. I'm using the Fabric Render Event to draw 2 textures with no depth testing in the world. It renders fine without Iris, but when Iris is present, the order of which it chooses to render them is reversed (it will render the one called last first). Iris also seems to render Water and other Transparent Geometry after these render, which shouldn't be possible as my mod is using WorldRenderEvents.LAST, which should render after those Intended Behavior Unintended Behavior Here's links to Render Captures, one with and one without Iris: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LA6URnB2kSi-T6TeN1VwDNlHAieAmxb_?usp=sharing ### Screenshots _No response_ ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 1.20.1 ### Iris Version 1.7.6 ### Operating System Linux Mint ### What is your GPU? issues.title: Iris with Distant Horizons causes incorrect ftransform() for transparent blocks
issues.body: ### What happened? Expected behaviour: in shadow.vsh, the ftransform() works for solid and transparent blocks alike to transform them from world into shadow coordinates. Observed behaviour: Liquids have a slightly wrong projection matrices and shadows do not match up with world. Steps to reproduce: - Install Iris and DH. - Used shaderpack: https://gitlab.ampericus.net/ampericus/ampishade/-/tree/bugreport/ (Shaderpack displays shadow texture to screen, bugged behaviour visible when toggling DH rendering on/off) ### Screenshots Normal behaviour (DH disabled): Bugged behaviour (DH enabled): ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 1.21.10 ### Iris Version iris-1.9.6+1.21.10-fabric ### Operating System uname -a: Linux [HOSTNAME] 6.14.2-1-default #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Apr 14 06:14:46 UTC 2025 (5512154) x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux ### What is your GPU? NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060, driver version 570.144 ### Additional context I tried multiple, well known shaderpacks to see if I am just bad at creating a shaderpack, but Noble , Sildur's Vibrant and Bliss all share this behaviour which leads me to believe that Iris (or Distant Horizons, but they don't have a public issue tracker) is at fault here.

issues.body: ### What happened? About 30% of the time joining a server, I get the attached screenshot for a result. That was using Bliss shader, but a similar issue occurs on MakeUp-UltraFast... what both issues have in common is that the sky fails to load in one manner or another. Since it's multiple shaders and just on multiplayer I wonder if the issue is in Iris. Singleplayer always works. The server in question is one I set up myself with no notable mods besides Distant Horizons. Reloading shaders fixes it every time, and I can reload dozens of times and it doesn't break, so the scope of the issue is only when joining a server, not just the fact of being inside of a server. I would settle for some kind of mod solution that automatically reloads shaders after they initialize the first time, but I couldn't find any such mod. issues.title: Auto switch shader when switch dimmension.

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Yes.
When switching between dimensions (for example: Overworld → Nether → The End), the shader currently stays the same.
This can cause visual inconsistency — for example, using a bright shader in the Nether makes everything hard to see, or an atmospheric shader in The End looks too dark in Overworld.
**Describe the solution you'd like**
An option or built-in logic that automatically changes the active shader depending on the current dimension.
For example:
Overworld → use “Complementary Reimagined”
Nether → use “BSL”
The End → use “Sildur Vibrant”
It could be configured via a small JSON or config file like:
***{
  "overworld": "shaders/complementary.zip",
  "the_nether": "shaders/bsl.zip",
  "the_end": "shaders/sildur.zip"
}***

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually opening the shader menu each time (tedious).
Using resource packs per dimension (not flexible).
Writing an external script to detect dimension change (possible, but hacky and not user-friendly).
**Additional context**
This feature would improve immersion and convenience for players using cinematic or realistic shaders per biome/dimension.
It could also be useful for content creators or benchmarkers who switch dimensions frequently.

issues.title: Transparency and flickering issues with custom 3D items (Ender Pearl, water bucket) in latest Iris build
issues.body: ### What happened? ### Description After the latest Iris update for Minecraft 1.21.8 (Fabric 0.17.2), transparent 3D items started rendering incorrectly. This happens even on a clean installation with only Iris, Sodium, and a resource pack that adds custom 3D models (Tools and Utilities). Examples: - Ender Pearl model has missing inner faces and flickering transparency. - Water bucket becomes partially transparent, making the back side of the bucket appear like glass. The issue **does not occur** on the previous Iris + Sodium builds (tested both available versions). When rolling back to the older build, all transparency and models render correctly again. ### Additional Notes - Minecraft: 1.21.8 - Fabric Loader: 0.17.2 - Resource pack: Tools and Utilities (adds custom 3D items) - Tested on multiple PCs, same behavior. - Some shaders (like UShader) do **not** lag or show the issue, but most others do. - The problem appears even on a clean profile, so it’s not caused by config or cache. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Install Minecraft 1.21.8 + Fabric 0.17.2 2. Add Iris + Sodium (latest builds) 3. Add resource pack “Tools and Utilities” 4. Equip or view an Ender Pearl or Water Bucket in hand 5. Observe incorrect transparency and flickering. ### Expected Behavior Custom 3D items should render correctly, like in previous Iris builds (no transparency glitches or flicker). ### Suspected Cause Likely related to recent changes in the translucent item layer or alpha blending/depth pass handling introduced in the latest Iris version. ### Screenshots ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version 1.21.8 ### Iris Version 1.9.2+1.21.8-fabric ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? issues.title: Unnecessary double UI rendering and blur with radius 0
issues.body: ### What happened? There are two issues: #### 1 The UI elements (all sprites, texts) in the shader pack configuration screen are rendered twice in total, with both draw calls being identical. This wastes GPU performance and should only be rendered once. #### 2 The MenuBlurRadius passed to global uniforms is 0 when the shader pack screen is opened, via a mixin. https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/07c59f3158e3b69b85354848f162952a307bb96e/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/mixin/MixinGameRenderer.java#L64-L71 Meanwhile, `Screen.renderBlurredBackground` is still calling `GuiGraphics.blurBeforeThisStratum`, which causes the UI rendering to run **six render passes**. All of these passes merely linearly sample the input texture and output it—effectively doing nothing—wasting a lot of GPU performance. You should **override `renderBlurredBackground` in `ShaderPackScreen`** to disable blur in specific cases, rather than hacking it by setting the radius to 0 (0 is not a valid value for the blur shader and causes compatibility issues). ### Screenshots 1. Two identical draw calls. 2. Because the radius is 0, the blur shader—which can be overridden by resource packs—may produce black output. ### Log output _No response_ ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.8 ### Iris Version Iris 1.9.1+mc1.21.7 ### Operating System Windows 11 ### What is your GPU? RTX 3070 ### Additional context This issue is not specific to any operating system or GPU.

issues.title: Iris + ImmediatelyFast + GeckoLib armours + JEI + Glow effect on mobs = Frequent crashes, especially when opening inventory
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Iris Version

iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1

### Sodium Version

sodium-neoforge-0.6.13+mc1.21.1

### Operating System

Windows 10, 11, Ubuntu 24.04.1

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA RTX 4090, RTX 4060, AMD RX 7900 XTX, various others

### Java Version

Java 21 (e.g. Adoptium, GraalVM, ranging from 21.0.4 to 21.0.7)

### Reproduction Steps

1) Create new world (with commands on)
2) Give yourself the following:
- A minecraft chest (`minecraft:chest`) and place it down
- A Lightbringer Chestplate (`irons_spellbooks:paladin_chestplate`) and equip it
- A Shadow-Walker Leggings (`irons_spellbooks:shadowwalker_leggings`) and equip it
- A Spectral Eye Amulet (`forbidden_arcanus:spectral_eye_amulet`), make sure to look towards a direction with glowing mobs on screen and keep facing those for rest of the process
3) Open chest and put the Spectral Eye Amulet into it, close chest
4) Wait about 3-5 minutes
5) Open chest, grab Spectral Eye Amulet to inventory (e.g. shift click it), close chest, and open Inventory

### Crash Report file and latest.log

As it's a JVM crash, no crash-report is produced.
Here's one hs_err_pid log from such a crash: https://mclo.gs/rSHuwjb

While latest + debug logs abruptly end, here they are just in case: [latest.log](https://mclo.gs/mRZfUV5) and [debug.log](https://mclo.gs/FGHvulA)

### Additional context

This is reproduced in a minimal instance in MC 1.21.1 using NeoForge 21.1.209, with an as narrowed down as possible modlist.
#### Mods list
```
curios-neoforge-9.5.1+1.21.1 (iron's dependency)
forbidden_arcanus-2.6.1 (source of global mob glow effect)
geckolib-neoforge-1.21.1-4.8
ImmediatelyFast-NeoForge-1.6.6+1.21.1
iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1
irons_spellbooks-1.21.1-3.14.3 (contains armour sets that use geckolib)
jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.22.1.316
player-animation-lib-forge-2.0.1+1.21.1 (iron's dependency)
sodium-neoforge-0.6.13+mc1.21.1 (iris dependency)
valhelsia_core-neoforge-1.21.1-1.1.5 (forbidden arcanus dependency)
```

#### Mods list explanation
While the core mods that when disabled make the crash go away are Geckolib + some Geckolib armour set + Iris + ImmediatelyFast + JEI, the other mods in that list make reproduction *much* more convenient and quicker (reproduction within minutes instead of potentially hours).

For Geckolib, some mod that actually provides armours using Geckolib is needed. I've chosen Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks for this, but this issue has occurred with armours from Advanced AE2 (quantum suit) and Ars Nouveau too. Numerous armour sets can all cause this issue, but for this I've chosen a Lightbringer Chestplate (`irons_spellbooks:paladin_chestplate`) and Shadow-Walker Leggings (`irons_spellbooks:shadowwalker_leggings`). These have to simply be worn, nothing else necessary.

Forbidden Arcanus provides a Spectral Eye Amulet which when anywhere in inventory gives all mobs the glowing effect that's also needed to cause this issue - this mod is just a convenient way to get this, it's been reproduced by other methods giving such a glowing effect like RFTools' Environmental Controller, or even with just a `/effect give @e[type=!player] minecraft:glowing 5` command but that one is *very* finicky at reproducing this).

This issue was originally encountered by many players across several popular modpacks from among others FTB and ATM. Here's my original report when encountering this issue in FTB Evolution: https://github.com/FTBTeam/FTB-Modpack-Issues/issues/9046
Some of the included logs over there, especially the one from lupusagax' reproduction, contain a much richer hs_err_pid file with a far more explicit stacktrace as he's on Linux/Ubuntu.
In that modpack, Embeddium + Monocle + Iris combo is present, but I could also reproduce it when replacing those with Sodium + Iris, and then I went on further narrowing it down until I got to this minimal modlist in this report that can still recreate the issue.

If any of the GeckoLib armours are not worn, or any of Iris / ImmediatelyFast / JEI mods are not enabled, or no mob glow effect is present, the issue cannot be reproduced anymore. There's multiple ways this can occur during gameplay, my reproduction steps involved here just seem to be one of the fastest and most consistent ways to get to the same issue and crash.

One of the more recent issue reports involving this on ATM10: https://github.com/AllTheMods/ATM-10/issues/3439

Report on ImmediatelyFast's side: https://github.com/RaphiMC/ImmediatelyFast/issues/421

issues.title: Mekanism Energy Cube floating core visual glitch w. shaders
issues.body: ### What happened? The issue pertains to a group of blocks from the mod Mekanism. I already reported it to their GitHub (ticket #8477), but they pointed to Iris Shaders as the cause. When using most shaders (such as BSL), the floating core of the Energy Cube from Mekanism will produce a glitched shadow on the ground depending on the angle of the sun, and it follows the player along the north-south axis in discrete steps, even at great distance. (See screenshot). This happens only when the cube contains energy and thus glows slightly. The issue does not seem particular to any version of NeoForge, Iris Shaders or Mekanism. Results may vary, however, with the kind of shader pack installed: - Bliss: Black, faint and blurry. - BSL: Colored with very clear detail. - Complementary Unbound: Does not appear. - IterationT: Brightly colored, but blurry. - MakeUp - Ultra Fast: Black color, blurry. Disabling entity shadows in the shader settings (or using a shader that lacks entity shadows) "fixes" the issue. ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22321200/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1 ### Operating System Windows 10 ### What is your GPU? issues.title: Shader won't load
Add an attribute for local (non-atlas) UVs and texture sizes of individual blocks

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Problem:
Currently, it is not possible to create certain effects that map directly to the pixels of a texture. *Ordinarily* this would be what UVs are for, coupled with the use of something like `textureSize()` or the `atlasSize` uniform, however these are not generally applicable (i.e. some textures may not be atlased, it is unsafe to assume that all textures are 16x16 pixels or even the same resolution across the entire pack).

## Personal motivation:
I'm working on the Rain World in Minecraft project. There is an effect called "grime" that needs to be overlayed conditionally onto blocks based on information in their texture. Alongside this, being mapped to a noise texture, it needs to be affected by the UVs of the block. Ordinarily, this is aligned to each pixel on the original texture so that it all lines up and looks good. 

Without this feature, it is currently impossible for me to replicate 1:1 without distortion or scaling problems on some custom models.

## Proposed solution:
I suggest implementing a new vertex attribute to store local/non-atlased UV (xy) and specific texture resolution (zw).

issues.title: Add a loading bar for shader compilation

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

 With larger packs, shader compile times can be several seconds or even longer. Iris holds up the game during shader compilation, which isn't a big deal for small packs, but is really bad UX for big shader packs.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a loading bar to track the progress of shader compilation, perhaps with little detail text on top like the world generation screen (e.g. `Compiling world0/gbuffers_terrain.fsh`) or something above. This was mentioned in in #1646 but I think it ought to have a dedicated issue.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

If shader compilation does become fast enough (see #1646 again), then it might not be so necessary to have a loading bar. In addition, you *can* see compile warnings pop up in the logs, but that's not helpful for tracking progress.

issues.title: Shader called “none” enabled by default
issues.body:
### What happened?

Like the title, when loading up iris for the first time, shaders are by default enabled. Even if no shaders exist. This is problematic, as it prevents users from changing their graphics settings to “fabulous”
This is fine, except that even without shaders you can’t change this. You can’t disable shaders either if you have no shader packs. You have to use the keybind, where it says “disabled shaders” and 
“Enabled shaders ‘none’”

To replicate, load up iris on an instance where it hasn’t been used. You will not be able to enable “fabulous” until you press K

issues.title: Significant Performance Drop with Shaders in 1.21.4+ Compared to 1.21.1
issues.body:
The same shader performs vastly differently between Minecraft versions below 1.21.4 and versions 1.21.4 or higher. A shader that runs at a stable 110-130 FPS in 1.21.1 drops to around 70 FPS in 1.21.4 and above. I've tested multiple shaders, and this performance decrease is **not an isolated case**—it happens consistently across different shaders.
RTX 4060 laptop

Rendersystem called from wrong thread is the error seen


net.irisshaders.iris.pathways.HandRenderer (a component of Iris Shaders) is attempting to perform a rendering operation.

It's doing this on a "Worker-ResourceReload-1" thread, which is incorrect. Minecraft's rendering API (RenderSystem) explicitly states that rendering operations must occur on the "Render thread."

Because this rule is violated, it throws an IllegalStateException and crashes the game.

issues.title: Mac Silicon Particles Blurry
issues.body: ### What happened? Under certain conditions, particles display extremely blurry / with incorrect resolution. I ran minecraft with only Iris, Sodium, and Complementary shaders on mac m4 silicon. I joined a world, turned on shaders, placed down a torch, and particles were fine. I then run `/weather rain`. The torch particles end up blurry and F3+T does not fix them. All particles (like rain splash effects, hearts from breeding, or bubbles) also remain extremely blurry. The only way to fix the problem is to wait for weather to clear (or run `/weather clear`), wait a few seconds, and then F3+T fixes the issue. However, during rain or thunder weather all particles are very blurry. Disabling shaders does not fix the problem, but running F3+T after disabling shaders fixes the issue (even while it is raining). Note: the /weather rain can be run in a desert biome as well (where no rain actually occurs) and still results in all particles becoming blurry. Issue occurs with other shaders that successfully run on mac (like Makeup Ultra Fast), which suggests it is not a shader problem. This seems somewhat similar to another issue (https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1776) related to Botania, and an oculus issue (https://github.com/Asek3/Oculus/issues/267). ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21304349/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar ### Operating System Mac Silicon M4 ### What is your GPU? integrated GPU ### Additional context _No response_

issues.title: Loading time for shader increases significantly when (performance) settings are not default
issues.body:
### What happened?

Versions:
- Minecraft 1.12.1
- Shader Complementary Reimagined r5.5.1
- Shader BSL v10.0
- Iris v1.8.12-snapshot+mc1.21.1-local
- NeoForge v21.1.191
- LWJGL v3.3.3\

I was trying to test out new settings for Complementary Reimagined when I noticed loading times between settings being applied was taking longer and longer. I decided to test comparing loading time with a completely fresh copy of Complementary, and discovered that changing at least one performance setting from its default value results in significantly longer loading time.

Complementary on purely default settings (performance set to High (Default)) takes ~0.5 seconds to load, pretty much instant.

But, with Advanced Coloured Lighting changed from Off to 4 chunks (all other settings are default), it takes ~20 seconds. This isn't as big of a deal when there's no settings to be changed, but if I'm tweaking settings a lot to figure out what looks the nicest, it can get very annoying very quickly.

I tested changing various settings, and found increased load times for Complementary when changing the following (all other settings left at defaults per-case):

- Real-Time Shadows to any non-default, even if lower than default or OFF. (Default is Medium).
- Light Shaft Quality any non-default, even OFF (Default is Medium).
- Detail Quality to any non-default, even if lower than default (Default is Medium).
- Water Reflection Quality to any non-default, even OFF (Default is Medium).
- Advanced Colored Lighting to any non-default (Default is OFF).
- Shadow Distance to any non-default, even if lower than default (Default is 12 Chunks).
- Entity Shadows to ON (Default is OFF).
- Cloud Quality to OFF (anything that isn't OFF loads about the same as the default Medium).
- Block Reflection Quality to any non-default, even OFF (Default is High).
- Texture Filtering to non-default (Default is OFF).

Only setting Anti-Aliasing (FXAA) and Edge Shadow (SSAO) settings do not result in any notable slower loading times when changed from their defaults. I have not tested changing any settings beyond these ones.

I had _initially_ thought this was a Complementary Reimagined issue, but then I tried doing the same to BSL v10.0 and it also had increased load times when performance settings were non-default. So, I believe the issue lies with Iris itself.

I don't know if anyone else has observed this. If it's not something that can be fixed with the shaderpack itself, I'd like to understand what's causing it, to figure out ways to mitigate the problem outside of the shader itself.

issues.title: Incorrect lightmap UV coordinates
issues.body: ### What happened? When using the base-330 template pack, the lighting looks slightly brighter than when no shaders are used. It seems that when shaders are enabled, a value of `0.03125` is added to lmcoord. Subtracting `0.03125` from lmcoord makes the lighting match with vanilla (no shaders). ### Screenshots No shaders: Base-330: Base-330 (when subtracting `0.03125 from lmcoord`): ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21216379/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.6 ### Iris Version iris-fabric-1.9.0+mc1.21.6.jar ### Operating System Windows 10 ### What is your GPU? NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 ### Additional context ```glsl lmcoord = (gl_TextureMatrix[1] * gl_MultiTexCoord1).st - 0.03125; ``` makes the lighting correct

DistantHorizons-2.3.3-b-dev-1.21.7-fabric-neoforge.jar I also tested this on version 1.21.5(fabric) and the issue persists, but since I'm mainly playing on 1.21.7, I'm reporting it for this version. ### Screenshots ### Log output [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21183268/latest.log) ### Minecraft Version Minecraft 1.21.7 ### Iris Version iris-neoforge-1.9.1+mc1.21.7.jar ### Operating System windows 11 ### What is your GPU? AMD RX5700 8G ### Additional context I recorded a video of the issue but can't get it to upload. The bug is easy to reproduce, though: a section of the water surface flickers constantly. I'm not sure if it's a chunk-related problem.

issues.title: `IrisTextVertexSink` uses wrong vertex stride when shaders are disabled
issues.body:
### What happened?

 - Install Sodium, Iris, and ComputerCraft in a fresh instance.
 - Configure Iris with the default settings (i.e. no shaders)
 - Place down a computer and a monitor next to it.
 - Write something to the monitor (e.g. `monitor left paint a`).
 - Observe the monitor is transparent.

This is a similar issue to #2053, but resulting in larger-scale corruption.

### Screenshots

### With shaders
![A screenshot of a ComputerCraft monitor displaying the paint program.](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/assets/4346137/4aefed7e-3768-49bd-93c0-92b22c936cb7)

### Without shaders

![A screenshot of a ComputerCraft monitor displaying the paint program. The monitor is transparent, and random quads are present disappearing into the distance.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0d3a28f-277d-446a-b9cd-8aa7ca5d0cac)

### Log output

https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21021121/logs.txt. See also https://github.com/cc-tweaked/CC-Tweaked/issues/2229

### Minecraft Version

1.27.1

### Iris Version

1.9.1+1.21.7-fabric

### Operating System

Linux, but I've had reports on Windows too.

### What is your GPU?

AMD Ryzen 7 Pro 4750U, confirmed on other GPUs

### Additional context

I sat down with RenderDoc and looked at this.

Inspecting the input of the vertex shader, we can see that when shaders are enabled, the vertices look normal:

![A table showing the vertices to draw. Each column (position, colour, etc...) has a sensible layout.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a89b137-8744-41f7-878c-56fa26041e67)

When shaders are disabled however, the contents are corrupted.

![The same table as before. The first vertex looks normal, but later vertices contain garbage.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44568ef2-55ad-420d-b92d-8171770d11e1)

As far as I can tell, this is because `IrisTextVertexSink` assumes we'll always draw with the `GLYPH` vertex format, setting a stride of 51. However, `RenderPipeline` mixin only uses it when shaders are enabled, so the VBO is configured with a much smaller stride:

https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/2f0bfb7424bf9579bb0331b2ddc1be9060c57457/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/mixin/MixinRenderPipeline.java#L28-L34

```glsl
mat2x3 pixelsToPlayerPos = mat2x3(dFdx(eyePlayerPos), dFdy(eyePlayerPos));
mat2 pixelsToTexCoord = mat2(dFdx(texcoord), dFdy(texcoord));
mat2 texCoordToPixels = inverse(pixelsToTexCoord);

vec3 tangent         = normalize(pixelsToPlayerPos * texCoordToPixels[0]);
vec3 bitangent       = normalize(pixelsToPlayerPos * texCoordToPixels[1]);
```

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When finishing tweaking shader settings, rather than clicking on another settings tab, I have to click on a Done button on the bottom.
The shaders button in Reese's Sodium Options is in the same place as it is without.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like it to be on the column with other Sodium tabs (when Reese's is installed) as well as making Iris settings more consistent with Sodium settings.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not changing the shader selection screen.

**Additional context**
Out of place shaders button

issues.title: Mipmap for shadowtex (shadow depth) isn't working
issues.body:
### What happened?

Iris does read the directives `generateShadowMipmap`, `shadowtex0Mipmap`, etc. And tries to generate mipmap using `glGenerateMipmap`. But it does nothing because the depth textures are created with only 1 mip level.
```glsl
this.mainDepth = RenderSystem.getDevice().createTexture("Shadow Map", TextureFormat.DEPTH32, resolution, resolution, 1);
this.noTranslucents = RenderSystem.getDevice().createTexture("Shadow Map / Opaque", TextureFormat.DEPTH32, resolution, resolution, 1);
```
https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/1.21.5/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/shadows/ShadowRenderTargets.java

This problem still exists in 1.21.6
https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/1.21.6/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/shadows/ShadowRenderTargets.java#L55-L56

issues.title: Broken the setup/clear of RenderType in Iris 1.8.12
issues.body:
### What happened?

Hello, I am the developer of Armourer's Workshop.

in recently some players [report](https://github.com/Armourers-Workshop/Armourers-Workshop/issues/523) that when it using iris 1.8.12, everything rendering is black.

after debugging, I confirmed problem occurs in [this commit](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/commit/b4b2c22c1587264989d746ae57423c32cf6dfcb4).

we have mixin in the `clearRenderState`, and the execute extra rendering logic when `clearRenderState` call, it work perfect.

but the `iris 1.8.12` add a `ImmediateState.mergeRendering` flag, it forced  skip we rendering logic.

https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/b4b2c22c1587264989d746ae57423c32cf6dfcb4/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/batchedentityrendering/impl/FullyBufferedMultiBufferSource.java#L139-L157

https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/b4b2c22c1587264989d746ae57423c32cf6dfcb4/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/mixin/MixinRenderType.java#L12-L23

issues.title: Missing hardcoded refmap file in multiple mixin configs for NeoForge releases
issues.body:
### What happened?

refmap file reference is hardcoded into the mixin json files but no refmap file is provided (in NeoForge release).

If a refmap is not required, and the chosen toolchain doesn't handle dynamic refmap entries, and it is still desirable to hardcode for the unnecessary refmap, then an empty refmap should be provided when refmaps are not needed.

issues.title: [Bug]: Broken player display on inventory if Iris used with Continuity + Any Emissive RP
issues.body:
### What happened?

There is a bug that has been going on for the past few weeks on my instances and I wanted to figure it out, and here I am.

The bug is part of multiple cases.
Being the mods:
1. Sodium 
2. Iris
3. Indium
4. Continuity
5. ANY resource pack that does not even touch any enchant glint related or any tool releated stuff, even glowing ores.

If you join the game with those mods, make sure that Continuity Emissive toggle is ON if you're above Continuity 3.0.0-beta.5+1.20.1, if you are in 3.0.0-beta.4+1.20.1 you will still experience the bug with Emissives OFF after enabling Iris once, while holding an item with an enchantment glint (any resourcepack that doesn't even change them). Even after disabling Iris this issue will be permanently sticked to your instance unless you reboot the game.

Here is how it looks like:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8815067a-add0-4be0-baaf-5f443073e6c2)

I have opened a report in Discord before but it did not mention that many details, now it does though.

The steps to reproduce is basically:
1. Enter the game with said mods and any resourcepack that adds emissives of your choice
3. Toggle ANY shader
4. Hold ANY enchanted item in your hand (Armor, sword, flint and steel, anything you can enchant.)
5. See bug, even after closing the shaders it will be there.
For extra context, it happens ONLY after 0.5.9, so 0.5.11 in my case since Iris doesn't have a release for 0.5.10 of Sodium.

### Minecraft Version

1.20.1 Fabric

### Iris Version

Any, but specifically in this instance there is 1.7.6

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

Sapphire RX 6500 XT

issues.title: Crash with Sneaky Curses
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.5

### Iris Version

1.8.11

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-0.6.13+mc1.21.5.jar

### Operating System

Windows 11

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia GeForce RTX 4080

### Java Version

Modrinth Launcher tells me, it is Java 21, so i guess Java 21

### Reproduction Steps

I want to make clear, that i don't exactly know what is causing this error. This is reproduction for my specific case with the mod "Sneaky Curses" installed.

1. Open a chest with a cursed item in it.
2. Game crashes

### Crash Report file and latest.log

```shell
https://gist.github.com/night2078/170de99552d2be696cac702bd497e551

Please note, that there is no crash log generated, once the game closes / crashes.
This is a log by the modrinth launcher itself, or atleast it is in it's folder.
```

### Additional context

I do not have any crash log for this case. It seems to be some sort of issue related to the way how "Sneaky Curses" applies a red enchantment tint to the item. Opening a chest or even your inventory with such item, instantly closes the game without any crash log or useful information in the latest.log

For this i kindly asked ChatGPT and it told me, that it seems to be an issue with either Iris, Sodium or both together. If i disable Iris, the crash stops and you can see the red enchantment tint on the item, which is why i assume it has something to do with that. Iris works otherwise perfectly for me. The provided crash / error log is from the modrinth launcher itself. There is sadly no crash log generated when the game closes. The log from the game itself also just ends without any error.

issues.title: Iris BREAKS Nametag Color (Gray instead of ...)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Wrong Nametag Color gray instead of vanilla white

Mods:
sodium and iris

### Screenshots

issues.title: Server Compatibility

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]
Many servers use core shaders to create emotes, custom armors, and animated 3D models (this one it's only me), but there is one issue. They are overridden by Iris (and OptiFine) shaders. They don't work anymore, and the server can't do anything. It can't even know that it doesn't work for the client.
**Describe the solution you'd like**
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
Adding a custom payload that will send information about Iris, such as the version, whether a shader is enabled, and which shader is enabled, if it is registered by the server. You may ask, "Why?" As the server knows the client is using a shader, he could send a modified version of the shader that contains the core shaders (it's easy to implement a core shader in an Iris/OF shader), like a resource pack, he could also send the client a payload that says "just disable your shader I swear it's better".
**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.
Make resource pack can override/modify an iris shader.
**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.
I know this feature is complicated, I am a developer, but I can help you develop it. 👍

issues.title: Make log field mandatory for bug report and crash report issue templates

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm always frustrated when people ignore the templates and don't share critical information.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make the log field mandatory.

You would also need to modify the placeholder for the field in the crash report issue template as it makes it look like people need to paste their crash reports in there, when they only need to upload the file. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I don't know of another solution 

**Additional context**
For a recent example, see https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/2738

No log means you don't know what shaderpack they're using, what graphics driver version they have, etc. 

I've brought this up on the Discord server a few times already but nothing has changed

issues.title: Incorrect block breaking colouring (Sildur's Vibrant Shaders)
issues.body:
### What happened?

```
MC 1.21.5
sodium-fabric-0.6.13+mc1.21.5
fabric-api-0.121.0+1.21.5
Iris-Installer-3.2.1
Sildur's Vibrant Shaders v1.52 Extreme-VL
```

Steps:
1. Install MC 1.21.5
2. Install the last supported versions of Sodium, Fabric, and Iris
3. Add Sildur's Vibrant Shaders v1.52 Extreme-VL to `shaderpacks`
4. In the game, select `Sildur's Vibrant Shaders v1.52 Extreme-VL` as the shaderpack
5. Place a torch and try breaking some lit blocks near it.

AR: Depending on where the player stands, we either get a completely dark breaking pattern or a distorted lit one (see screenshot)

ER: The breaking pattern colouring corresponds to the one seen when using OptiFine (subjectively the same as vanilla)

When using Sildur's shaders combined with Iris, we get wrong colours while breaking the blocks lit by light sources like torches. 

This issue has been reported before:
https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1180

But it was closed with a fix. However, the fix doesn't seem to work right now as the behaviour is as before.

Commented on that ticket, but I can't reopen it, so raising a fresh ticket.
https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1180#issuecomment-2849269357

Thank you.

### What happened?

Unsure if it could be related to Sodium as well, but performance with shaders in 1.21.5 is halved (at least with my specs) compared to 1.21.4 despite higher fps average without shaders on. I think more testing on other configs needs to be done (I am kind of limited in this regard) but with my testing with Complimentary Reimagined (5.4 and 5.5.1 as well), my results are as follows...

NOTE: I also tried out Silders Enhanced Default, what should have been an easy 130 fps average in the past turned into 72 fps average from my quick testing, so its highly unlikely that this is an issue with the shader pack in question if this is consistent across 2 different shader packs now.

1.21.4:
No Shaders: 140 fps avg
Complimentary Reimagined: 47-55 fps avg
Silders Enhanced Default: 120-145 fps avg

1.21.5:
No Shaders: 269-271 fps avg
Complimentary Reimagined: 25-29 fps avg
Silders Enhanced Default: 71-75 fps avg

Specs:
Intel Core i7 8700
Nvidia GeForce GTX 1060 3GB
16 GB DDR4 2666 MHz
Windows 11 (have not tested Arch Linux yet)
JDK Version: Eclipse Temurin™ JDK 22
RAM Allocation: 2048 MiB Min, 10000 MiB Max
Shader pack settings preset: Custom (mostly low-medium though)
Test map seed: -4960670273589965778 (Large Biomes)
Command used for testing: /tp @p -517 120 632 0 40

Unsure as to what is the cause of this, but I urge performance testing to be done by others on the 1.21.5 build vs the 1.21.4 build. Could it be Sodium related? I'm not sure because I'm getting better performance without shaders when updating. Resource utilization looks to be roughly the same, though I seem to be using a bit less RAM overall, but that would definitely not explain -45% performance. If anyone can test these 2 versions and update the Issue, that would be cool and could probably give everyone more insight as to what's going on.

You also need Sodium and Fabric API because they're dependencies.

With shaders enabled, there will be severe graphical artifacts when opening any kind of UI (pause menu, crafting table, etc.)
No errors will appear in the console
The issue goes away if you exit and reenter the world. Though it will randomly come back after a while.

The issues look different depending on the shader though it seemeingly affects every shaders
- Complementary will display a blank white screen
- BSL will display a blank white screen
- Photon will have all translucents disappear and hall of mirrors effects will happen on the skybox
- Bliss will have all shadows and translucents disppear as well as the skybox

- Install Iris, Res Control++, Cubes Without Borders, Sodium and Fabric API

- Enable a shader
- Press ESC to pause the game

issues.body:
### What happened?

Also see GeForceLegend/SEUS_PTGI_GFME#72

If DH shadow is enabled with provided environment (latest Iris and DH in 1.21.1), before rendering DH shadow, glViewPort will be set to screen size, causing shadow program write to a screen sized part in the lower left part of shadowmapping, causing completely wrong shadow.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b63c52fe-928e-4794-b416-6a64de9e3dd7)

issues.title: Tangent and normal attributes aren't normalized in non-terrain programs
issues.body:
### What happened?

Iris' patched attributes `iris_Normal` and `at_tangent` (the xyz components) are stored in 3x8 snorm XYZ format, which causes them to not be fully normalized when decoded. issues.title: Incompatibility with Xdi8Aho Mod 3.0.0-beta1: textures of Symbol Stone S and N showing as purple-black squares
issues.body:
### What happened?

I am the developer of Xdi8Aho Mod. Yesterday, I received a bug report that when Xdi8Aho Mod (fabric-1.21.4-3.0.0-beta1) and Iris Shaders Mod (fabric-1.8.8+mc1.21.4) were installed on Minecraft 1.21.4 at the same time, the texture images of Symbol Stone S and Symbol Stone N were missing, showing as purple-black squares.
However, only these two blocks have the bug. The other blocks render normally, and when the Iris Mod is not installed, these two blocks also render normally. 

Through testing, I can confirm that the bug is caused by Iris Shaders. The textures files are not correctly recognized by Iris. Though the images are actually in the resource pack, the game cannot render them. The locations of them are assets/firefly8/textures/block/symbol_stone_s.png and assets/firefly8/textures/block/symbol_stone_n.png.
Since the new version of the Xdi8Aho Mod has not been released publicly, I submitted the file as an attachment in the issue. Fabric API (0.107.0+) and Architectury API (15.0+) are needed for the mod.

### What happened?

When using Iris on macOS, using a MacBook Pro M4 Pro, when trying to play at above a 60 fps limit, the game becomes a stutter mess. It does not happen at 60FPS. issues.title: Batched entity rendering causes Powah reactor to become translucent
issues.body:
### What happened?

To reproduce:
1. On NeoForge (I used 21.1.84), install Iris 1.8.1, Powah 6.1.6, Industrial Foregoing 1.21-3.6.22 (and associated dependencies).
2. Open the following world: [reactor_sorting_issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18630722/reactor_sorting_issue.zip)
3. Observe that stained glass and the IF working area visual both render through the reactor.

Disabling the working area on the IF machine (can be done on the central right portion of its GUI) makes the reactor correctly occlude geometry behind it.

This issue can be observed without a shader enabled, but not if Iris is completely removed, so I suspect it's an issue with the batched entity rendering optimization.

### Screenshots

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad434483-b57f-4293-b23c-163eac1c2f62)

### Log output

_No response_

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 1.21.1

### Iris Version

1.8.1

### Operating System

Arch Linux

### What is your GPU?

RX 6600

### Additional context

The working area and reactor both appear to render as block entities using a typical `BlockEntityRenderer` that writes into a buffer provided by the `MultiBufferSource`. The issue seems dependent on the order in which they render, so their placement relative to one another in the chunk section is important.

Powah's BER: https://github.com/Technici4n/Powah/blob/1.21.1/src/main/java/owmii/powah/client/render/tile/ReactorRenderer.java
IF's BER: https://github.com/InnovativeOnlineIndustries/Industrial-Foregoing/blob/1.21/src/main/java/com/buuz135/industrial/proxy/client/render/WorkingAreaTESR.java

issues.title: Iris reports incorrect emissive entity data for shaders depending on items in hotbar
issues.body:
### What happened?

Shader + an enchanting table resource pack (includes optifine-styled emissive textures) + continuity (does not touch entities) with emissive textures on causes some entities to have emissive textures when they shouldn't. The pixels change depending on hotbar items.

```
Minecraft 1.21.1

Fabric 0.16.10
Continuity 3.0.0+1.21 or 3.0.0-beta.5+1.21
Complementary Shaders - Reimagined r5.2.2
- RP Support: Integrated PBR+
- Performance Settings > Shadow Sample Quality: Off or Very Low
Fabric API 0.115.0+1.21.1
Iris Shaders 1.8.1+1.21.1-fabric
Sodium mc1.21.1-0.6.5-fabric

Better Enchanting Table 1.2 by Jacosvaldo
```

Texture pack: https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/enchanting-table-magic-circle

The last piece to this enigma is that the mob emissions are dependent on what item is right-most in your hotbar. Angle of view, such as having entity on edge of your screen, can also influence the effect.

Bug is removed by turning off emissive textures in continuity settings, changing one of the two shader settings mentioned, turning off the shader, unequipping the resource pack, having most items right-most in hotbar, or pressing F1 to disable GUI.

### Screenshots

Screenshots below show an affected mob. The item does not need to be held for this effect to activate, it just needs to be right-most in hotbar. Held to show what item was causing what effect (it's curious!). Additionally, effect is removed if F1 is pressed to hide GUI.

issues.title: Server Shader Pack

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Using vanilla minecraft, Resourcepacks can change core shaders. This allows some fancy clientside effect on modded servers. Sodium sadly breaks this. I'm working on a modded server without the need to install client mods, resource packs or shader packs. Resources are provided via a Server Resource Pack, but even with sodium and iris installed, shaders can't be sent or even suggested by the server. Since many modded clients use or support Iris and some even bundle it like [Lunar Client](https://www.lunarclient.com/news/sodium-and-iris), it would be very beneficial to be able to load shader packs from the server via Iris. 

TLDR: Core shaders break with sodium; Iris is like a stable shader API for sodium; To get the functionality of core shaders with iris, it would be good to suggest shaders from a server or inside a resource pack.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
One way would be to introduce a new packet or a plugin message that shows a similar prompt like the resource pack thing. When serverside packs are loaded, no other packs can be loaded (or at least without confirmation). Distribution works like vanilla - send the client a link and a checksum. Why should this be implemented in Iris? Because it is the de-facto standard for shader support and many users already have Iris installed.

Another way would be allow shaderpacks to be added to (server) resource packs. If Iris shaders are integrated, core shaders are ignored and only the Iris shaders are loaded. This would also circumvent a potential privacy problem with servers being able to detect if iris/sodium is present on the client (There was a discussion about this a while back on the Minestom discord). 

Both of these are not optimal - core shader support in sodium would be best but I think this is a good compromise. Please tell me about any issues or ideas you might think of.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Not supporting sodium or Iris
- Try merging core shader support into Sodium (afaik sodium devs don't want this)
- Prompting the user myself to go install a custom shader pack every time they join (UX nightmare)

**Additional Info**
If you want, I can create a simple protocol specification and implement it in a PR. But this is a non-trivial feature and I want to get feedback on the idea first.

<sub>Also thanks for Cosmic on the Minestom discord for providing a lot of good feedback</sub>

issues.title: Crash when reloading textures using CIT Resewn custom glint texture
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Iris Version

iris-fabric-1.8.1+mc1.21.1

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-0.6.5+mc1.21.1

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060

### Java Version

Java 21

### Reproduction Steps

1. Use [these](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qq-fWEvhUZ3-I40fDTML4_T2Nfhcp7ev?usp=drive_link) mods and sample resourcepack.
2. Open up game and a test world.
3. Move the sample resource pack to selected in option (Sometime the crash happens in this step).
4. Press F3 + T to reload resource pack, this might need to be done multiple times to trigger the crash.

### Crash Report file and latest.log

```shell
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R6vJllmn0oNN4XgGCKFHDXPuDl4Wcsdd/view?usp=drive_link
```

### Additional context

Related issue in [CIT Resewn](https://github.com/SHsuperCM/CITResewn/issues/122).

This reload crash occurs only when I am using Iris Shaders with CIT Resewn custom glint texture. Without Iris Shader, The CIT Resewn custom glint will reload fine without any crash.

The mysterious part is that it only occurred occasionally, but still frequent enough that it's very bothersome when I am tinkering with custom glint function with CIT Resewn. Given the [logs](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R6vJllmn0oNN4XgGCKFHDXPuDl4Wcsdd/view?usp=drive_link) and the nature of crash, it might have something to do with race condition when it is trying to load custom glint texture with "texture": "texture_name.png" in the custom enchantment_glint.properties file.

issues.title: Wrong texture when rendering invisible cube of boats
issues.body:
### What happened?

Almost same as sp614x/optifine#7608. When rendering the invisible cube of boats (vanilla use it to ignore water in boat), Iris will just use the albedo texture of last draw call for current one, which may cause render result changes with other entities, especially in shadow.

### Screenshots

2 captures showing shadow inside boats changes while giving player invisible effect, caused by texture used for the invisible cube changed to another one (tho both of them are not boat texture) in shadowmap generating.

### What happened?

I'm using the Hysteria Shaders in a very large modpack, and for every update you've released since 1.8.0-beta.4, the shaders will fail to load on startup. issues.title: Iris 1.8.1 not tagged for 1.21 game version tag on Modrinth
issues.body:
Iris 1.8.1 is missing the 1.21 game version tag on Modrinth.

This means that when updating mods Prism will update Sodium to 0.6.5 but does not find the required Iris 1.8.1 dependency, resulting in a broken installation that cannot launch.

Installing manually from https://modrinth.com/mod/iris/version/1.8.1+1.21.1-fabric will work but this is obviously not ideal from a UX perspective.

Please can the Iris 1.8.1 be correctly tagged as being compatible with BOTH 1.21 and 1.21.1 on Modrinth.

Thank you.

issues.title: Possible Memory Leak. Excessive memory usage after changing settings one too many times.
issues.body:
### What happened?

I was messing with shader settings to look into a shader issue. I noticed that after messing with the settings for a while memory usage will constantly climb higher until it hits the allocation limit and constatnly triggers garbage collector resulting in heavy lag and the game being unplayable.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2118e831-1296-4ce5-b80b-8e011b786fd0

issues.title: Incorrect vertex normal for terrain

labels.name: status: underlying issue identified
labels.description: A root cause of the issue has been identified (only devs should add this tag)

issues.body:
### What happened?

Iris is using unsigned normalized octahedron decoding for vertex normal. To get exact vertex normal for common surfaces, it needs the input be 0.0 and 0.5. But in vertex attributes, Iris is using RGBA8_SNORM and even throw values between [-1.0, 0.0) away, and 0.5 will be about 0.496 in vertex attribute. This will create obvious artifact in some situation, like this image using ComplementaryReimagined_r5.2.2, because of the incorrect normal, left part is reflecting things under water:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29769842-63e7-449c-b5d6-ad7dce8920f8)

As Iris is using RGBA8_SNORM as vertex attribute format, why not just using the full [-1.0, 1.0] range, and removing `* 2.0 + 1.0` in the beginning of octahedron decoding code? RGBA8_SNORM can get 0.0 correctly (works same as 0.5 in current solution), which means we will get exact normal data on common surfaces.

### Screenshots

issues.title: Inconsistent behavior for IRIS_TAG_SUPPORT when trying to combine tags
issues.body:
### What happened?

Trying to combine vanilla tags with modded tags to define a group of blocks does not work, however combining modded tags does.

Example:
Does work
`block.ID = %supplementaries:candle_holders:dyed/black:candles=2:lit=true`
Does not work
`block.ID = %candles:dyed/black:candles=2:lit=true`
Variations like these also don't work
`block.ID = %minecraft:candles:dyed/black:candles=2:lit=true`
`block.ID = %candles:c:dyed/black:candles=2:lit=true`

### Screenshots

This is Bliss Shader Commit 482 with colored light/candles enabled and having both entries from the example above in the corresponding block.ID field. The vanilla candle should emit the same amount of light as the modded candle.


### Additional context

Again going over the details. With only these mods installed;

Fabric loader 1.21 0.16.9
fabric-api-0.102.0+1.21.jar
iris-fabric-1.8.0+mc1.21.1.jar
sodium-fabric-0.6.0-beta.2+mc1.21.1.jar

Shaderpack where the issue was found;
Mellow Shader v1.5.2.zip

Go into any world, single or Multiplayer and load the Mellow shaderpack. The game crashes.

Reloading the game straight after a crash works fine but now you can not join any worlds, single or multiplayer without it crashing again.

The game will reload ok straight after a crash but to stop it from still crashing, you must do either;

1) Disable the shader or change to another pack within the video settings before trying to open world or join a server.

2) Disable or remove both, the shader pack and Iris from the system folders. If you try to remove or disable only the shader pack from shader folder, the game will still crash. At this point, both the shader pack and Iris need to be disabled or removed, the game reloaded, then you can reload the game once again with Iris installed.


As of right now, I have only found the issue to happen with this one shader pack. I tried it with some of the others I had installed at the time but I didn't try all of them or others.

issues.title: Vanilla visuals are not maintained if a gbuffer pass is omitted
issues.body:
### What happened?

When creating a shader, the vanilla visuals of Minecraft are not maintained if a specific gbuffer pass is omitted. For example, if gbuffers_skybasic is missing, there are no stars at night; if gbuffers_clouds is missing, the fog is not applied correctly to them; if gbuffers_armor_glint is missing, the glint is then not animated; and so on.

This forces shader developers to do more work than necessary if they wish to keep some parts vanilla, especially since in some cases it's not so trivial to cover all edge-cases with a replacement. It also differs from Optifine, which keeps vanilla visuals in this scenario.

issues.title: Exclude dimension(s) from folder in dimension.properties

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
My mod conflicts with a lot of shaders that work with iris, and so I decided to give people instructions on how to add my custom dimensions to the dimension.properties so that shaders simply won't do anything in that dimension. However, I found that to do this with most shaders, I had to take out any wildcards (*) for folders. For example, the Complimentary Reimagined file was:

```
dimension.world0=*

dimension.world-1=minecraft:the_nether minecraft:nether

dimension.world1=minecraft:the_end minecraft:end
```

But to remove my dimension from the shaders I had to change it to:

```
dimension.world0=minecraft:the_overworld minecraft:overworld

dimension.world-1=minecraft:the_nether minecraft:nether

dimension.world1=minecraft:the_end minecraft:end
```

However, now the shader doesn't work in _any_ modded dimension, as I've removed the wildcard from the world0 folder.

As a solution, I would like some way to exclude a dimension from a wildcard, instead of only including. Something like:

`dimension.world0=* !namespace:mydimension`

(would work on any dimension except namespace:mydimension)

If there is already a way to do this, or an alternative, please let me know. But I definitely think this would be a good feature, if there's nothing like it already.

issues.title: Uniforms start with dh does not match projection matrix in dh gbuffers
issues.body:
### What happened?

Uniforms starts with dh (`dhProjection`, `dhProjectionInverse`) does not match the `gl_ProjectionMatrix` in dh gbuffer, when projection matrix is changing. It's mostly visible when using and stop using spyglass, and start or stop sprinting while flying. This image shows those uniforms in a frame capture.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2316f09f-22eb-4499-9179-4eb76aa513cd)

Looks like all depth factor of dh uniforms are 1 frame behind. Tho using `dhProjection` instead of `gl_ProjectionMatrix` in dh gbuffer can fix this, most developer will (and tons of developers still now) use `gl_ProjectionMatrix` in the first time, making them confused.

### Screenshots

This is an example on old version of my project, which still uses `gl_ProjectionMatrix` but not `dhProjection` in dh gbuffers. When stop using spyglass, dh terrian sometimes become closer than expected, causing strange screen space shadow around the edge of normal terrain and DH terrain.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f617f45-f28b-44e8-a673-38f9e9cd9cc1)

Activating a sticky piston with redstone sometimes causes the items in the hotbar and inventory to turn black. Also all text (chat, buttons, ...) turns black. Reloading shader packs does not work, issue even exists on title screen after leaving world. Can be temporarily fixed by mining any block.

issues.title: Translation change bug using the resource pack
issues.body:
### What happened?

When I want to change the iris translation (in my case I was changing the Ukrainian translation) using the resource pack, it doesn't apply until I remove the translation file from the mod's jar.
Iris is the only mod in which I noticed such a problem, and I don't know why it appears and I hope you can fix it.

Note: when I added a translation to the lines that were not in the translation file (in my case, the Ukrainian language translation file), the translation worked fine.

### Minecraft Version

26.1.x

### Iris Version

iris-1.10.9

issues.title: [Bug] Minecraft Black Screen with Iris and Sodium Mods After Several Minutes of Play (1.20.1)
issues.body:
### What happened?

I am experiencing an issue where the screen randomly turns black after several minutes to half an hour of play in Minecraft 1.20.1. The game continues running (I can hear sound), but the screen remains black. No crash report is generated. I have to manually shut down my PC and restart it. This issue also happens even when only using the Sodium and Iris mods together.

**Mods**:  
- Iris Shaders (installed via Iris installer)
- Sodium
- Other performance-enhancing mods (Indium, LTHum, Nvidium, etc.)
**Java Version**: OpenJDK 17

**Steps to Reproduce**:
1. Install Minecraft version 1.20.1.
2. Install Fabric version fabric-loader-0.16.9-1.20.1.
3. Install Iris Shaders and Sodium using the respective installers.
4. Play the game with shaders enabled and render distance set to 32 chunks or higher.
5. After several minutes to half an hour, the screen turns black, but the game continues to run with sound.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Log output

[15:53:08] [Thread-33/INFO]: OpenGL debug message: id=1280, source=API, type=ERROR, severity=HIGH, message='GL_INVALID_ENUM error generated. <attachment> does not specify a valid attachment for the default framebuffer.'

### Minecraft Version

fabric-loader-0.16.9-1.20.1

### Iris Version

iris-1.7.2+mc1.20.1.jar

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA RTX 3080

### Additional context

- RAM: 32GB


**What I've Tried**:
1. Switching Java versions (Java 8, Java 17)
2. Adjusting Iris and Sodium settings
3. Modifying OpenGL settings (`-Dorg.lwjgl.opengl.display.allowSoftwareOpenGL=true`)
4. Updating GPU drivers

**Expected Behavior**:  
The game should not show a black screen and should run without issues.

**Additional Information**:  
The issue happens randomly after anywhere between 6 to 36 minutes of gameplay. It occurs even with only the Sodium and Iris mods. The mods were installed using their respective installers (Iris from the official Iris installer).

The shader used is ComplementaryUnbound_r5.3.

Thank you for your time and help in resolving this issue. I appreciate the hard work that the development team puts into making this mod possible.

1.7.2

RX 470/570

Java 22

issues.title: Static initialization of VertexFormatElements is incompatible with other mods
issues.body:
### What happened?

The game crashes when multiple mods try to add new `VertexFormatElement`s if their IDs overlap with Iris'.
Additionally, due to the parallel nature of Mod Startup in NeoForge it probably isn't threadsafe.

The advice I got on what to pass to the ID parameter was to AT the `ELEMENTS` array in `VertexFormatElement` and use its `size()` method; doing so, on the NeoForge side, in `FMLClientSetupEvent#enqueueWork`, so it's thread safe.

Additionally XFactHD mentioned that the passed values to the `index` parameter are not correct

https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/d6bf750fe256c6be54c560de543892f1f00e9654/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/vertices/IrisVertexFormats.java#L20-L24

Apparently, what should be passed there is how often the specific USAGE has occurred before, so you'd have to count through the `ELEMENTS` array how many are there already.

Here's the direct quote from the Discord:
> What should be passed to the `index` parameter?

> The occurence of the "element usage". It's 0 for most things, but UV for example has indices 0, 1 and 2 for texture, hurt overlay and light respectively. They'd have to count how many elements with any given usage are already registered and use that as the index (you should ideally do that too)

issues.title: iris crashes when running on neoforge 1.21
Add an interpolated temperature uniform

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
I am designing a mock thermal vision shader. It currently uses a mixture of lighting values and block colors, but to further enhance the visuals, I implemented the temperature value provided by the mod. This addition works great, however for lack of any interpolation, there is a jarring and often extreme transition between color tones when changing biomes, a transition that becomes especially annoying around the borders of intermingled biomes.

This issue would be resolved if some form of interpolated temperature were provided. As far as the proposed timescale, I suggest using a `uniform vec4` laid out such that the transition time is equal to `(1 second, 2 seconds, 5 seconds, 10 seconds)` if possible.

I am not opposed to other implementations, the only real concrete interest is that a value is provided which is interpolated over a span of time around 5 seconds.
