issues.title: Idea: Overwrite layered entity / block entity rendering - banners, horses, etc

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Currently, to blend gradients and different textures together on layered content like horses and banners, Minecraft repeatedly draws the same model with different textures / blending modes. This might mean that rendering a complex horse or banner could require upwards of 16 draw calls.

This leads to a number of issues, including performance concerns, as well as not working well with Iris batched entity rendering. In addition, it is not compatible with deferred-rendering shaderpacks, which are not able to properly handle translucency in many cases.

A smarter approach would be to place all of these different layers into a 2D texture array, and then have a shader that is capable of sampling from this array in a loop as needed. It's likely that some sort of auxiliary UBO or similar would be necessary to pass information about the ordering of layers.

Then, existing vanilla / Iris shaders could be patched to read from this array instead of sampling the main texture. This would alleviate challenges with having to pass horses & banners through Iris batched entity rendering, it would allow deferred-rendering shaderpacks to handle horses & banners properly without any special work needed for translucency, and finally it could improve performance as well.

This would have some mod compatibility & implementation complexity concerns. In addition, it might be more fit for a mod like Sodium that is oriented towards optimization & replacing vanilla rendering.

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When I updated the mod and booted up my instance, it told me to stop using Not Enough Crashes. Fine, I thought. I'll use Crafty Crashes. **Describe the solution you'd like**

The words "Crafty Crashes" in the message should directly link to the mod's GitHub page.

N/A

N/A

issues.title: FSR 1 / 2 Toggle
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Shaders are pretty heavy on gpu.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Creating a toggle for fsr 2 or at least 1 would free some gpu resources for shaders

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Resoluution Scalers could do the same buut with higher quality hits.
**Additional context**
This would allow more people to use shaders and give parity with the resolution scaler of optifine.

issues.title: NVIDIA Reflex support for Iris
issues.body:
Shaders usually use 99% of your GPU when framerate is uncapped. This introduces huge amounts of input lag and the only practical counter for it currently is capping the framerate.

It would be such a good quality of life improvement to have NVIDIA Reflex implemented into Iris as it syncs the GPU and CPU loads to mitigate the input lag. I'm not too sure if it supports OpenGL or if it's even possible to implement as a mod although I believe it has been modded for Skyrim for example.

It would simply be awesome to always be able to play the game with the highest possible framerate and smoothness without any hinder.

issues.title: Iris Support for VulkanAPI
issues.body:
Hello,

I'm here to mention this mod https://github.com/xCollateral/VulkanMod which allows to start minecraft with the Vulkan API instead of OpenGL, chances are if the mod get's enough attention.. it might support FidelityFX Super Resolution which will drastically improve performance.
As an example this mod https://www.nexusmods.com/aplaguetalerequiem/mods/9 replaces DLSS with FSR in A Plague Tale Requiem, without the mod i had an average of 40 FPS on a GTX 1080 Ti 1440p ultra settings. With the FSR mod on Quality mode i had an average 80 FPS with the same settings while the image still looked even better then native.
Those results are crazy.
I beleve this (DLSS and FSR) are the future and will be supported by all major upcomming games.
The potential is to much to be ignored, my opinion.

Taking a look at VulkanMod's github page it clearly says this: "This is a fabric mod that rewrites Minecraft OpenGL renderer to use Vulkan API."
With 12,163 downloads the mod is still pretty smal compared to fabric / optifine / sodium, then again imagine what Fabric, VulkanAPI, Optifine, and FidelityFX Super Resolution could do together, i have no doubt minecraft's performance would skyrocket.

Seus Shader and Patrix Resourcepack are very performance hungry, getting an average 60 FPS with both enabled, i consider them both mandatory for playing minecraft as they look really good.
With Vulkan and FSR those 60 FPS could easily turn into 120.
At this moment using optifine with fabric requires optifabric, combining those mods with vulkanmod results in a game-crash.
By creating this "issue" i hope to bring more attention to the vulkanmod and it's potential for FSR.
If fabric, optifine, and optifabric would officialy support vulkanmod

Just like Optifine, Sodium and Iris also crash combined with Vulkanmod.
With fabric loader OpenGL and sodium i get 1300 FPS max when looking at the sky.
With fabric loader and vulkanmod i get 1150 FPS max when looking at the sky.
Combine those and...

![Seus PTGI + Patrix](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/116210112/198885316-b9ad5b1d-8915-4930-8608-4686f6a21209.png)

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Since glsl-transformer is in iris, debugging shaders has become more difficult due to syntax errors being caught by glsl-transformer, which doesn't include program names in its error messages. this is annyoing when working on files that are included by multiple programs.
example error message:
`[18:34:14] [Render thread/ERROR]: Failed to create shader rendering pipeline, disabling shaders!
org.antlr.v4.runtime.misc.ParseCancellationException: line 1529:0 no viable alternative at input 'sldakfnge\nvec3'`

**Describe the solution you'd like**
error messages thrown my glsl-transformer should contain the name of the program in which they occurred. the example error message shown above could be changed to something like

`[18:34:14] [Render thread/ERROR]: Failed to create shader rendering pipeline, disabling shaders!
org.antlr.v4.runtime.misc.ParseCancellationException: program "gbuffers_basic.fsh" line 1529:0 no viable alternative at input 'sldakfnge\nvec3'`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I considered booting up optifine every time I get an error like that, but that's tedious

issues.title: Block Entity Delayed Update with Shaders Enabled

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
### What happened?

When placing/breaking a block entity, such as a sign, chest, mob head, etc, the visual update of it being placed or breaking is delayed until you move in some way. If you are completely still while doing this, the block entity will not update, or will take a few seconds to update. If you move your mouse even slightly, it will update as soon as you do.

This issue only happens with shaders enabled. If shaders are disabled, block entities update normally.

It will happen with only Sodium and Iris installed. No other mods or resource packs required to reproduce.

This is not guaranteed to happen every time, but it does happen often. Perhaps 70% of the time.

I have attached a video below to show the issue, in case it is confusing. I first break, then place a sign with shaders on. The issue is visible. Then I disable shaders, break/place the sign again. The issue is no longer occurring.

### What happened?

After my many tests, only the new version 1.19.2 of Iris has this problem on all SEUS (continuum is its own problem), while the old version of 1.17.1 does not, this is definitely a bug. 
Physics mod
In addition to this I also found a problem with the Parallax Mapping on SEUS HRR 3
Entities such as 3D particles in Physics Mod will have texture errors.
If HRR 3 has parallax mapping turned on, it will produce black pixel jitter where the edge of the screen intersects the parallax square。to be clear, this is not a big issue.
BUT，if you On motion blur，Black pixels will be motion blurred and flickering will greatly affect the experience.Also tested in Optifine, no same problem.
Texture mapping errors with SEUS occur in all SEUS shaders I've tried (including Renewed, E12, HRR 2.1, HRR 3, E12)
I guess it may be because of the update of the parallax map that the first batch of SUES supporting parallax is abnormal, because we also know that SUES has not been updated for a long time and will not be updated for a long time.

It's possible that I'm wrong, it's SEUS own problem, if so, then I apologize for all Developer

issues.title: Investigate parallel shader compilation

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Shader packs can have extremely complex shader programs, resulting in shader compilation taking multiple seconds for many packs and as much as 20 seconds for the most complex packs. Currently, Iris compiles shader programs sequentially, waiting for one program to finish before compiling the next. This is very suboptimal.

At a minimum, Iris should dispatch all required glCompileShader invocations before starting to query the compilation status (which forces the compilation process for the queried shader to complete) and similar for the linking operations. This would require a sizable restructuring, especially on 1.17+ where we're working with code that's pretty highly intertwined with Minecraft's shader system in vanilla. However, on modern systems with many cores, it could make shader pack loading and settings changes many times faster, perhaps over an order of magnitude.

In addition, if that does not bring an improvement or if we want to not freeze Minecraft while waiting for shaders to compile, we might want to investigate https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/main/extensions/ARB/ARB_parallel_shader_compile.txt. Imagine if we could have an interactive loading bar displaying compile progress instead of the trusty old `Minecraft (Not Responding)` title bar?

issues.title: Red or black overlay on items and mobs
issues.body:
### What happened?

Some entities and items have red tint, as if they were a mob that just took damage. It appears to only happen when camera is rotated at certain angle. Presence of mobs seems to increase chances of reproducing this.
Also I found a similar bug report on forge fork of iris https://github.com/Asek3/Oculus/issues/17 but the issue here seems a bit different. Entities are not red at all times and can also render in black in case of inventory items.

issues.title: Piston head has no animation / bugs when standing completely sill

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
### What happened?

When powering a piston, where normally the animation of the head extending should play, the piston head just disappears and reappears extended. This only happens when standing completely still. When moving your head or moving around, the animation works fine. Sometimes, the animation completely bugs out and the head goes up and down really fast.

issues.title: Implement FSR 2.1 (Video attached showing potential performance improvements)

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Normally FSR wouldn't really benefit Minecraft because it's a very CPU intensive game but with shaders the GPU is utilized enough to warrant the addition of FSR.

[Here's](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0clmmzZvE6I) an old video of someone using a fairly hacky way to use an early version of FSR on Minecraft with shaders. As you can see the benefits are pretty exceptional. The improvements with FSR 2.1 and a real implementation could achieve massive performance gains.

issues.title: F3 Reduction/Cleanup

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The debug screen can get extremely cluttered in a modded environment, one of the bigger causes is iris and its entity batching/shadow debug info.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be extremely helpful to have some sort of toggle to remove the extra unneeded debug info contributing to the "f3 pollution".(but also keeping the iris version and shaderpack info on the f3 menu often does not show any immediate issues and can be helpful for the support team and debugging so might as well be keeped).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I am unsure of what could be done in a clean, simple, non intrusive way to do this so I might just leave it up to the developers stances. A potential solution for cleaning up the f3 menu is compressing the shadow debug info down extremely. I was thinking of a similar system of what vanilla does to reduce screen space clutter in the f3 menu, specifically the system where the value is shortened down to a single letter "A: 'value' ", doing this method could potentially allow compressing the multiple lines of debug info into one or two lines which may be harder to understand to the average user but will still be easy to understand for the developers and support team.

**Additional context**
Maybe potentially moving the iris version info to be right below the sodium versioning(as in the next line) for organization reasons.

issues.title: Iris-Installer-2.0.4.jar reported success but resulted in no new minecraft profile and a 0KB iris-fabric-loader jar
issues.body:
### What happened?

I downloaded and ran Iris-Installer-2.0.4.jar.  Install options: Iris+Sodium, Minecraft v1.19.1, install to default dir (.minecraft), not as a Fabric mod.

The installer reported success after a brief progress bar.  When I launched minecraft, there was no new runtime profile to launch using Iris.  When I instead ran my previously existing 1.19.1 profile, there was no option on the video settings screen to customize shaders.

When I looked in my .minecraft folder, I did see a few new files, such as an updated launcher_profiles.json, which contained references to Iris.  I also found a new sub-folder iris-reserved, which contained two 1.19.1 jars.  I also found a new folder under versions, which is screenshotted below; however that folder contained a 0 KB file named iris-fabric-loader-0.14.8-1.19.1.jar.

As of now, I don't seem to be able to use Iris.

Earlier in the year, I had installed and used Fabric, Sodium, and Phosphor without Iris on 1.18.  These mods were still installed in my .minecraft installation when I attempted the Iris install on the newest Minecraft version.

issues.title: VectorizeSIMD Java flag breaks villager/passive mob rendering
issues.body:
### What happened?

Villagers and passive mobs will turn invisible after some time (usually less than a minute), but *only* if the VectorizeSIMD flag is enabled.


**Steps to reproduce the issue**

- Download the latest GraalVM EE Java 17 release. Its free, but requires registration here https://www.oracle.com/downloads/graalvm-downloads.html

- Edit your settings to launch the game with GraalVM EE, with the following flags: `-Dgraal.VectorizeSIMD=true -Dgraal.UsePriorityInlining=false`

- Launch Minecraft 1.18.2 or 1.19.x with sodium, fabric, and iris, using GraalVM EE 17 

- Create a peaceful, superflat, singleplayer world

- Find a village. After some time (usually less than a minute), villagers and passive mobs will turn invisible. 

- This will not happen when Dgraal.VectorizeSIMD is set to false. 


It doesn't seem to matter if shaders are even enabled or not, it happens either way. It does not happen with Sodium by itself, and it doesn't happen in any other Java distribution, including GraalVM CE.



### Screenshots
Shaders are completely disabled in the top screenshot, and enabled (Complimentary V4) in the bottom.
![Screenshot (9)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8422224/182039597-63a14c55-ce48-4048-8e16-84514e437275.png)
![Screenshot (10)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8422224/182039599-bf378ebe-dfc3-4985-8804-45b77a8aa5b9.jpg)



### Log output

https://mclo.gs/vNdU1Ls

### Minecraft Version

1.19.1 and 1.18.2

### Iris Version

1.2.6

### Operating System

Windows 10 21H2

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia Geforce RTX 2060

### Additional context

Also documented on Oracle's Github page: https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/4775
 
Unlike my closed sodium issue, I have confirmed this does not happen in vanilla, or with just sodium + fabric.

issues.title: Iris loweres FPS with EBE + Entity Culling.
issues.body:
### What happened?

27 of June I noticed a weird thing. Iris lowers FPS with EBE (Enhanced Block Entities) and Entity Culling mods.
All tests was made on RestWorld map from same angles. 
Here's the results:
Sodium + Iris = 150 FPS.
Sodium + Iris + EBE = 165 FPS.
Sodium + Iris + Entity Culling = 195 FPS.
Sodium + Entity Culling + EBE = 280 FPS.
Sodium + Iris + Entity Culling + EBE = 150 FPS.

Today I updated my GPU drivers and the results are way better, but FPS drop is still noticeable:
Sodium + Entity Culling + EBE = 420 FPS.
Sodium + Iris + Entity Culling + EBE = 285 FPS.

### Screenshots

![With_Iris](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83837475/181919907-59529034-fe91-4340-9332-b9129ccc90ac.png)
![Without_Iris](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/83837475/181919909-bb19309d-6c43-4bf4-b6a9-1c276becf91c.png)

issues.title: Lack of custom uniform support in Iris breaks the biome temperature checks used for rain reflections in Sildur's Vibrant Shaders.
issues.body:
### What happened?

(Apologies for the second bug report in such a short timespan. ;P)

The biome temperature parameter used for rain reflections in Sildur's Vibrant Shaders is broken (or possibly completely unimplemented…?) on Iris.

The relevant GLSL code can be found in `composite1.fsh`:
```glsl
	#ifdef BiomeCheck
		bool isRaining = (BiomeTemp >= 0.15) && (BiomeTemp <= 1.0) && iswet > 0.01 && land && !transparency && isEyeInWater == 0.0;
	#else
		bool isRaining = iswet > 0.01 && land && !transparency && isEyeInWater == 0.0;
	#endif
```

`BiomeTemp` is defined in `shaders.properties` as:
```glsl
# Biome temperature
uniform.float.BiomeTemp=temperature
```

---

I've confirmed that this behaviour occurs on the following Minecraft + Iris version combinations:
* Minecraft 1.19 + Iris 1.2.5
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.5
* Minecraft 1.18.1 + Iris 1.2.0-pre
* Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.5
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.5

It seems likely to me that this feature never worked correctly on Iris, and it just so happens that no one had noticed until now.

---

### Workaround

Users can work around this issue by disabling biome temperature checks entirely, either by setting the configuration key `BiomeCheck=false`, or simply commenting out `#define BiomeCheck` in `shaders.settings`.

**※ NOTE:** Using this workaround will result in rain reflections rendering in dry biomes you wouldn't expect them to, such as deserts.

---

### Screenshots

Expected behaviour from Minecraft 1.19 + OptiFine+OptiFabric 1.19 HD U H8 (※ Ignore the fact that the beacons aren't rendering, that's a separate bug with OptiFabric+Debugify):
![optifabric-reference-2022-07-23_21 52 13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1980487/180605793-66ce105e-75c6-4c12-99e2-d28887ec4409.png)

Incorrect behaviour from Minecraft 1.19 + Iris 1.2.5 (`BiomeCheck` is present / enabled):
![irysodium-biomecheckPresent-2022-07-23_21 49 30](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1980487/180605838-534b0c2d-b4fc-412d-86ae-0e4ebba62971.png)

Workaround to get rain reflections to render on Minecraft 1.19 + Iris 1.2.5 (`BiomeCheck` is commented out / disabled):
![irysodium-biomecheckComment-2022-07-23_21 44 42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1980487/180605870-d41b27c9-f6b0-40f9-b33b-868890df5264.png)

---

### Operating System

Windows 10 19044.1826 21H2 and macOS 12.4 21F79

---

NVIDIA RTX 2060 (NVGRD 512.95, DCH) and Apple G13J

issues.title: When water reflections are enabled in Sildur's Vibrant Shaders and the player is in a column of water surrounded by air, world geometry will completely fail to render in Minecraft 1.19, 1.18.2 and 1.17.1 (but NOT 1.16.5) in combination with pretty much every modern version of Iris, including Iris 1.2.5

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
### What happened?

(Sorry for the really long issue title, it was a challenge trying to summarise the bizarre nature of this bug ;P)

When water reflections are enabled in Sildur's Vibrant Shaders and the player is in a column of water surrounded by air, world geometry will completely fail to render.

The following Minecraft + Iris version combinations are **affected**:
* Minecraft 1.19 + Iris 1.2.5
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.5
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.4-build.38
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.3-build.35
* Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.5
* Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.4-build.37
* Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.3-build.34
* Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.2-build.31
* **Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.1-rc1-90bdb008**

The following Minecraft + Iris version combinations are **NOT affected**:
* **Minecraft 1.18.1 + Iris 1.2.0-pre**
* **Minecraft 1.17.1 + Iris 1.2.0-pre**
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.5
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.4-build.36
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.3-build.33
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.2-build.30
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.1-rc1-20f1aa54
* MInecraft 1.16.5 + Iris 1.2.0-pre

※ I _tried_ to test these Minecraft + Iris version combinations in an attempt to further bisect this issue to make your lives easier, but I can't remember the correct combination of Sodium + Fabric API versions required to get these old builds to work and not immediately crash at startup. If you guys keep that documentation around, these versions may possibly be worth exploring to try to bisect the issue.
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.2-build.32
* Minecraft 1.18.2 + Iris 1.2.1-rc2-0cc372f0-dirty

---

Given the above test results, it seems _very_ likely to me that the breaking change was introduced _somewhere_ between Iris 1.2.0-pre and Iris 1.2.1-rc1-90bdb008.

I am not sure why Minecraft 1.16.5 is unaffected by this issue ー perhaps that may help clue you guys in on where the issue is occurring.

This issue goes away when water reflections (configuration key `waterRefl`, or simply comment out `#define waterRefl` in `shaders.settings`) is disabled.

---

### Screenshots

Expected behaviour from Minecraft 1.19 + OptiFine+OptiFabric 1.19 HD U H8:

issues.title: Minecraft freezes when certain shaders are reloaded

labels.name: more information needed
labels.description: More information is necessary to continue investigating this issue

issues.body:
I am using
- Windows 11
- AMD Radeon RX 6600 with Adrenalin Edition Version 22.6.1
- Minecraft 1.19
- Sodium 0.4.2+build.16 with Iris 1.2.5
- SEUS Renewed v1.0.1

Whenever the shaders are reloaded, the game freezes, and will never unfreeze. This happens when going to another dimension, when changing shader settings, when disabling then re-enabling shaders, etc. It seems to happen with only SEUS (I think every flavor of SEUS), and possibly with some others. It happens at least almost every time. This means I have no way of going to the nether without freezing/crashing my game when I have shaders on.

I've tried looking around for a solution, some have been speculating that it's because of the AMD drivers, and that a fix would be to roll back to 20.4.2. Well, the thing is, I've tried that and it doesn't appear to be compatible with my graphics card. None of the other proposed workarounds have worked for me, like using a different version of Java, and some said that updating to the latest drivers worked for them, but it didn't work for me.

Is there any way this could be fixed? Or are there any other workarounds? I know it sucks if it's the fault of AMD and not Iris, but I would love for this to be accounted for and fixed if possible.

issues.title: RFC: Warn users on LabPBR/OldPBR format mismatches between shaders

labels.name: high priority
labels.description: This issue is encountered frequently and needs to be fixed quickly

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: If the user has a LabPBR shader and an OldPBR texture pack or vice versa, graphical users will occur. There is no way currently to detect if this happens, is it possible for us to solve this?

issues.title: RFC: How to handle invalid paths in Optifine texture packs

labels.name: high priority
labels.description: This issue is encountered frequently and needs to be fixed quickly

issues.body:
Optifine allows normally invalid paths in PBR/textures. How should this be resolved? Should we be allowing all invalid paths, or only allowing those used by Iris?

Blocking 1.3.

issues.title: Other Fabric mods not working if Iris is installed via the universal jar
issues.body: Not necessarily Iris related, but I understand that the universal jar also installs sodium and fabric loader. But when I put other fabric mods like lithium and phosphor to the .minecraft/mods folder, none of them work. I verified it in my log files. Is it because the universal jar installs the fabric loader in a different way?

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A shaderpack can look very different by changing its config, and it would be cool if we could make presets configs for a shaderpack, but to do that we need to duplicate files, have multiple files for the same shaderpack, change the shaderpack and remake the config for each duplicate shaderpack (and updating these configs when an update for the shaderpack is released is a pain)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be cool if in the shaderpack settings there was a preset button, then we had the ability to create a preset that we could save, then create another one to have 2 presets, then we could just change presets by selecting the one you want (and updating the shaderpack would be easier because we would only have one file to replace)

**Describe who this solution would work**
Currently in the shaderpacks folder there is the <shaderpack>.zip and a <shaderpack>.zip.txt which contains the config
Perssets could be saved the same way except they would be saved as <shaderpack>.zip_<preset>.txt
<preset> which would correspond to the name given to the preset

issues.title: Iris should allow shader pack authors to create separate versions of shader programs that activate after the deferred pass
issues.body:
This would avoid a number of currently unfixable issues in shader packs related to differing buffer usage patterns before and after the deferred pass.

This is most likely a requirement for hybrid deferred rendering in most shader packs, where all content before the deferred pass uses deferred rendering and all content afterwards uses forward rendering.

issues.title: Broken lighting with shadow lines.
issues.body:
### What happened?

I'm on 1.18.1 fabric with sodium 0.4.0 and iris 1.2.0. The bug causes shadows to become lines on the screen for **every** single shader pack and resource pack. However the effects are different for each. If motion blur is enabled on Sildurs, it creates cuts in the blur. However, if motion blur is enabled on BSL, objects within the cuts are blurred. This only occurs on 1.18.1. When I went to 1.19, it was perfectly fine. I am unsure on how to recreate this.

### Screenshots

Shadows on Sildurs
![2022-06-16_14 45 13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97543528/174178343-7734f248-ab9e-4f9c-b7f2-b0a862073cfa.png)
Blur on Sildurs
![2022-06-16_15 06 21](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97543528/174185153-4652c903-df0f-4729-ab7e-8d8402965287.png)
Blur on BSL
![2022-06-16_15 10 14](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97543528/174185205-6f438120-ad16-4c57-8cae-47a398527272.png)

### Relevant log output

_No response_

Minecraft 1.18.1

### Iris Version

iris-mc1.18.1-1.2.0-pre

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-mc1.18.1-0.4.0-alpha6+build.14

Windows 10

NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970

Java 17

issues.title: Croptopia crops on trees do not render correctly

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
### What happened?

When using shaders, [Croptopia](https://github.com/ExcessiveAmountsOfZombies/Croptopia)'s tree crops make the leaves behind them darker.

I'm pretty confident this is an issue with Iris as it's rendering related and happens with other shaders (less noticeably on some) and resource packs, and not a Croptopia or BSL issue.

issues.title: [feature request] Uninstaller
issues.body:
**Note for admin who doesn't read posts to the end before answering/closing:**
If you have read the whole post you would notice that the installer makes these folders/files which should be deleted if you want to uninstall Iris:
.minecraft\versions\iris-fabric-loader-0.14.6-1.19
.minecraft\iris-reserved
.minecraft\config\iris.properties

This is not a bug report but a uninstaller feature request.

Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I downloaded "Universal JAR" installer. It detected Minecraft and offered to install Iris & Sodium, 1.19, in .minecraft folder. Didn't select install as Fabric Mod. Performance dropped to unplayable 5-10 FPS.

Describe the solution you'd like
Running installer again should detect current installation and offer uninstallation.

Describe alternatives you've considered
Manually deleting files which I don't know where Iris put them.

Additional context
I am using Tlauncher with Fabric installation out of the box.

I see that there is now a new version added in .minecraft\versions\iris-fabric-loader-0.14.6-1.19
There is also a folder .minecraft\iris-reserved and .minecraft\config\iris.properties

I have deleted them all and I'm not sure if it is needed to delete something else.

issues.title: Idea: Use Batched Entity Rendering to avoid building entity geometry twice for entities visible in both the main pass and shadow pass

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Building geometry for entities is really slow. It's possible to only build the geometry once for a given entity or block entity each frame & make use of our entity batching setup, but a few things also are needed:

- Now we need 3 buffers: shadow-only, player-only, both
- We'll need to suppress beacon beams in the shadow pass differently. It's also worth checking whether hitboxes, entity shadows, text labels, and similar things should be rendered in the shadow pass at all.
- Things that violate the vanilla contract of entity renderers / block entity renderers by issuing draw calls directly will break with this system (Lifts monitors, ComputerCraft monitors) and will need to be handled separately.
- This could break some general expectations of mods as well
- The modelview matrix is currently baked into the geometry, but since it differs between the main pass and the shadow pass this would need to be changed.

Other considerations:

- The proposed Instanced Entity Rendering feature being developed as a Sodium PR could make this a lot less impactful. We would need to ensure that batched entity rendering doesn't get too entangled with Iris

issues.title: More working shaders to add to supportedshaders.md
issues.body:
I tried a lot of shaders and ended up finding 5 shaders packs that seems to work well under Iris that were not listed in [Iris/docs/supportedshaders.md](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/trunk/docs/supportedshaders.md#a-the-following-shaders-have-been-tested-and-work-well)
I tested the latest version of all listed shaders with the Fabric 1.18.2 and the latest Iris version.

[SORA Shaders](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/sora-shaders): Has a message saying it is compatible with Iris in the curseforge description.
![SORA_2022-05-21_18 52 04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62779748/169672940-73277db5-4887-4309-ab11-e37d2d74867a.jpg)

[Simplicissimus Shader](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/simplicissimus-shader):
![Simplicissimus_2022-05-21_18 47 53](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62779748/169672944-9eab16fa-b765-42e9-8941-01f03aa5b791.png)

[Beyond Belief Shaders](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/beyond-belief-shaders): Based of SEUSv11
![Beyond_Belief_2022-05-21_18 54 55](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62779748/169672946-b46d8888-1baf-4e33-a2df-6e41fc8380ed.png)

[Oceano Shaders 3.0](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/oceano-shaders):
![Oceano Shaders 3 0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62779748/169672958-fbf296f8-8137-484e-b71a-a0078ece9c48.png)

[RRe36's Shader](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/rre36s-shader): This shader is discontinued and will not have new updates, but RRe36's newer shaders all don't work in Iris. (Other than Simplicissimus, but I already listed it, and they look very different.)
![RRe36's Shader](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62779748/169672960-5905755e-9820-470e-b1da-54d320492690.png)

issues.title: Figure out how to deal with extended vertex attributes not being available
issues.body:
Iris doesn't currently provide extended vertex attributes for everything. We should figure out either how to fill in some of these holes, avoid issues that result from the missing attributes, or both.

Split off from https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/773

issues.title: Should have `gbuffers_` programs available for lightning and dragon death beams, perhaps end portals as well

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: Shader pack authors want to apply specialized effects to these things, so it would be a good idea to provide separate passes for them instead of forcing hardcoded ID checks in other programs.

issues.title: Shader options?
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Welp, I'm finally writing this. Hey, I'd like to see a "Shaders options" button which allows you to change a specific shaderpack's options. I've seen forks of iris do that, But they're all outdated now.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like a button to be added where you can change shaderpack options like in optifine.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I've considered changing back to the old fork of iris, Starline. But that isn't supported on 1.18.2 so I won't download it.

**Additional context**
Welp, Is there any more context to this?

issues.title: Separate entity batching
issues.body:
The entity batching optimization is really useful in scenarios like minigame lobbies, bringing a 1.5x and more FPS increase. The thing it, it does not really belong to Iris. 
It would be better to release it as a separate optimization mod, in case it's needed alone without the shaders functionality.

labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

labels.name: performance
labels.description: This is an issue with overall performance, but may or may not be caused by an issue in Iris.

issues.body:
### What happened?

I've posted a large bug report on the create github already found [here](https://github.com/Fabricators-of-Create/Create/issues/281).  Basically the moment shaders are enabled, there is a severe and unplayable FPS hit with the create mod running.  I'm not sure where the fault lies so I'm opening something here as well.  Getting close to the area with create entities completely pulverizes FPS and shows a large bottleneck as the GPU usages drops like a lead weight and 3D clocks don't get activated.  I use complementary v4.4 (v4.3 has the same issue and I used that since world creation).  Walking away from the create contraptions will slowly make the issue go away.  With the same seed in a new world, just a small amount of create entities already substantially hit the FPS.  I'm not sure if it's a system issue with just me, if this is expected with create and shaders (turning shadows off with small amounts of create entities helps in the test world, but in my real world it makes no difference at all).  I'm attaching the screenshots and profiler zip here that I logged there as well as quoting what I wrote in the create github bug report:

> The moment shaders are enabled, performance takes an unplayable hit resulting in an obvious bottleneck that is preventing GPU usage from increasing. The shaders I use are complementary v4.4, but I've tried a bunch of others and all result in the same problem. I've tried swapping to GravalVM and Open J9 to see if it's a Hotspot issue but nothing changed (in fact J9 made the performance plummet even more, down to literally a handful of frames). Originally I thought this world is just pushing the limits of contraptions and shaders, but upon creating a new test world with the same seed, dropping barely anything in it, the problems start to show themselves and the FPS drop is already significant.


> I have 2 kelp farm based furnage engines. a windmill, and a bunch of automated belt lines for crushing, washing, blasting, mixing and pressing. Based on some of the nutty things I've seen people build, I'm not even convinced this is "a lot". My included screenshots will show the base (in the screenshots, the large, long building is empty). I have included screenshots with the RTSS overlay showing the issue both in the "real" in use world, and the test world, made with the same seed, to show the perf without create objects in it, and with, and what contraptions I have in the world. You'll have to pardon the need to zoom in to see anything since I play at 5120x1440 so the shots are "interesting".


> When I start to walk away from the area, the screenshots will show the FPS bounce back up and eliminating the small hit printscreening does, I go back up to 70FPS and higher with shaders fully on blast once I've walked far enough away and am not looking towards the direction of the create setups. In the test world, standing still I can get up to 110+ FPS in the spot I took the screenshot in, but dropping just the schematic of the iron farm I use and the schematic of my furnace engine kelp farm setup already drops the FPS considerably, and the furnace engine setup isn't even running. Also moving close to the iron farm and walking already shows the clock speeds and usage starting to show the dropping behavior just with this stuff in it, standing still will bring it back up but moving immediately drops it. The FPS in this shot is already below 50.

> Despite having the nvidia panel set to always go to max perf, and I even have nvidia inspector Multi display power saver running telling the system to forcefully activate 3D usage with X% usage, 15% to be exact to test, although I start to wonder if the driver is overriding this, there is something holding clocking back big time as the clocks stay locked at 1350mhz in the issue, despite the usage being reported at or above the 20% mark, and as I back away from the area they slowly start to crank up. Forcing the clocks locked at 2100mhz maybe add an FPS or two but the low clocks aren't the perf problem, they are just an interesting symptom of the bottleneck.

> This is with build https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/issues/548 and Iris and sodium, and sodium's respective add-ons lithium, indium and phosphor, are all latest. I have gone back to the first working and least bug free of the early 1.18.2 builds and same thing happens with those. The log has nothing in it being spammed to indicate an issue so instead of I have launched the built in profiler and attached it here. Note, I have tested the idea that Iris and complementary's shadowing is the problem, but despite turning off real-time shadows, block and entity shadows fully off, no difference is made. Something is just really turning off Iris somewhere. Maybe my world is asking too much, maybe my system just has an issue. This funky FPS problem has left me scratching my head for I cannot pinpoint whose at fault, even if I make a test world and start blowing away contraptions the issue only really goes away fully once everything is gone.

### Screenshots

issues.title: 1.17+: Non-overridden shaders write to the shader depth buffer

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body: Since we now share the depth buffer with Minecraft, now non-overridden content can write to the shader depth buffer and break shaders. We should probably disable depth writes for non-overridden things somehow.

issues.title: Significant Performance drop when looking away from sun/moon
issues.body:
### What happened?

Framerate when looking away from sky light source is significantly lower then when it's on screen/nearly on screen. I've tested with only Iris+sodium, with both Sildur's and Complementary shaders, and in both 1.18 and 1.17. In one scene it went from 130 to 77fps, and in another lower resolution test it began at 243 and was lowered to 139 with the sun behind the player. I'm aware this might just be how Iris or shadow frustrum culling works, I don't know that much about it.

issues.title: [ Bug ] Insane frame drops + Log spam + Worlds not loading
issues.body:
### What happened?

Starting the game up with **iris 1.18.2 1.2.3** ( iris-mc1.18.2-1.2.3-build.35 ) causes the game to have horrible framerates inside menus, etc.
Worlds also won't open and shows "Saving World" after the loading screen finishes

### Screenshots

Minecraft Menu Screen
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77690119/165022165-9fc0bb7f-4238-4a8e-b868-6008db3b875d.png)
Minecraft Showing "Saving World" after the loading screen finishes
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77690119/165022191-cfa72ed5-3f38-434f-aa62-396511c8eea8.png)

### Relevant log output

issues.body:
The following error happens:
```
% java -jar brachyura-bootstrap-0.jar runMinecraftClient
Using brachyura bootstrap 0
00:27:58.222 ERROR: Task Failed
00:27:58.222 ERROR: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: error: invalid flag: --assetIndex
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main.Arguments.reportDiag(Arguments.java:889)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main.Arguments.doProcessArgs(Arguments.java:395)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main.Arguments.processArgs(Arguments.java:347)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main.Arguments.init(Arguments.java:246)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api.JavacTool.getTask(JavacTool.java:191)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api.JavacTool.getTask(JavacTool.java:119)
        at jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api.JavacTool.getTask(JavacTool.java:68)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.compiler.java.JavaCompilation.compile(JavaCompilation.java:132)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.project.java.BaseJavaProject.runRunConfig(BaseJavaProject.java:88)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.project.java.BaseJavaProject.lambda$getRunConfigTasks$1(BaseJavaProject.java:54)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.project.Task$NoArgTask.doTask(Task.java:53)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.project.BrachyuraEntry.main(BrachyuraEntry.java:45)
        at io.github.coolcrabs.brachyura.bootstrap.Main.main(Main.java:74)
```

In the .launch file there is this: `<stringAttribute key="org.eclipse.jdt.launching.PROGRAM_ARGUMENTS" value=""--assetIndex" "1.17" "--assetsDir" "/Users/douira/.brachyura/cache/minecraft/assets" "/>`. In the vscode launch config the flag also appears:

```
"args": [
        "--assetIndex",
        "1.17",
        "--assetsDir",
        "/Users/douira/.brachyura/cache/minecraft/assets"
      ],
```

The launch works through VSCode but not on the command line. @CoolMineman gave the following hint on what might be broken here:

> Ok looks like runtime flags are being passed to the compiler lmao

If this is an issue with Brachyura instead of Iris' buildscript, this issue could be migrated.

issues.title: World seems to be transparent when switching worlds on a multiplayer server
issues.body:
### What happened?

I logged onto Hypixel today after updating Fabric and Sodium and Iris, and I seem to have encountered a bug. The entire world is transparent except for entities and tile entities until I disable and then reenable my shaders. Reloading the shaders doesn't fix the issue either. I couldn't seem to reproduce this issue in singleplayer, and it also didn't happen when I only had sodium enabled.

issues.title: Iris causes aura shader in Arcanus to mess up

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
### What happened?

When using Iris, the aura shader from Arcanus will treat texture transparency as if it's opaque, when normally it would ignore it when rendering.

On top of that, Iris also causes armour to cut off the shader in weird ways, as if it's culling parts of the model but only sometimes.

Finally, when a shaderpack is enabled, the aura shader renders in front of all entities and blocks, but I'm not sure if that's something either of us can fix.

issues.title: The Iris shadow pass causes issues with some mods using Fabric's WorldRenderEvents

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
The frustum passed to callbacks during normal world rendering is the shadow frustum because the shadow pass setup terrain runs after the normal pass setup terrain code. We'll have to run setupTerrain for the shadow pass before the normal world pass to fix issues with these mods.

This seems to be at least one of the causes of issues with Litematica schematic rendering & Light Overlay.

issues.title: "Max Shadow Distance" should be a per-shaderpack setting

labels.name: area: user interface
labels.description: The parts that users interact with directly - GUI, configuration, in-chat errors, etc

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
It was mostly added as a band-aid to allow people to stop Sildur's Vibrant Shaders from rendering a ridiculous amount of chunks in the shadow pass. With the new shader config GUI, we now have a sensible place to move it to.

This would allows us to more easily address https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/834, and also likely address issues where people set their Max Shadow Distance to a certain value and then forget about it.

issues.body:
### What happened?

When setting `alphaTest.shadow=off` in shaders.properties, it doesn't apply to all shadow gbuffers programs. Specifically, it doesn't apply to `shadow_terrain_cutout`.

the attached shaderpack demonstrates this by drawing all triangles in the shadow pass to three large triangles with transparency going from 0 to 1 along the x axis. the topmost triangle consists of translucent blocks, the middle one of cutout blocks, the bottom one of solid ones.
beware, it runs very poorly and scales badly with increasing render distance.

issues.body:

Entities & block entities **significantly** affect how much GPU resource is even used.

An underlying issue appears to be in the vanilla game, but the vanilla game barely uses any GPU in the first place, which is what I'm poking at here.

If anything more GPU-side can be done, that would be great.

issues.title: Iris and Distant Horizons throw a tantrum when trying to comprehend a sheep's existence together :bruhmoment:
issues.body:
### Minecraft Version

1.18.1

### Iris Version

iris-mc1.18.1-1.2.0-pre.jar

### Sodium Version

 sodium-fabric-mc1.18.1-0.4.0-alpha6+build.14.jar

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

NVidia GTX 1660 SUPER

### Java Version

Java-17.0.1

### Reproduction Steps

1. Import these mods into whatever program you use to manage your MC Instances (I'm using the Curseforge app):
[Perf Test 1.zip](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/files/8176464/Perf.Test.1.zip)

2. Create a new world or join one you've already made
3. Spawn in some sheep (3-5 should do it)
4. Game should crash upon reopening the world OR while you're in the world placing the sheep

### Crash Report file and latest.log

```shell
Crash Report: https://pastebin.com/Hb78rp5G
Latest.log: https://pastebin.com/hUUNTk19

I refuse to put both of those into a single window, that just looks fucking awful and is annoying to read through. I would know since I've had to deal with this before when trying to help one of my friends -_-
```


### Additional context

Settings for all mods are set to their defaults for this to occur. No shaders were enabled during this crash either, not even "_Fabulous_" graphics.

"NOOO YOU CAN'T JUST CRASH ON MEEE!!1!1!" -Some kid probably

issues.title: Stained Glass broken with SEUS Renewed
issues.body:
### What happened?

Stained Glass **Panes** have proper coloring of the world behind them, but Stained Glass **Blocks** have improper coloring, most noticeable with the sky being discolored.

To replicate:
- Enable the latest version of SEUS Renewed
- Place stained glass or tinted glass **blocks**, look through them, and voila! They're broken!

*I've included a <4MB video below showing the issue.*

### Screenshots


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51380437/153733167-c0805c6e-5c8b-435b-b967-39d4dbecd792.mp4



### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Minecraft Version

Minecraft 1.18.1

### Iris Version

iris-mc1.18.1-1.2.0-pre.jar

### Sodium Version

sodium-fabric-mc1.18.1-0.4.0-alpha6+build.14.jar

### Operating System

Windows 10 Pro 21H1

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia GTX 1660-Ti (Mobile)

### Java Version

jdk-17.0.1.12-hotspot from Adoptium

### Additional context

Glass behaves properly with the latest version of OptiFine.

issues.title: Noticeable Input Lag at Framerates lower than 60

labels.name: performance
labels.description: This is an issue with overall performance, but may or may not be caused by an issue in Iris.

issues.body:
### What happened?

When using shaders that run at 60 fps or lower (mostly SEUS PTGI HRR 2.1 and Complimentary Shaders at high settings), there is a noticeable amount of input lag, with movement and mouse movement, but most noticeably with mouse movement. When using SEUS PTGI HRR 2.1 (I run about 20-40 fps with Iris), there seems to be very prevalent input lag (when I jerk my view a bit, the game camera starts moving when my mouse is stopped already). With most of the settings turned up on Complimentary Shaders (I run about 59-60 fps using Iris), the input lag is nowhere near as bad, but still there. It's not the type of input lag you see, but rather that little bit that's just enough to notice. When I play with Sodium/Iris without shaders, Optifine, or vanilla, I experience no input lag like this. I can't record with a camera, but I'll try attaching a screenshot of my F3 menu with the Shift+F3 pie chart open (now that I took the screenshot, it may not be as useful as I thought), as well as game logs.

issues.title: Iris handles datapack dimensions in a way that is inconsistent with both Vanilla and OptiFine
issues.body:
### What happened?

- Iris (and OptiFine, for reference) fail to render datapack dimensions even in "vanilla MC" in a way that minimally looks how it does and should look like in vanilla, including but not limited to dimension fixed time, sky effects, sky light and ambient light
- Iris and OptiFine dimension detection is inconsistent with each other, with (I think) OptiFine handling it better - (dimension type was set to "the_overworld" but it only had a curvature on optifine, something else was making Iris think it was The End. The last screenshot are a custom end dimension, but it is based on the overworld so that it looks less broken with shaders, so technically Iris should have probably detected it as such)
- Iris and OptiFine have drastically different visuals on the same place and settings. I guess one of the two has to be wrong?

### Screenshots

Dimension Settings for the first 3 screenshots:
daytime: 6000

issues.title: Incompatible with sodium `0.4.0-alpha6+build.12`
issues.body:
### What happened?

When the announcement in caffeinemc was sent that sodium `0.4.0-alpha6` was released, I downloaded it.
When downloading it from modrinth *at that time*, it gave me sodium version `0.4.0-alpha6+build.12`.

I had issues with mods last night but was too lazy to fix them.

This morning, when updating iris, I attempted to run it with version `0.4.0-alpha6+build.12` of sodium.
It did not allow the game to launch with this.

Upon checking the decompiled class file, it is looking for the *exact* sodium version `0.4.0-alpha6+build.14`. Because of this, it seems that it doesn't want to match version `0.4.0-alpha6+build.12`.

After checking the modrinth, it seems that I now download sodium version `0.4.0-alpha6+build.14`. Due to this, I'm inclined to believe that the version on modrinth was updated. I have not checked for curseforge.

A fix for this issue would be to change [`AllowedSodiumVersion.exact("0.4.0-alpha6+build.14")`](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/1.18.x/1.1.5/src/main/java/net/coderbot/iris/compat/sodium/SodiumVersionCheck.java#L9) to `AllowedSodiumVersion.prefix("0.4.0-alpha6")`.

Iris should not depend on a specific build of sodium.
What if someone were to build sodium from source? If they were to do so at the same commit that this requires, it would not be allowed to launch.

issues.title: Requesting Error Messages on Shader Errors
issues.body: As an option, error messages should be displayed to help shaderpack developers (and end-users) diagnose and solve errors. Optifine has a similar feature to this, which leads shaderpack developers to use it during development rather than IRIS. Since IRIS gives worlds better performance than Optifine and is gathering a ton of support, modern shaderpacks *should* be designed for IRIS.

issues.title: Decreased performance when breaking filled chest

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
### What happened?

Release notes for 1.1.4 said:
> Fixed a performance drop with shaders disabled compared to base Sodium - Iris with shaders off should no longer measurably decrease performance

Unfortunately, Iris still notably affects performance in disabled state.

My test case is breaking a single chest filled with items and then picking them up. I tested in Singleplayer Creative, standing far enough from the chest so that I don't pick up any of the items right after breaking the chest. Then I ran into the items to pick them up.

1) Water Bottles (ie. a single item per chest slot)
With Sodium, breaking a chest full of Water Bottles wasn't noticeable at all.
Picking them up wasn't noticeable at all.
With Sodium + Iris, breaking a chest full of Water Bottles caused only a small hiccup.
Picking them up also caused a small hiccup.

2) Nether Wart (ie. 64 items per chest slot)
With Sodium, breaking a chest full of Nether Wart caused a small hiccup.
Picking them up also caused a small hiccup.
With Sodium + Iris, breaking a chest full of Nether Wart caused about a 1s lag.
Picking them up literally froze my game for 2 seconds.

issues.title: More diverse Noise Function
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Having to implement Custom Noise takes up a valuable colortex Channel, so it would be best to pack as much into a single tex as possible.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
 I propose creating a custom noisetex that combines the random noise used currently in thel, a random perlin heightmap for smooth noise when that is required in the alpha channel and a 2 channel normal map of that noise to get faster normals (e.g. for wave genereation). using .r and .g for normals is the most common implementation so i would stick to that, put the heightmap into .b and the old Random.nextBytes into .a

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If using a vec4 noisetex is impractical, the normalmap can be left out, and instead replaced with something like simplex or brownian noise, or a musgrave/voronoi texture as those have applications aswell.

**Additional context**
3 Channels of the same Noisetype is pretty redundant, as you could always just sample again at a shifted location instead of using a second channel. The performance difference can be neglected.

issues.title: Cascaded Shadow Maps

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This feature would mitigate the problem of needing high resolution shadow maps for smooth sharp shadows that decrease performance.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add support for multiple shadow maps in the shaders properties file. A shader properties could define multiple shadow maps and use each of them for cascaded shadow maps.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**
Cascaded shadow maps are documented at https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dxtecharts/cascaded-shadow-maps.
There is a feature request for optifine to add cascaded shadow maps at sp614x/optifine#659.
This feature is implemented in [vram-guild/canvas](https://github.com/vram-guild/canvas)

issues.title: Optifine Shader Options in Shader Menu
issues.body:
Hi,

I've been using this mod for awhile now and I've noticed the lack of the normal Optifine shader which really irritates me due to this mod being compatible with normal Optifine shaders and the lack of Shader Options either makes it difficult or impossible to modify the settings of shaders.

I would find some way of implementing it as either a work around or something similar to how normal Optifine reads and writes to the shader options.

issues.title: Launching installer prompts a blank window on linux
issues.body:
### **Description of the issue :** 
a white window pops up in place of the installer when executing the installer's jar file through bash


### **Steps to reproduce the issue :** 
- input "java -jar Iris-Installer-2.0.3.jar" in the command line in a wayland session (haven't tested if the issue is present when using X11) and press enter
- a blank window pops up


### **System specs :** 
- **OS :** arch linux with kernel 5.15.7-arch1-1
- **DE/WM :** wayland with sway (xwayland is installed for compatibility with x applications).
- **Shell :** bash 5.1.12



## screenshot of the aforementioned issue : 
![screenshot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43518872/147353432-6415b539-b0c1-439c-9ab9-d32fe7396354.png)


Please tell me the steps I have to take in order to provide the information you need.

issues.title: Compatibility with SEUS V10 RC2 (Revived) and RC6

labels.name: pack: seus
labels.description: SEUS-specific issue / only observable with SEUS

issues.body:
Hello!
It's a weird issue that I create here and I will try my best to explain it:
The SEUS RC6 shaders can be loaded on the latest optifine version, but they are totally broken and look like this: 
![2021-12-24_11 12 57](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32510957/147344457-dc6a9da9-ff97-4607-bd37-d051f5fe51b1.png)
Instead of this (screenshot taken in 1.4.7)
![2021-12-23_12 43 05](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32510957/147344480-174a9a56-d2c3-4167-b576-2e322d0617c9.png)
On Iris, the shader just looks like vanilla Minecraft.
So as you can see, water and moving leaves work. The problem is the shadows etc. I create this issue because this shader with Optifine was at the beginning not working at all, and over the years it became more and more compatible (water started working, no lines between chunks etc.) so I was wondering if it was possible to make this shader work again on modern versions of Minecraft.

This also applies to SEUS RC2 that had a "Revived" shaderpack made by robobo meant to be compatible with MC Optifine 1.8/1.9, but it's not working anymore since 1.17.1 and now looks like this (very similiar lightning issue)
![2021-12-24_11 15 45](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32510957/147344848-1a37653a-9dc1-428f-ad0a-e0c62c3ef859.png)

Hope it's possible to make these shaders work again, I loved them!

issues.title: Night Vision Compatibility Fix causes 1.18.x branch to spam errors.
issues.body:
### What happened?

When attempting to use Night Vision Flash Be Gone along with Iris in a 1.18.x environment, Instead of the game crashing this time; 

It instead will produce a spamming list of errors in latest.log file - Causing it to grow endlessly and locking the client in place; forcing user to kill the java process with task manager/command line.

(Starts spamming as soon as first "Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.class_746.method_31548()" because "this.field_3690.field_1724" is null" is mentioned in logs)

### Screenshots

Cannot produce any screenshots - Only thing i can say is that the client will become locked upon attempting to join worlds.

### Relevant log output

issues.title: [Request] Add some opacity to the buttons on the upcoming GUI
issues.body:
![transp](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25572454/147122151-486469fe-c6d3-4543-8ba0-075399f8fac2.gif)
Hi, if possible, please make the Iris UI buttons darker, I think most people will agree they will look nicer and be significantly more readable with that, otherwise users might have issues in the future on bright backgrounds.
The GIF above should make a comparison of how it is and how it could be
_(Got the screenshot from someone else just as an example and edited it in paint, don't mind it too much)_

This was tested with the Fabric Loader using sodium, phosphorous and Lithium

issues.title: Emmisive Texture Support
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There is no Optifine format emmisive texture mods for Fabric. The closest are Continuity (which adds Optifine connected textures) and CTM Fabric (which implements a different format). [When I requested the devs of Continuity](https://github.com/PepperCode1/Continuity/issues/7) implemented emmisive textures, they said they were unable to due to API limitations. With how Iris already works, I think that it can bypass the limitations that the devs mentioned.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like Iris to add support for Optifine Emmisive textures.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using CTM Fabric texture packs.

issues.title: Memory barriers are missing for image load/store
issues.body:
Image load / store follows the rules of incoherent memory access: https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Memory_Model#Incoherent_memory_access

As a result, we need to manually ensure that the results of writes are visible to other shader programs.

https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Memory_Model#Ensuring_visibility

https://www.khronos.org/opengl/wiki/Memory_Model#External_visibility

TL;DR we need to figure out when to call `glMemoryBarrier()` and figure out the flags we need to call it with. Currently image load store in Iris isn't fully usable because you can't actually 100% rely on stored values being available in other programs yet. Figuring out the optimal time to issue memory barriers might be complex if it involves figuring out when a shader program is making use of data written by image load store in another program.

issues.title: Iris with shaders disabled in addition to Sodium causes a performance drop compared to just Sodium
issues.body:
### What happened?

Comparing on 1.17.1. Test world with no entities present at all (all mobs killed, no item frames, no chests, etc)

sodium 0.3.3 (no iris), gpu usage is at 96% @ 921Mhz (cpu has headroom and can operate as low as 1.58Ghz without fps dropping, max frequency is 2.091Ghz)
resulting fps is 169fps stable

sodium 0.3.3 + iris 1.1.3, gpu usage also 96% @921Mhz (cpu has headroom and can operate as low as 1.58Ghz without fps dropping, max frequency is 2.091Ghz)
resulting fps is 150fps stable

so a 10% performance drop from just adding iris (no settings changed). It seems like iris must be creating additional gpu work (since the gpu is the bottleneck in both cases) even without any shaders present. I think users would expect that disabling shaders would make performance match sodium without iris but this is not the case.

issues.title: Low priority: Iris for MC 1.18 without Sodium has suboptimal / weird / potentially buggy shadow culling behavior

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
1.18 completely changed how chunk iteration works, moving most of the iteration into an off thread that asynchronously updates the chunk graph, and separating out frustum culling into a separate function that can be applied to that chunk graph on the main thread, but Iris for 1.18 appears to have not been changed at all to account for this. This works with Sodium because Sodium overwrites that rendering pathway.

Thanks to @qouteall for pointing this out.

issues.body:
### What happened?

One player casts a fishing rod, which draws a line from the end of a rod to the bobber, as expected. When a second player casts, it draws the expected line as well as an extra, straight black line from one player's bobber to the other's fishing rod.

Not captured in screenshot, but as more players join in, more lines appear. 

The line is always drawn from the oldest cast fishing rod to the newer bobber, then from that player's rod to the bobber next in the age order, and so on.

issues.title: Some shader packs (Chocapic v7/v8/v9, Kappa, etc) do not work

labels.name: type: shader pack compatibility
labels.description: An issue regarding a request for support / compatibility with a shader pack

issues.body:
Iris is not a complete shader mod implementation, and as a result, some packs that use features that Iris does not support do not work at all on Iris, and show a black / solid-colored screen, revert to vanilla rendering ("fallback"), or have similar issues. We've decided to collect some of the common requested packs into a list to avoid many non-actionable issues being created regarding these packs not working on Iris.

While these packs will all be supported eventually, currently Iris does not support them. **Please don't open additional issues regarding the packs listed below along the lines of "this pack black screens" unless you have additional information to add about the cause.**

- [x] Chocapic13 v7
- [x] Chocapic13 v8
- [x] Chocapic13 v9
- [x] Chocapic13 HighPerformance Toaster
- [x] Nostalgia
- [x] NostalgiaVX
- [x] MollyVX
- [x] ApolloRT
- [x] Spectrum: https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1029
- [x] [Simplicissimus](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/simplicissimus-shader) (appears to be very close to working, mainly needs custom uniforms)
- [x] [Wisdom Shaders](https://github.com/bobcao3/Wisdom-Shaders)
- [ ] [NV Shaders](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/customization/nv-shaders)
- [x] Super Duper Vanilla Shaders (needs custom uniforms, maybe more)
- [x] [Chronos](https://www.patreon.com/user?u=49201970)
- [ ] [Magnificent](https://www.patreon.com/posts/magnificent-57042663)
- [ ] [OctrayRewrite](https://www.patreon.com/BruceKnowsHow)

As a prerequisite, almost all of these packs heavily rely on custom uniforms (https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1027) being supported by Iris, and it's likely that further investigation into their issues might not be worthwhile until custom uniforms are fully working.

labels.name: status: fixed in next release
labels.description: This issue will be fixed in the next release of Iris

labels.name: type: shader pack compatibility
labels.description: An issue regarding a request for support / compatibility with a shader pack

issues.body:
This is a list of things needed to be fixed before Spectrum can work. Note that this is not a complete list, there might be things we don't know about. It represents a *minimum* of what needs to be supported as a result.

issues.title: Consider using Brachyura as a replacement for Gradle + Fabric Loom
issues.body:
[Brachyura](https://github.com/CoolCrabs/brachyura) is a build tool created from the ground up to work for Minecraft modding. It is a Gradle + Fabric Loom replacement that aims to be efficient and allow the user to create fast and easy-to-debug build scripts.

While Gradle and Fabric Loom have been *functional* for Iris thus far, it's pretty obvious while using them that Gradle was never really designed to accommodate Minecraft modding. While it has improved in this respect more recently, we still have a number of day-to-day issues that come up.

More significantly, Gradle is incredibly complex software with many layers of abstraction and indirection, making it extremely challenging to debug. The practical implication of this is that even though both Gradle and Fabric Loom are open-source software, if issues come up we're entirely reliant on others to go in and fix these issues. Brachyura promises to address these issues by having a much more straighforward project organization, using conventional Java for buildscripts, and being focused around Minecraft modding instead of having modding being something tacked on to it with plugins.

Considerations:

- JitPack will not recognize Brachyura by default (notably, Immersive Portals relies on Iris being available through JitPack), however we can create a configuration file to tell JitPack how to compile our project: https://github.com/jitpack/jitpack.io/blob/master/BUILDING.md#custom-commands
- Brachyura won't be recognized by most IDEs by default, however, it will have the ability to generate project configuration files for most of the popular / relevant IDEs.
- Brachyura is still in an early stage, so at the current stage of development it *could* end up causing more issues for us than Gradle + Fabric Loom. Hopefully these issues will go away, and the remaining ones will be simpler to debug and resolve.
- ~~While Brachyura does make most of its external dependencies very clear, its bootstrap phase does rely on a modder's personal maven server (`maven.hydos.cf`), and we would rather avoid relying on the personal maven servers of any modders due to poor experiences in the past. Generally, we prefer for our libraries to be available on Maven Central or a repository of similar reliability, or vendored into the Iris repository.~~ This is now fixed.

issues.body:
Referencing Minecraft classes in the shaderpack loader is very fragile when it comes to running our test framework, and this is a legacy hold over. Luckily, forkless Sodium makes this refactor simpler to carry out.

Fixing this will help let GitHub Actions pass on the 1.17+ branches again, but we still need to address https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/1081

issues.title: Consider changing the mod package to net.irisshaders.iris instead of net.coderbot.iris
issues.body:
Back when Iris first started, I was the only real developer, and sorta just chose `net.coderbot.iris` as an initial package. While I'm still the lead developer, the project has grown to have many contributors other than myself.

Reasons to change the package:
- `irisshaders.net` is an actual domain that we own. `net.coderbot` on the other hand is not an actual domain - this isn't in line with Java package standards.
- It's more professional to not have the code packaged under the name of an individual developer of the project if the project is jointly developed by multiple people.

Reasons to not change the package / considerations to be done while changing the package:
- Mods referencing the internal API of Iris will break with this change. Mods shouldn't reference the internal Iris API, but without any sort of public API they don't really have a choice. We'll want to add a public API and give time to migrate first.
- This could seriously mess up the Git history of many files if not done correctly. Git handles mass renames and moves like this, but it doesn't love them. We should pair this with a separate distinct large-scale reorganization of the Iris source code to minimize how much we mess up the Git history over the course of the project.

issues.title: Iris should use an optimized vertex writer implementation when running with Sodium
issues.body: Currently, Iris uses Java NIO for vertex writing when building chunks with Sodium, which is fast enough, but it could be faster if we used Unsafe or LWJGL MemoryUtil. This is mainly a reminder and won't be implemented until we can address code duplication issues.

issues.title: quad in fullscreen programs has wrong vertex coordinates
issues.body:
### Expected Behavior
The quad's vertex coordinates should be provided in the range [0, 1] and then transformed to [-1, 1] in the vertex shader using the normal transformation matrices: `gl_ModelViewProjectionMatrix * gl_Vertex`
A common optimization (which does the exact same thing) is this: `vec4(gl_Vertex.xy * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)`

### Actual Behavior
Iris' quad coordinates already range from -1 to 1, and the model/view/projection matrices seem to be identity matrices. The optimization incorrectly positions the quad. A workaround is simply using `vec4(gl_Vertex.xy, 0.0, 1.0)`.

Yes

Radeon RX590

java 16

1. either adventurez or eldritch mobs mod present
2. night tme

issues.title: Add A Feature for "Emissive Textures" For Optifine Parity
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
So Optifine, one of the best Shader client mods with one problem: Performance
and as we all know Iris aims to solve that problem, but so far, It has way less features than Optifine has. 
Optifine has a feature for Vanilla Shaders, to make some textures be able to have a glowing effect, an effect like Enderman's eyes, but for blocks, the fire in the furnace has a glow, separate than the rest of the texture. it also adds support with it for resource packs and mods. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

**What ARE Emissive Textures Exactly?**
Emissive textures are overlay textures that glow in the dark. They can be added to basically any texture using Optifine. Resource pack creators can choose to make an entire texture emissive, or just elements of a texture.

issues.title: Complementary white borders with Emissive Ores
issues.body:
### What happened?

When using Iris, I have white borders around the glowing parts in diamond ore.
This issue does not persist in OptiFine. It also goes away when specular reflections are turned on.

issues.title: The Iris Sodium fork should explicitly mark old Drip Sounds versions as incompatible
issues.body: They cause a very peculiar crash like this that is otherwise hard to debug: https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/655. Newer versions of Drip Sounds fix the issue, but users might not know that they have to upgrade.

issues.title: Iris should detect when it is valid to apply conventional frustum culling in the shadow pass

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: If we can figure out that the shadow program isn't doing any complex non-linear transformations, conventional frustum culling with the shadow model view & shadow projection matrix should work just fine.

issues.title: Iris should support occlusion culling in the shadow pass somehow

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body: Advanced Shadow Frustum Culling in Iris 1.1.2 is pretty much the best we can do with normal frustum culling techniques. Occlusion culling is needed to improve culling. Obviously, it doesn't work with voxelization. Though, it does work with the sun-bounce GI in SEUS.

Unlike staying true to vanilla's (superior) implementation of the fix for https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MC-3366, the end portal bottom is rendered as if the portal block's hitbox extends all the way to the bottom of the block space (which was the case for 1.16 and below), instead of only half way (which is how it works in 1.17 and above). This not only looks worse than vanilla, but also lets the player clip their camera inside of the end portal texture without being teleported, as demonstrated by this video. https://youtu.be/Z6LDzzPZVis

### Screenshots

![2021-09-10_18 15 24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68349758/132924469-c6095482-8899-4467-8b14-27d29bfc7543.png)

![2021-09-10_18 24 09](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68349758/132924472-3a54325e-eda0-4fd8-8503-11b88a9170b3.png)


### Relevant log output

_No response_

Minecraft 1.17.1, Iris 1.1.2

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

Yes

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

GTX 1050 Ti

### Java Version

Java 16

issues.title: Vanilla-Like Settings GUI
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Just my own irritation that the iris menu is inconsistent compared to other minecraft menu's. The shaders menu even goes back to vanilla gui style! Its inconsistent even within itself.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A more vanilla-like gui option, so that the menu fits with the other settings gui's. It will just seem more coherent and a bit easier to get around, rather than learning a new arbitrary menu type that only one mod (afaik) uses. Its not like the current menu is hard to get around / learn, but rather is something that shouldn't have to be done in the first place.
Id be happy with even just keeping the general layout you currently have, but replace the buttons with minecraft buttons and sliders.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
No reasonable alternatives.

**Additional context**
The menu I would like to be more in line with vanilla menu's (as well as the other sub menu's; Quality and Advanced)

issues.title: Iris should not use IrisRenderLayerWrapper on 1.17

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

labels.name: version: 1.17+
labels.description: This issue only affects Iris on 1.17+

issues.body:
On 1.16 this was needed in order to associate a shader program with a given render layer, but on 1.17 this isn't necessary because vanilla already does that with the 1.17 core shaders.

This causes problems with Satin, which has to hack around internal Iris code in order to enable the copying and modification of vanilla render layers:

* https://github.com/Ladysnake/Satin/commit/2e5846fc98a44db53e6a6108932b5f6ae47e604c
