issues.title: [Immersive Portals] Audit references to Iris from Immersive Portals

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
It would be preferable to see if all references to internal Iris code can either be handled within Iris or be replaced with proper APIs. This would avoid having Immersive Portals break with internal Iris refactors.

---

This reference is because Immersive Portals tries to patch the shaders that Iris provides (see https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/issues/805):

* https://github.com/qouteall/ImmersivePortalsMod/blob/599ce5e1f6e531d5cfee8e57578f269c77c92b91/imm_ptl_core/src/main/java/qouteall/imm_ptl/core/compat/sodium_compatibility/mixin/MixinIrisSodiumSodiumTerrainPipeline.java

These references are only needed since Iris updates SystemTimeUniforms in GameRenderer#render instead of GameRenderer#renderWorld, this should be fixable within Iris:

* https://github.com/qouteall/ImmersivePortalsMod/blob/f918113eed2f58289f5f4c0474542ff05762cf02/imm_ptl_core/src/main/java/qouteall/imm_ptl/core/compat/iris_compatibility/IrisCompatibilityPortalRenderer.java#L114
* https://github.com/qouteall/ImmersivePortalsMod/blob/f918113eed2f58289f5f4c0474542ff05762cf02/imm_ptl_core/src/main/java/qouteall/imm_ptl/core/compat/iris_compatibility/IrisPortalRenderer.java#L293

This reference is needed to save/restore the WorldRenderer.pipeline object cached by Iris during world rendering:

* https://github.com/qouteall/ImmersivePortalsMod/blob/fab9064e3d3fcd1061e584bd8503702122089003/imm_ptl_core/src/main/java/qouteall/imm_ptl/core/render/MyGameRenderer.java

This reference helps with saving/restoring the pipeline field, but also allows Immersive Portals to check if Iris is using shaders for rendering.

* https://github.com/qouteall/ImmersivePortalsMod/blob/f918113eed2f58289f5f4c0474542ff05762cf02/imm_ptl_core/src/main/java/qouteall/imm_ptl/core/compat/iris_compatibility/IrisInterface.java

labels.name: mod compatibility

labels.name: status: underlying issue identified
labels.description: A root cause of the issue has been identified (only devs should add this tag)

issues.body:
Only one pipeline is created for each dimension. However, with non-clearing buffers & uniforms like previousCameraPosition, state that is intended to refer to the previous frame from a given viewpoint ends up referring to state from the same frame from a different viewpoint. Naturally, this severely breaks TAA.

According to qouteall, it should be possible to separately track previous frame data for different logical viewports:

> IP uses List<UUID> to discriminate the different logical viewpoints. List contains the portal UUIDs from outer to inner. IP uses that to do portal visibility prediction optimization.

issues.title: Iris should support CIT
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Custom Item Textures and Custom Entity Models are Optifine options for texture packs that allow resource pack creators to add custom changes textures based on a text file.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be nice if CIT and CEM could be implemented in Iris

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Optifine has a working CIT implementation, but Optifine is slow and not open-source.

**Additional context**
The main reason Optifine is valued by map and resource pack creators is for its implementation of CIT.

issues.title: Iris should apply patches to shaders to fix driver compatibility issues
Ensure that all vertex attribute / sampler inputs always have valid values
issues.body:
Some render types in Minecraft don't provide a valid base texture (texture/gtexture/tex) or lightmap. They might also not provide valid texture coordinates, lightmap coordinates, vertex normals, or similar.

Where existing code doesn't provide these values, Iris should provide placeholders so that code using these values works as expected.

- texture/gtexture/tex: A 1x1 white pixel
- lightmap: The lightmap texture, as expected
- gl_MultiTexCoord0: (0.5, 0.5)
- gl_MultiTexCoord1: (240, 240)

These placeholder values should make shader packs work as expected more often. It's needed for lines to properly cast shadows with BSL / Complementary and for enchantment glints to work with Sildur's Enhanced Default, for example.

issues.title: Support loading the gbuffers_lines program
issues.body:
This program was added as part of OptiFine's attempts to get lines to render properly with 1.17's new line rendering methods. While we now have a way of patching gbuffers_basic to work properly with line rendering, it's possible that some shaderpacks might want to provide their own program.

In addition, it would make sense to give access to the proper variables and inputs needed for shader packs to handle the new line rendering themselves.

issues.title: Add a way to dismiss the "Sodium isn't installed, you will have poor performance"
issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Because I have a Mac with an M1 chip, I've found that removing Sodium from Iris's JAR actually improves performance (see [this conversation in Discord](https://discord.com/channels/774352792659820594/849360601267830825/877471788534206496)). However, because I removed it, this means that whenever I run shaders I get a big warning that says "Sodium Isn't installed, you will have poor performance". I'd like to be able to dismiss this message since it obstructs important parts of my HUD and it doesn't apply in my (admittedly niche) case. 
## Describe the solution you'd like
I'd like to be able to toggle this message. I understand that it is useful for most people, but it isn't useful for me, it's just getting in the way. Ideally it would be a toggle in the shader packs selection screen, but if that is too accessible I wouldn't mind an obscure toggle hidden away, or even having to modify something in fabric-mod.json, I just don't want to have to modify raw code because I'll just break it.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
The only alternative I can think of is having a list of graphics cards that are worse with Sodium installed, and not display the warning if one of them is detected. I think my original suggestion of a toggle or even an obscure setting would be much better though.
## Additional context
In case anyone doesn't believe me about Sodium performance being worse, here are comparison images (also available in the Discord conversation linked above):

issues.title: [Feature request] Support changing render quality / render resolution, as well as dynamic resolution

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, Minecraft's render resolution is tied to window/screen size, and not configurable.
Newer laptops have denser displays, yet they do often have low power iGPUs and little battery capacity and those 1080p pixels aren't that worthy of computing. A dynamic resolution or fixed resolution that reduce power usage and improve battery life would be a great addition to Minecraft Java Edition. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Iris should implement a dynamic and/or fixed resolution system:
- Fixed resolution by far is the most straightforward here, Iris gets configured to render the game at a certain resolution, but not the UI.
- Dynamic resolution is the trickiest, there are two points to look up on mobile devices: power usage and poopness of iGPUs. Ya know how dynamic resolution works, if a target FPS isn't reached, lower the resolution until it reaches the target FPS or a lower bound, this *should work* as mobile SoCs do throttle and give feedback by how bad the game is running.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Set the whole system screen res lower LoL.

**Additional context**
None really, the feature request addresses common day to day issues with laptops and low power computers in general.
Oh, my laptop doesn't reach 60fps with shaders and 1080p res without a dangerous boost during a 46°C summer.

issues.title: name tags turn red when using font and shader
issues.body:
### What happened?

When using [Fabulously Optimized (beta 2)](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/modpacks/fabulously-optimized) with [sildurs shaders](https://sildurs-shaders.github.io/) and then adding this [roboto font](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/hd-font-roboto) it makes all nametags (player and animals) red and have a black fill.
If I turn off either the font or the shader it goes back to white.

Brought this issue up with the font pack creator and [they said](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/hd-font-roboto?comment=31) it seemed like an iris bug. 

### Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7709438/128617740-68f3b130-8d6c-4974-b65f-2497719dee36.png)


### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Iris and Minecraft Version

Minecraft 1.17.1, Fabric 0.11.6, Iris 1.1.1, Fabulously Optimized-2.1.0-beta.2

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

Yes

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia GTX1070Ti

### Java Version

Java 16

_No response_

issues.title: iris mod spams log when font resource pack is applied
issues.body:
### What happened?

when font resource pack is applied, iris spams log with this:
` [Render thread/WARN]: Iris has detected a non-wrapped render layer, it will not be rendered with the correct shader program: text_intensity `
this message should be logged only one time, but it does as much as it can.
this logged 17940 lines in 31 secs, around 578 lines per second.
log spam can be a big issue not only in debugging, even in long-time gameplay.
this problem never happend again after i got rid of font mod.

issues.title: Iris should use Mojang Mappings instead of Yarn Mappings
issues.body:
Moving to Mojang mappings ("Mojmap") has some important upsides over using Yarn mappings ("Yarn"):

1. **Consistent name quality.** Though there are some weird names in Mojmap, these names aren't incorrect, they're just a bit awkward to work with when they come up. Overall, nearly every name in Mojmap is "acceptably accurate." Meanwhile, a number of names in Yarn (especially in the 1.17 rendering areas) are blatantly incorrect. The absolute worst example was the swapping of `bind()` and `unbind()` on `Shader`, which means that updating mappings will silently introduce bugs into Iris!!!! This is completely unacceptable.

2. **Not closely connected to any specific toolchain.** Yarn mappings are very closely tied to the Fabric toolchain, and as a result Iris is completely reliant on the continued updating of Yarn mappings to each new version of the game. If the unpaid volunteers maintaining Yarn decide to disappear, we're screwed! While Mojang could decide to stop updating Mojmap, I find that to be a lot less likely.
    Mojang mappings have gradually become a community standard. Modern versions of Forge now plan to use them by default, Fabric supports Mojang mappings, Quilt might use them by default, or at the very least it will support them, etc. There's also some interesting possibilities with projects like [VanillaGradle](https://github.com/SpongePowered/VanillaGradle) which offer an incredibly barebones toolchain for working with Minecraft using Mojang mappings.
    In short, using Mojang mappings gives us *options*, whereas Yarn locks us in to the Fabric toolchain.

3. **Instant mapping updates.** Mojang releases the new Mojmap file with each new update - it's unnecessary to wait for mappings to update since the updated mappings are shipped alongside updates.

4. **Name stability.** Yarn names change periodically as people refine mappings. While this is nice, since the changes often aren't backported, it makes it more annoying to maintain Iris for multiple versions.

Of course, some people will object to this. Here's my responses to some common criticisms:

1. **Mojang mappings are restrictively licensed!** Guess what? Minecraft is restrictively licensed too! People seem to forget that it's not an open source game. Using Mojang mappings to create mods for Minecraft doesn't have a huge practical difference from using Yarn mappings to create mods for Minecraft. Either way, we're modifying Mojang's game in a way that they've explicitly allowed us to in the EULA. Some have tried to point out subtleties in Mojang's mappings license that supposedly prove that you cant use them for modding. In reality, Mojang's intent is clear - they want to bring the modding community together by getting everyone to use the same mappings set.

2. **Changing mappings will break open PRs!** You're absolutely right, which is why this change won't be made until most big important PRs have been merged and things have stabilized. It will certainly happen before Minecraft 1.18 releases since updating to newer versions of Yarn is dangerous and could easily introduce bugs.

3. **Yarn contributors will no longer be able to contribute to Iris / read Iris source code without seeing Mojmap!** This isn't a big deal since the intersection between "people who contribute to Yarn" and "people who contribute to Iris" is basically nil. If they want to read through Iris's code, one option is to import it into their development environment as a dependency, where it will automatically be remapped to Yarn. Again, it doesn't make much sense to inhibit the development of Iris over this small group of people.

4. **Why don't you just contribute fixed names to Yarn?** I'd rather spend time developing mods instead of bikeshedding mappings. Migrating to Mojang mappings is a one-time cost, fixing Yarn mappings is a continuous time sink.

If you decide to respond to this issue, please actually read it in full. People who just come here to spam objections without reading my reasoning in full will be removed from the issue tracker. I understand that using Mojang mappings is somewhat controversial in the Fabric community right now, and I hope that people take the time to read and understand my reasoning here. Thanks.

issues.title: Iris shouldn't spam the log so much

labels.name: high priority
labels.description: This issue is encountered frequently and needs to be fixed quickly

issues.body: Iris has a lot of logspam, making it hard to actually pick out important things. I'd like to make it a lot less spammy. In particular, it shouldn't print out patched shader source code to the console in a development environment, but it could print it to a folder of patched shader files for debugging.

issues.title: Iris should support shader pack options / configuration
issues.body:
A common user request is the ability to customize shaders through a settings menu.

**This is by far the most requested feature for Iris - please do not create additional issues on the topic, or ask for ETAs ("shader option support when?"). We fully intend to support it, but these things just take time. Shader option support will be added when it's ready.**

If you'd like to express support for this feature, feel free to add a "thumbs up" reaction below.

We are aware that there are experimental forks of Iris that try to add shader option support. They all use the same core implementation of option detection & modification, but unfortunately that core implementation has a fatal design flaw that causes it to severely break shader packs when you toggle some options. This underlying code cannot be used by Iris - it must be rewritten, which is in progress.

A few big things need to happen first:

1. Support for detecting these options from shader packs, applying them, and the user's modified values from a .txt configuration file. I am gradually working on an implementation of this system in private.
2. A shader pack GUI. FoundationGames & Justsnoopy30 have a prototype of what this might look like.
3. Support for the underlying features required by the options in the packs that we're focusing on supporting. Often, enabling certain options makes shader packs use features that Iris does not currently support. I would like to ensure that all options work properly first, because it's rather lame to have a shader option system implemented if half of the options cause things to explode.
4. Support for parsing shader directives (like `/* DRAWBUFFERS */`) from the final preprocessed source file. This is needed for packs that change what buffers they write to based on configuration. See #540.

issues.title: Crash using a shader pack with a custom noise texture set to a built-in texture
issues.body:
Reproduction steps: Create a shaders.properties file with the following content

```
texture.noise=minecraft:dynamic/lightmap_1
```

Iris crashes while initializing the ShaderPack because it tries to read the noise texture through interpreting that as a file path, when it's actually a texture location.

iris-mc1.17-1.1.0 and sodium-fabric-mc1.17-0.3.0+IRIS1-rev.7491e3a for 1.17.1

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

Yes

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

RTX 3090

### Java Version

Java 16.0.1

### Reproduction Steps

1. Join a Single Player or Multiplayer world
2. Fly around in spectator mode

### Additional context

Since the leak is in the OpenGL side Minecraft JVM memory settings don't affect it (other than decreasing JVM memory will somewhat delay the crash).

I've tested this with no other mods than Iris, Sodium and Fabric API so I can say for certain that the problem for me is within the modified Sodium.
I've also tested Iris standalone (no issues) and regular Sodium (no issues).
From what I read, Sodium might've had a similar issue recently, which was supposedly patched in the latest version (and as said didn't cause any problems for me on the regular Sodium).

For me the crash usually occurs when the remaining memory drops under 1 GB.

Sorry for not having a better crash report or log, but the issue should be reproducable easily enough. Maybe set Minecraft JVM memory very high to induce the crash quicker?

issues.title: memory accumulation when loading a lot of chunks
issues.body:
When loading a lot of chunks, systems memory gets accumulated and doesn't decrease. After a while Minecraft crashes due to "Out of Memory".

I have tested this phenomenon with vanilla mc, just Fabric, Fabric with mods and Fabric with Iris Shaders (Shaders on and off).
But only with Iris Shaders I encountered this problem.

I am able to reproduce this the best when traveling through a nether portal over and over.
Every time I jump between worlds ± 200MB gets accumulated.

My system:
I7 10th gen
16GB DDR4 RAM

Minecraft settings:
JVM Arguments: -Xmx4G
Graphics: Fancy

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

Yes

### Operating System

Windows 10

Nvidia GTX 1660 TI

### Java Version

issues.title: Incorrect time in dimensions with fixed time
issues.body:
### What happened?

In a dimension with a fixed time the shader will use the time in the overworld instead of the time of the dimension you are in. This can result in night time in a perma-day world.

To reproduce: 
1. Create a new world and install the attached datapack ( [fixed_time.zip](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/files/6823263/fixed_time.zip) )
2. Go to the alternative dimension by running `/execute in suppergerrie2:fixed_time run tp @s ~ 64 ~`
3. Run `/time set night` and `/time set day` both with shaders enabled and disabled
4. Observe how with shaders disabled the sun does not change but with shaders enabled the sky changes based on the overworld time.



### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Iris and Minecraft Version

iris-mc1.17-1.1.0+rev.01d8631 (latest commit on 1.17 branch at time of writing)

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

No

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060

### Java Version

Java 16

### Additional context

The issue is caused by [WorldTimeUniforms#getWorldDayTime](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/01d8631f1887a055a8305d9aef3eb93f69e29364/src/main/java/net/coderbot/iris/uniforms/WorldTimeUniforms.java#L28-L33) and [HardcodedCustomUniforms#getWorldDayTime](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/01d8631f1887a055a8305d9aef3eb93f69e29364/src/main/java/net/coderbot/iris/uniforms/HardcodedCustomUniforms.java#L27-L32).

These need to be fixed to take the fixed time into account. The only way I've found to get the fixed time is by adding an accessor for DimensionType.fixedTime and then changing getWorldDayTime to check that:

```java
((DimensionTypeAccessor) world.getDimension()).getFixedTime().orElse(timeOfDay % 24000L);
```

issues.title: Iris should make use of JCPP for preprocessing GLSL source files & ID mappings
issues.body:
JCPP is a Java library that implements a C preprocessor: https://github.com/shevek/jcpp

This is needed for properly parsing comment & const directives (like DRAWBUFFERS) and parsing block ID mappings. For block ID mappings we currently have a basic preprocessor implementation that works for most files in the wild, but obviously it would be preferable to use a proper preprocessor.

We could also fully preprocess source files before sending them to the driver. This would allow for more robust injection of non-preprocessor code fragments into shaders without accidentally injecting them before #extension directives, like what currently happens with [Spectrum](https://github.com/zombye/spectrum/blob/0ac7ea715850a65c8339ae9455e6e30b452e81cf/shaders/include/shared/header.glsl#L11) (#533).

Even better, we could hoist #extension directives to the top of the file, so that shader packs are more likely to compile on Mac & Mesa drivers. Most drivers don't enforce the positioning of #extension drivers, but these drivers do. IMO, it's likely best to just accept the fact that shader authors put #extension directives in the middle of files, and fix those shaders up ourselves. This would avoid requiring Linux users to make weird changes to their global system configuration like with #391.

issues.title: Support symbolic links for the "shaderpacks" directory on Windows
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I use symbolic links on Windows to share the `shaderpacks` directory among different minecraft versions to save disk space. OptiFine correctly handles this scenario, but Iris is currently just ignoring the whole directory.

FYI, I create symbolic links with the following PowerShell command:
```powershell
New-Item -Type SymbolicLink -Target "/path/to/real/shaderpacks" -Path "shaderpacks"
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If directory `shaderpacks` is a symbolic link, follow the link to detect shader packs.

issues.title: Light sources don't work with Prismarine Shaders
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Prismarine shaders, only skylight works, and all light from blocks doesn't work.
It's an edit of BSL, but BSL's block lights work fine.
This issue was probably caused by the recent colored shadows commit, I'm pretty sure it didn't happen before that.

### Screenshots

![Uploading NoShadowsPrismarine.png…]()


### Relevant log output

_No response_

### Iris and Minecraft Version

Iris 1.1.0+null (most recent commit, with colored shadows)

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

No

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080

### Java Version

Java 16.0.1 64bit

issues.title: A way to configure shader options
issues.body:
So far the mod looks and functions great! However, since my device isn't the most powerful, I do still need a way to change shader pack presets.

Currently the shaders menu only has these 5 options:

1. Open Shader Pack Folder...
2. Refresh Shader Packs
3. Cancel
4. Apply
5. Done

I think there needs to be a "Shader Options" button that allows for configuration of shader presets and individual settings. Optifine's shaders selector has a button that takes the user to a menu where they can toggle options on or off. I think something similar needs to be implemented.

I hope this mod combo gains as much traction as Optifine has!

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
### What happened?

A bug happened!

### Iris and Minecraft Version

1.1.0 / 1.17

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

No

### Operating System

Windows 10

### What is your GPU?

Um... AMD?

### Java Version

Java 16

### Additional context

Currently if any mods attempt to render an entity outside of an active game (i.e. from the main menu, or sub-menu thereof) without loading a client world first, the game will imemdiately crash with a NullPointerException with the message `the return value of "net.coderbot.iris.pipeline.PipelineManager.getPipeline()" is null`.

I've been able to trace this problem to this line in particular:
https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/35f888d9048e41e8bf04e9e793b178bae3e88399/src/main/java/net/coderbot/iris/mixin/MixinWorldRenderer.java#L52

Specifically that this is only being called *when a world is loaded*, and there doesn't appear to be any safeguards in place to protect against render calls happening prior to this event.

Now I am able to create a workaround for this, however it's messy and prone to causing more issues in the future, not to mention there could be [other mods](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/mobs-main-menu) out there doing something very simliar to what we do in HDSkins that would be facing this exact same problem, so I believe it would be best if Iris were to change their code to lazy-init the pipeline `PipelineManager#getPipeline` rather than relying on a mixin event to ensure your system is in the correct state.

Related issue: https://github.com/MineLittlePony/HDSkins/issues/45
Related commit in HDSkins: https://github.com/MineLittlePony/HDSkins/commit/ee78ad6e38695163c827777b642f63d1cbb7ff39

### What happened?

How to reproduce:
1) use the latest revision of Iris (f06a69d) and Sodium ([`26537f6`](https://github.com/IrisShaders/sodium-fabric/commit/26537f6e3414a611ef14897de5a10553f2c12e66))

4) place down some stone brick related blocks or magenta/red tinted ones (like magenta concrete powder, terracotta, wool or red concrete powder) and probably some other blocks as well

### Iris and Minecraft Version

MC: 1.16.6, iris version: all

### Are you running Sodium along with Iris?

Yes

### Operating System

Arch Linux

### What is your GPU?

RTX 2080ti

### Java Version

Java 8, Java 11, Java 16

### Additional context

I am convinced the stuttering is related to the crashing, however I as of yet cannot get stock sodium to crash in the same manner as sodium+iris. Even with shaders disabled, sodium+iris will eventually crash if the stuttering goes on long enough. 

I believe that, while this only happens presently in extreme situations, the problem exists at all time and is merely brought to surface faster by extreme situations; similar to some sort of memory leak or program that isn't cleaning up properly after itself.

This issue should be linked to in sodium's GitHub issues as well, as it seems to be related to iris and sodium.

I've as of yet had no luck getting the game to crash on single player, but multiplayer seems to be quite constant in some situations, especially a sugar cane farm I've built on a Skyblock server. Thanks to a spigot plugin, I'm able to plant sugarcane without water nearby, which allows me to create a massively dense sugarcane farm which no doubt pulls a lot of shenanigans to prevent the sugar cane from exploding on block updates.

issues.title: Iris renders Minecraft's default shadows in addition to the shaderpacks shadows

labels.name: high priority
labels.description: This issue is encountered frequently and needs to be fixed quickly

issues.body:
![2021-06-19_14 37 59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61254500/122643783-119c3b00-d112-11eb-919e-0f185f8b9141.png)
As you can see in this picture, on the right there's the shadow rendered by the shader pack (Sildurs Enhanced Default in this case), while on the left there's the shadow of the same structure, which looks like the default Minecraft lighting system.

I am using Arch Linux and an AMD RX580 GPU and the open source Mesa 21.1.2 drivers (RadeonSI), OpenJDK 16, MultiMC 0.6.12, Fabric 0.11.6.
I might try this later on another computer which also runs Linux but has an NVIDIA GPU (GTX 1060) with proprietary drivers.

I noticed the same issue on:
- different shaderpacks: Sildurs Enhanced Default, Sildurs Vibrant shaders, SEUS Renewed
- Different versions of Iris: The 1.0.0 release on Github with and without Sodium, the latest build of Iris and Sodium for MC 1.16.5, the latest build of Iris for MC 1.17.
- With or without these additional mods: Indium, Lithium, Phosphor (and Sodium of course)
- With the Mesa 21.1.2 drivers and Mesa-git as well as the latest proprietary AMDGPUPRO OpenGL drivers
- With and without the environment variable `force_glsl_extensions_warn=true` that is required for some shaders with Mesa

However, the same shaderpacks work just fine in Optifine.

Here's the log:
[latest.log](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/files/6680769/latest.log)
(Edit: I just looked at the log again, you can probably ignore most OpenGL errors up to line 2023 because apparently I started the game with SEUS PTGI, which isn't known to work correctly anyways and had totally different issues, and only at line 2023 did I switch to SEUS Renewed which is supposed to work fine but doesn't for me)

issues.title: Shaders reload when exiting the shader GUI
issues.body: This isn't a problem until we start to load heavy shaderpacks. The shaders always load twice - once when you press Apply and once when you leave the GUI. Naturally, reloading a large shaderpack (like Sildurs Extreme with Volumetric Lighting or Complementary) twice in a short timeframe results in a large performance drop (fps spike). It also has the unfortunate side-effect of that we can see the chunks being rendered with the shader when we press Apply, but then when we exit the GUI we lose all of that progress and all the chunks have to be rendered again which looks discontinuous.

issues.title: IdMap and FRAPI Support

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
Sometimes a mod wants some of it's quads to render like a different block, Bits and Chisels is my use case but there is likely others. I would like this data to be able to be baked into a FRAPI `Mesh` for both ease of use and performance. In Canvas/FREX there is a `MaterialMap` that allows you to get `RenderMaterial`s that renders like a certain block that allows me to do this with Canvas. It would be nice to have something similar possible with iris. However, I don't see any non-invasive way to attach the short from iris's `IdMap` that controls what block the quad renders like currently as indigo/indium uses a fixed pool of `RenderMaterial`s (https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric/blob/b7ab612143d0de808476ea6039740c123c109231/fabric-renderer-indigo/src/main/java/net/fabricmc/fabric/impl/client/indigo/renderer/RenderMaterialImpl.java#L43).

Potential Options
- Replace indigo/indium's RenderMaterial code with iris's own
- Have indigo/indium add compat code
- Provide iris's own frapi impl? (Prob not a good option)

issues.title: Mipmap produces weird artifacts on grass blocks.
issues.body:
Below are some screenshots showing how black bars render on the side of grass blocks, between the dirt part and the grass part. However, this only seems to be noticeable at very low resolutions, and only with Mipmapping enabled. The effect gets worse as the mipmap level is increased in video settings.

These screenshots were taken with Resolution Control Plus, but the effect seems to happen without the mod as well, by using small window sizes to simulate the low resolution. The resolution in these screenshots is 1/10 of 1080p, but the effect does happen with some higher resolutions as well.

This may be related to #297 #236 and/or #288 

### Specs:
- Intel Core i3 10th gen
- NVIDIA GTX 1650
- Linux Mint 20.1
- Java 16 (AdoptOpenJDK)
- Minecraft 1.16.5
- Fabric Loader 11.3
- Iris 0.4.0 (release)
- sodium-fabric (iris fork)
- ResolutionControl+
- Sildurs Vibrant Shaders Extreme 1.283 (?)
- BareBones Resource Pack (happens with vanilla textures but BB is more playable at low res because it's less noisy)

### Screenshots:
With Mipmap Level set to 4:
![2021-05-25_17 13 39](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76263371/120116910-848c4480-c158-11eb-9032-0c37b797eebb.png)
Black lines on grass blocks are visible in the center and right side of the image.

With Mipmap Level set to 0:
![2021-05-25_17 13 19](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/76263371/120116939-b9989700-c158-11eb-9b57-050676a81def.png)
Black lines no longer visible.

As you can see, it also seems to darken the color of the grass in the far background, which is probably a related problem.

Note that the camera angle may look weird  because I took the screenshot using OkZoomer. This was to get the grass blocks more parallel; otherwise the same row of grass blocks may have the lines at one end and not at the other, because of FOV warping. However, the lines do still occur without zoom, much closer to the player.

Any vertical dark lines in the image are a result of normal directional lighting being viewed at low res and a shallow angle, this may look weird but it is normal behavior.

I have not checked on OptiFine yet because it is incompatible with RC+
Also need to check without mods, this may just be a side-effect of vanilla mipmapping.

issues.title: GUI doesn't show shaderpacks if the shaderpack directory is a symlink
issues.body:
The GUI configuration doesn't work if the `shaderpacks` directory is a symlink (tested with EXT4 symlinks, but it shouldn't matter). It doesn't show any shaderpacks other than the builtin ones (`(internal)`).

This can be problematic for people that use symlinks to deduplicate files inside their Minecraft instances (such as me).

issues.title: Shader pack selection UI includes the .minecraft/shaderpacks folder as an option if there is a non-zip shader pack installed
issues.body:
If you have a non-zip shaderpack installed, the shaderpack selection UI shows `shaderpacks` as an available option since `.minecraft/shaderpacks` contains a `shaders` folder in its file tree and was never checked for.

To reproduce:
- Add a folder to `.minecraft/shaderpacks` which contains a `shaders` folder, or add a `shaders` folder to `.minecraft/shaderpacks`
- Open shader pack selection UI

issues.title: Missing ground light updates with Sildur 1283 (all presets)
issues.body:
# TL;DR

Skylight is not considered when rendering blocks that are 'under' another block. Note that this is different than having 'shadows', in the sense that even without shadows, lightlevels for blocks should be used to make blocks darker in low light conditions.

Possibly already reported in issue #153, but very unclear description then.


# How to replicate 

1. build a large floating platform
2. look under the platform
3. you will notice that mobs are 'dark', i.e., they are rendered with the appropriate light level
4. you will notice that blocks are 'light', i.e., they are **rendered as-if the plaform above had no effect on light level**
5. move under the platform
6. at first nothing will happen
7. after a couple of seconds, the scene will darken and everything will turn very dark (I think this is a feature of Sildur relating to dynamic aperture)

# Pictures a worth a million words?

issues.title: Weird issues with view bobbing when running with the Fabric version of Create

labels.name: mod compatibility
labels.description: A compatibility issue with another mod

issues.body:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22420959/112536935-501c9680-8d6b-11eb-9c97-a75af9ecbfed.png)

Relevant code: https://github.com/Create-Fabric/Create-Refabricated/blob/mc1.16/fabric/dev/src/main/java/com/simibubi/create/foundation/mixin/WorldRendererMixin.java

1. completely ignores the modelview matrix passed in, which will cause issues with iris moving the view bobbing over to the projection matrix
2. it renders fragments of block entities between fragments of terrain, which isn't what shaderpacks expect - block entities should be rendered after terrain or else some shaderpacks will have problems
    * alternatively, Create contraptions can be classified as terrain
3. it clears the active program, and Create tries to use its own shaders for rendering, which will conflict with the shaders that Iris loads

issues.title: RFC: Shaderpack awareness and control over whether the vanilla glowing effect is used

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
With the changes in https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/commit/92a71b5a06c1db377c2be04aa231e126523fccaa, Iris now bypasses shaderpacks for rendering glowing effects. Overall this is a win since it's hard for shaderpacks to implement glowing effects in a nice way. However, some shaderpacks might want to use their own glowing effect. In addition, others may want to detect when the vanilla glowing effect is being used, so that they may disable their own glowing code for performance reasons.

For allowing shaderpacks to decide whether they want to override glowing rendering and be responsible for properly rendering it themselves, I propose adding the following option to `shaders.properties`:

```
# false by default
overrideVanillaGlowingEffect=false|true
```

In addition, I propose making the following define available to allow shaderpacks to detect when the vanilla glowing effect is currently active, and thus when the shaderpack is not responsible for handling the rendering of the glowing effect:

```
#define VANILLA_GLOWING_EFFECT
```

An absence of this define will be understood to mean that the shaderpack is responsible for properly rendering the glowing effect.

Note: The names here are not final and are subject to change, if you have better suggestions feel free to let them be known.

issues.title: Investigate using a "program stack" for tracking the currently active program
issues.body:
The render-layer-experiments branch shows how using render layers can make things more convenient, but it brings some issues of its own. If mods create their own render layers in unexpected ways, it will completely break down, for example. As such, I'd like to investigate a hybrid approach that could result in more robust program usage.

Essentially, Iris would utilize a stack of programs, and would push and pop programs onto and off of the stack as appropriate.

For example, with entity rendering, Iris would push the ENTITIES program at the start of entity rendering, then with special cases (glowing, etc) it would push the associated program (ENTITIES_GLOWING, for example). This would mean that Iris would only need to use the wrapped render layers approach where necessary, and for everything else, it could use WorldRenderer injections, which are more likely to handle mods doing unexpected things.

issues.title: Use Canvas materialmaps to automatically infer additional mappings for block.properties

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
Shader packs have a `block.properties` file that has rough purpose of defining materials. For example, a shader pack may link `minecraft:oak_leaves` and the other leaf blocks to a given ID, such as `block.18`. Then, the given block ID (or, more properly, a material ID), is used to selectively apply certain affects. For example, leaf and foliage blocks generally wave, water generally takes on completely different rendering, and lava has some general wavy effects.

Unfortunately, few shaderpacks include support for mods. This means that your Terrestria sakura leaves won't wave with most shaderpacks, for example. And, even when shaderpacks support mods, often they only support popular mods, and even then only partially.

Canvas has a similar system in the form of materialmaps. Materialmaps are designed in a much better way and fully support mods. Since many mods include built-in support for Canvas materialmaps, Iris could read these files in order to automatically apply affects such as leaf waving to modded blocks. It should be fairly easy to reverse-engineer materials from block ID groupings: for example if all vanilla leaf blocks map to `block.18`, it's safe to say that `block.18` is the render material for leaves.

Ironically, this could mean that installing something like [More Canvas Compat](https://github.com/TeamMidnightDust/MoreCanvasCompat) would also help with Iris compatibility.

issues.title: Dimension overrides are not supported
issues.body:
Shaders can put dimension-level overrides in world0 (overworld), world1 (end), world-1 (nether), and so on.

`ShaderPack` should be able to load all of the relevant dimension overrides contained in a shaderpack, provide convenience methods for loading the shaders for a given dimension with proper overrides, and `ShaderPipeline` should be able to use them properly.

Also, shaders need to be compiled for the proper dimension, and switched when the player changes dimensions. Or, in the case of Immersive Portals, loaded at the same time.

issues.title: Shadow mapping is not supported
issues.body:
Many shaderpacks require this to work properly. They'll run without it, but things won't look right.

* [x] Ability to orient the camera to point at the player from the current shadow light position
* [x] Configuring the projection matrix as required by the shaderpack
    * [x] Orthographic projections (SHADOWHPL), used by most shaderpacks    
    * [x] Perspective projections (SHADOWFOV), legacy
* [x] Rendering the world (or parts of it) twice per frame: once for shadows, once normally
    * [x] Ensure that this is implemented in a way that doesn't trip up other mods
    * [x] Open question: should the events in WorldRenderEvents be fired for both the shadowmap rendering and standard world rendering, or only standard world rendering?
        * Canvas does not fire special world events when rendering shadows. This seems like sane behavior to replicate.
    * [x] An initial implementation could focus only on rendering terrain and perhaps the player entity, since those are the most important things for shadows.
* [x] Render to special shadow render targets and then make the render target content available to other shaders
* [ ] Decent shadow culling
    * I discussed shadow culling with Grondag a while back. Essentially, the only chunks that should be considered for shadow rendering are chunks that are (a) directly visible to the player or (b) potentially occluding (ie, casting shadows on) chunks directly visible to the player from the perspective of the sun / moon
    * Based on the absolutely abysmal performance of shadow rendering with most shaderpacks on OptiFine (some shaderpacks spend 50% of the CPU time on shadow rendering, and probably a bit of GPU time too!), I'm going to guess that it just flat out does not cull anything during shadow rendering. This is likely to solve the "why is the mountain behind me not casting a shadow" problem, but it results in very poor performance.

labels.name: contributions requested
labels.description: Feel free to fix / implement this in a PR!

issues.body:
OptiFine supports block states (instead of just blocks) in block.properties, we should too. This causes a lot of logspam with Sildur's and similar packs otherwise.

It's not 100% clear how to make this work seamlessly, consider the following examples:

```
block.0 = minecraft:stone_slab[half=top]
block.1 = minecraft:stone_slab[half=bottom]
```

```
block.0 = minecraft:stone_slab
```

We'll need to support both cases, because sometimes shaderpacks choose to differentiate based on state and sometimes they do not depending on the given block.

issues.title: Parse `const`-style directives from shader source files properly

labels.name: contributions requested
labels.description: Feel free to fix / implement this in a PR!

issues.body:
OptiFine/ShadersMod both allow shaderpacks to supply directives and configuration by declaring constants in the shader files. Here is an example: https://github.com/sp614x/optifine/blob/master/OptiFineDoc/doc/shaders.txt#L388

```glsl
const float shadowDistance = 160.0f;
```

ShadersMod uses the following logic to locate that directive on each line:

1. Match any number of space/tab characters (including zero)
2. A `const` literal
3. Match any number of space/tab characters (including zero)
4. A `float` literal
    * Naturally this will differ for directives of different types - it could be `bool`, `int`, `vec4`, etc.
5. Match any number of space/tab characters (including zero)
6. A literal containing the name of the directive, in this case `shadowDistance`
    * Again, this will differ for each directive
7. Match any number of space/tab characters (including zero)
8. A literal `=` character
9. Match any number of space/tab characters (including zero)
10. Optionally match a negative sign (`-`), since these values can be negative
11. Any digit or `.` character. There must be at least one digit for the directive to be valid.
    * Technically ShadersMod will match `const float shadowDistance = .;` as well but obviously that isn't valid. It's okay for Iris to ignore that case.
12. Optionally match a float type suffix (`f`), for example the `f` in `160.0f`
    * Naturally this will differ for directives of different types. 
13. A literal `;` character
14. Any character (ShadersMod doesn't care about anything that comes after the semicolon)

Of course, the above logic is tailored to float values. Boolean, integer, vec4, and other types directives will need slightly different logic.

The above logic could be implemented as a regular expression, however it is also possible to implement it without regex. It's possible that an implementation that doesn't use regex could be more readable and understandable.

issues.title: Make a progress tracking issue

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
It would probably be helpful for developers trying to contribute to have a "checklist" issue with a list of things that are needed to be implemented and the ones that already are. That would allow them to know what to work on without having to look through the entire source to find those spots, or to see things needed in case they don't know what actually needs to be implemented.

Another option would be making an issue for each feature and then adding those to a Project, which could even be organized in categories like To do, In progress or Done. Projects can also take regular texts ("cards") that aren't linked to any issue, but having each as an issue (or PR) allows for a description, discussion, someone saying "working on it", or assigning them to users. Projects can also be automated, so things like closing those issues or merging the PRs can automatically move them to Done.

Maybe a mix of both (tracking issue with a list and then project with linked issues for started/considered "important" at the moment), in case you like Projects but don't want to have the issues tab filled (although that's what it is for, isn't it?).
Another way could also be cards for those that "don't need discussion (yet)", and asking to replace them with an issue/draft PR in case someone wants to work on them or discuss them.

Disclaimer: I don't know anything about shader code, and probably won't be able to contribute, but I may if I'm bored enough.

issues.title: blockEntityId and entityId uniforms are almost certainly broken
issues.body:
Minecraft renders block entities and regular entities substantially differently in 1.15+ compared to previous versions. As such, it's much harder to track exactly what entity is currently being rendered, since entities are often drawn to the screen whenever a *different* entity starts being rendered.

The reason for this is how `VertexConsumerProvider.Immediate` works: with the exception of a few special render layers, whenever entity render layers are switched the content of the previous layer is immediately drawn to the screen.

It's unclear whether uniforms even work here anymore. Maybe attributes will need to be used? That would require some pretty hacky code changes to shaders however.
